Hul3VALKi0.one_liner: Optimistic value-iteration lookahead planning with an annealed feasibility margin for multi-stage Bayesian optimisation under unknown stopping constraints.
Hul3VALKi0.problem: In multi-stage processes with unknown transitions and stopping constraints, a single violation aborts the run and blocks all downstream observations, so exploration must trade aborts against value.
Hul3VALKi0.method: Formulates the problem as a feasibility-indicated Markov decision process and proposes FI-O-VI, a value iteration method for optimistic lookahead planning that uses an annealed feasibility margin to control the exploration-failure trade-off.
Hul3VALKi0.key_idea: Plan optimistically over a feasibility-indicated MDP, annealing the feasibility margin to tune how much risk of aborting the run is tolerated.
Hul3VALKi0.evidence: Sublinear rates for cumulative abort count and value regret under standard RKHS regularity and feasibility assumptions, plus experiments on eight synthetic benchmarks and two application settings against baselines (per reviews).
Hul3VALKi0.claimed_gains: Derives sublinear rates for cumulative abort count and cumulative value regret and reports competitive performance on synthetic and real-world problems; no numeric gains are stated in the abstract.
Hul3VALKi0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the sublinear abort and regret bounds under RKHS and feasibility assumptions are a strength, with broad experiments where FI-O-VI and FI-PoF-VI generally beat baselines.
Hul3VALKi0.main_concern: The theory does not cover implementation choices (fixed lookahead, approximate value functions, a fixed future-stage threshold), and optimism causes many more failures than FI-PoF-VI on some tasks without better reward.

ReOTai8HD3.one_liner: Ranks KV-cache regions by predicted attention times demotion damage; low-bit base on GPU, restorable residual in host memory.
ReOTai8HD3.problem: Existing KV quantization fixes precision when states enter the cache or only lowers bit width, although earlier KV states can become important again and demotion damage varies across generation stages.
ReOTai8HD3.method: Partitions historical KV states into regions aligned with storage blocks and periodically estimates pi (significant next-interval attention) and d (significant damage from low-bit demotion); the product pi*d ranks regions for precision allocation under a fixed GPU KV-byte budget. Each region keeps a low-bit base on GPU and a separable residual in host memory that restores approximately high-bit precision when reactivated.
ReOTai8HD3.key_idea: Rank regions by the product of predicted next-interval attention and demotion damage, and store a separable residual so precision can be demoted and restored repeatedly.
ReOTai8HD3.evidence: Agent workflow tasks including tau^2-bench and BFCL (named in reviews), with ablations on repeated precision recovery; the abstract is cut off after 'On agent workflow tasks'.
ReOTai8HD3.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; a review cites success-rate gains of 5-10.5 percentage points on the tested agent tasks.
ReOTai8HD3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear (earlier KV regions can regain importance and their quantization sensitivity changes) and value separately modeling demand and risk with restorable precision, which gives high compression with little accuracy loss.
ReOTai8HD3.main_concern: The predictors are trained per workload and may not transfer to unseen request mixes, and comparisons with FP8 KV, ThinKV, and R-KV plus system-cost and uncertainty reporting are missing.

LHm0tOWX3c.one_liner: Generates Escher-style conformal-map images with pretrained diffusion by interleaving denoising steps between the map and its Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse.
LHm0tOWX3c.problem: Ordinary generative models fail to produce Print Gallery-style conformal power-map images; applying the transform inside sampling makes the model either fix the twist as damage or drift out of it.
LHm0tOWX3c.method: Applies a conformal transformation T inside the sampling loop using the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse of the non-invertible map, interweaving diffusion steps with both directions of the transform so the denoiser sees in-distribution images and the Penrose identity guarantees a transformed result.
LHm0tOWX3c.key_idea: Interleave diffusion steps in both transform directions: steps between the pseudo-inverse and the map advance the straight image, and the reverse steps stitch details of the transformed image.
LHm0tOWX3c.evidence: Qualitative generation across scene types with off-the-shelf pretrained diffusion models; the abstract is cut off, and reviewers note a checkerboard round-trip test in the appendix but no quantitative consistency evaluation.
LHm0tOWX3c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is creative and technically meaningful, with visually impressive results and an engaging presentation.
LHm0tOWX3c.main_concern: No quantitative evaluation of recursive content or geometric consistency, and no analysis of how often the method fails.

fxtLdanc2R.one_liner: Explains cross-lingual representation similarity in middle layers using synthetic hierarchical grammars where Bayes-optimal prediction is belief propagation.
fxtLdanc2R.problem: Representations of translated sentences are similar in the inner layers of multilingual language models, an observation tied to the platonic representation hypothesis, but this has not been explained theoretically.
fxtLdanc2R.method: They generate synthetic languages from probabilistic context-free grammars that share upper-level but not lower-level production rules, so the Bayes-optimal next-token predictor is belief propagation, whose messages encoded in successive layers give analytical predictions that agree with trained transformers. The framework separates similarity (shared neighborhood geometry) from alignment (shared coordinates), the latter arising when code-switched data is abundant.
fxtLdanc2R.key_idea: Assume data have hidden hierarchy with shared abstract levels and language-specific surface levels, so belief-propagation messages across layers give a middle-layer similarity peak.
fxtLdanc2R.evidence: Synthetic PCFG languages with transformers trained on them, plus confirmation of the layer-novelty prediction (subtracting the component linearly predictable from the preceding layer) in pretrained LLMs.
fxtLdanc2R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is an elegant, interpretable account that predicts many observed cross-lingual effects, progressing clearly from a theoretical network to small transformers to LLMs and distinguishing similarity from alignment.
fxtLdanc2R.main_concern: The middle-layer peak may be built into the assumptions and belief-propagation setup rather than explained, so it is unclear the theory explains how real transformers learn it, and the layerwise novelty method is described only in the appendix.

3IWnGo30Hq.one_liner: Schema is an LLM agent harness that learns unknown environments as executable programs, verified against history and used for planning.
3IWnGo30Hq.problem: LLM agents in unfamiliar environments usually record discoveries in prose, which gives no compact, explicit, testable account of how the environment works.
3IWnGo30Hq.method: A persistent program workspace plus interfaces to check programs against the interaction history, plan within them, and execute plans under step-by-step verification, while the LLM decides what to investigate and how to act.
3IWnGo30Hq.key_idea: Represent the evolving understanding of the environment as executable programs that are validated against interaction history before planning and verified at runtime.
3IWnGo30Hq.evidence: ARC-AGI-3 public split, DiG-bench games and MazeBench, with same-base-model comparisons against basic and coding harnesses, component ablations and analysis of mechanism discovery.
3IWnGo30Hq.claimed_gains: Schema raises RHAE on the public split of ARC-AGI-3 from 58.7% to 99.2% with the same base model, solves 100% of the public DiG-bench games, and reaches the median performance of the top-50 human players on MazeBench.
3IWnGo30Hq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important, using executable programs for prediction and planning is well motivated, and the same-base-model gains over basic and coding harnesses are substantial.
3IWnGo30Hq.main_concern: Evidence for reusable, generalizable world models is limited because metrics mostly measure task completion and code statistics, and method details such as prompts and transition-readiness criteria are missing.

ZTjpA2iuXH.one_liner: ADHERE denoises hypergraph features and incidences with learned differentiable masks, then uses cross-view contrast and pseudo-labels for clustering.
ZTjpA2iuXH.problem: Real-world hypergraphs contain feature and structure noise that degrades input reliability, distorts learned representations and destabilizes optimization in clustering.
ZTjpA2iuXH.method: A reparameterized differentiable mask selects reliable node features and hyperedge incidences to form two denoised views, cross-view contrastive learning and pseudo-label self-supervision in a low-dimensional label space shape the representations, and a parameter-pruning gradient update suppresses unstable optimization signals.
ZTjpA2iuXH.key_idea: Learnable reparameterized masks select reliable features and hyperedge incidences to create two denoised views, trained with cross-view contrast, pseudo-labels and parameter-pruned gradient updates.
ZTjpA2iuXH.evidence: Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets (eight per reviews) across clustering metrics and several hypergraph encoders, plus theorems on propagation stability and clustering error.
ZTjpA2iuXH.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports effectiveness and robustness across several clustering metrics without numbers.
ZTjpA2iuXH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the noise problem is practical, the input-representation-optimization design is coherent, and learnable masks are a reasonable improvement over random augmentation.
ZTjpA2iuXH.main_concern: Each component (learnable masks, cross-view contrast with k-means pseudo-labels, gradient pruning) is established, and the theory does not show learned masks reduce the noise terms it assumes, so robustness claims are not fully supported.

LEZCBNrgpM.one_liner: Flow-based actor-critic that also trains the policy velocity field's cross-update change to follow critic target motion estimated via JKO responses.
LEZCBNrgpM.problem: In online RL a generative policy's target is defined by a critic that changes every update, so the policy chases a moving target and existing methods use only where the target is now.
LEZCBNrgpM.method: T-MAC adds to the current-target loss a loss that makes the cross-update change of the policy velocity field follow the target motion. Target motion is estimated by comparing Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto responses of successive critics on the same source actions, and a response-magnitude gate weights each state by how far its target moves.
LEZCBNrgpM.key_idea: Estimate how the critic-defined target moved between updates via JKO responses on shared source actions, and train the velocity field's change to follow that motion.
LEZCBNrgpM.evidence: Six MuJoCo and four HumanoidBench tasks against model-free and generative-policy RL baselines, with a statistical test on the aggregate improvement; reviews cite diagnostics with shuffled, zero and direct-gradient teachers.
LEZCBNrgpM.claimed_gains: Highest mean return on all ten tasks (six MuJoCo and four HumanoidBench) with a statistically significant aggregate improvement.
LEZCBNrgpM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea simple, intuitive and falsifiable, with careful diagnostics and clear writing, and one calls the JKO-based target-motion teacher a new application of Wasserstein gradient-flow geometry.
LEZCBNrgpM.main_concern: The gain is not isolated to target motion, since the teacher reduces to roughly a critic-gradient difference that may act like an ordinary policy-gradient direction, and a closely related recent method (GORL) is missing from the comparisons.

e1yRYFdCNa.one_liner: A learning-race model predicts when monitored LLM agents' hidden conventions emerge, turn over, or give way to silence.
e1yRYFdCNa.problem: Monitored LLM agents can coordinate through hidden codes, but how such codes arise from individual LLM behavior and why they persist is not understood.
e1yRYFdCNa.method: They extend social-convention theory into a model of monitored communication in which the agents and the monitor all learn in-context from the interaction history, with penalty strength selecting between direct communication, convention turnover and silence. They test it in multi-agent LLM experiments in AI trading and tutoring, using causal interventions that edit the interaction log.
e1yRYFdCNa.key_idea: Hidden conventions persist or turn over according to a race between the receiver learning a code and an in-context-learning monitor catching up and penalizing it.
e1yRYFdCNa.evidence: Controlled multi-agent LLM experiments in AI trading and tutoring reproduce the predicted turnover and the effects of penalty strength and monitoring lag; causal interventions show turnover is driven by a learning monitor.
e1yRYFdCNa.claimed_gains: not stated; results are qualitative regime predictions confirmed in experiments.
e1yRYFdCNa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the theoretically grounded new setting for studying collusion and the well-designed causal interventions that edit the interaction log.
e1yRYFdCNa.main_concern: The setup is narrow (a single agent pair, binary signal, single-emoji messages, explicit transmission rewards), so findings need scoping and claims such as strong penalties favoring silence are not isolated by the experiments.

9djgJUGgkg.one_liner: An offline estimator learns an empowerment-maximizing policy and its discounted state-occupancy from unlabeled trajectories to guide exploration.
9djgJUGgkg.problem: Existing empowerment estimators need online policy rollouts, so unlabeled prior data cannot be used to decide where to explore during online learning.
9djgJUGgkg.method: The estimator jointly learns an empowerment-maximizing policy and its discounted state-occupancy through a Bellman recursion on the occupancy measure, trained on unlabeled trajectories from any unknown policy with no environment interaction. The pretrained estimator is then used as an exploration bonus in online goal-conditioned RL.
9djgJUGgkg.key_idea: Jointly learn an empowerment-maximizing policy and its discounted state-occupancy from offline trajectories, so empowerment is estimated without any rollouts.
9djgJUGgkg.evidence: Qualitative empowerment maps in environments such as Ant-Soccer and Cube, and online goal-conditioned RL experiments with the bonus, reported with five seeds in reviews.
9djgJUGgkg.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims intuitive empowerment measures and improved online exploration without numbers.
9djgJUGgkg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find using offline data to identify high-control states a useful, carefully formulated idea, with empowerment maps that match intuition and encouraging gains when combined with RND and SUPE.
9djgJUGgkg.main_concern: Whether the estimator recovers true empowerment is checked only qualitatively with no ground-truth comparison, and online gains are small or neutral on several task and dataset combinations.

Jn6kASdwgk.one_liner: Training-free decoding that gates soft thinking by entropy and top-1/top-2 margin, and caps mixing support by Renyi-0.5 effective number.
Jn6kASdwgk.problem: Applying soft token mixtures at every step ignores whether the next-token distribution has a clear leading token, and selective methods still use a fixed candidate budget or the full vocabulary.
Jn6kASdwgk.method: AGC-ST gates steps with entropy and the top-1/top-2 probability margin, selecting steps where mass is broadly distributed and the two likeliest tokens are similar. At gated steps the Renyi-0.5 effective number sets a support cap and a cumulative-mass prefix selects the final mixing support.
Jn6kASdwgk.key_idea: Decide per decoding step whether to mix and how many candidates to mix, from the local next-token distribution's entropy, margin and Renyi-0.5 effective number.
Jn6kASdwgk.evidence: Five reasoning models from the Qwen and Llama families spanning 7B-32B parameters across five benchmarks, with gate and support-cap ablations and paired bootstrap confidence intervals in the appendix.
Jn6kASdwgk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evaluation comprehensive across five models and five benchmarks, with consistent accuracy gains over baselines and supporting statistical analysis.
Jn6kASdwgk.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate soft-input mixing from removal of sampling randomness at gated steps, nor the joint gate at matched activation rates, and the gains are modest.

ByTiyPcxn0.one_liner: Benchmark for memory unlearning in LLM agents with paired control dialogues and five forgetting-related test suites.
ByTiyPcxn0.problem: Existing agent-memory benchmarks test writing, retrieval, and organization but not whether agents forget requested information while keeping unrelated memories intact.
ByTiyPcxn0.method: Bemula has 50 multi-session dialogue instances, 135 forget requests of six types, and 1,742 test questions, each dialogue paired with a control version without requests. Five suites measure storage, removal, preservation of unrelated memories, relearning of similar facts, and resistance to extraction attacks.
ByTiyPcxn0.key_idea: Pair each forget-request dialogue with a request-free control so only systems that actually stored the target can earn forgetting credit.
ByTiyPcxn0.evidence: Evaluates six mainstream memory systems under three backbone LLMs, plus the Full Context LLM on two of them.
ByTiyPcxn0.claimed_gains: No evaluated system passes more than 1.5% of forget requests end to end across all systems and backbones, and most pass none.
ByTiyPcxn0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the paired-control design, which prevents credit for never-stored facts, and the preservation, relearning, and extraction probes that go beyond simple recall checks.
ByTiyPcxn0.main_concern: Most evaluated memory systems cannot delete memories, so poor results are expected, and reviewers want baselines that translate forget requests into explicit deletion operations.

2hbehF9EBG.one_liner: Weight-only PTQ that jointly selects clipping ratio and zero point by scoring candidate grids under simulated error compensation.
2hbehF9EBG.problem: Static group-wise grid evaluation scores grids on weights before intra-group compensation, ignoring the compensation updates each candidate grid induces, and a fixed zero point during clipping search can miss lower-error grids.
2hbehF9EBG.method: CAJQuant jointly selects the clipping ratio and zero point using compensation-aware grid evaluation, which measures reconstruction loss under optimal compensation while accounting for the weight updates induced by each candidate grid.
2hbehF9EBG.key_idea: Score each candidate quantization grid by its reconstruction loss after the column-wise compensation updates it would trigger, over joint clipping and zero-point choices.
2hbehF9EBG.evidence: Llama models from 7B to 70B at 2, 3, and 4 bits, measured by WikiText-2 perplexity and average downstream accuracy.
2hbehF9EBG.claimed_gains: Substantial quality improvements at 2 bits, outperforming all evaluated baselines in WikiText-2 perplexity and average downstream accuracy across all four models.
2hbehF9EBG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coupling between grid search and sequential compensation is a clear, simple observation and the fix is a drop-in change compatible with GPTQ-style pipelines, with strong 2-bit gains.
2hbehF9EBG.main_concern: Gains are clear only at 2 bits (3-bit and 4-bit gains are marginal with no variance estimates), quantization is slower than GPTQ, and validation is limited to LLaMA-1 and LLaMA-2 models.

on0XUoz5mO.one_liner: Randomized polynomial-time bandit algorithm for adversarial monotone submodular maximization under matroids, using compressed balanced fractional exchanges.
on0XUoz5mO.problem: No sublinear-regret algorithm was known for adversarial bandit maximization of monotone submodular functions under general matroid constraints.
on0XUoz5mO.method: Views the problem as learning an exchange policy for the Poisson base walk, which links it to contextual bandits but would need exponentially many policies. Balanced fractional exchanges compress the policy mixture into a single fractional base while keeping the exchange information the Poisson analysis needs, giving a polynomial-time algorithm with one feasible value query per round.
on0XUoz5mO.key_idea: Compress the exponential mixture of exchange policies into a single fractional base via balanced fractional exchanges while keeping the Poisson-walk analysis valid.
on0XUoz5mO.evidence: Theoretical regret analysis; reviews note there are no experiments or implementation.
on0XUoz5mO.claimed_gains: Expected (1-1/e)-regret of order n^(1/3) k^(2/3) T^(2/3) up to logarithmic factors, for a rank-k matroid on n elements, with one feasible value query per round.
on0XUoz5mO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it resolves an important open problem by extending bandit submodular maximization to general matroids, with rigorous analysis that builds naturally on the Poisson base walk.
on0XUoz5mO.main_concern: Novelty over the existing Poisson base-walk framework and standard online-learning tools is unclear, and there are no experiments to show practical efficiency.

DfQ3hgmXJI.one_liner: Predicts which model pairs allow KV cache transfer from attention-sensitivity statistics and certifies per-request risk with conformal control.
DfQ3hgmXJI.problem: Cross-model KV cache transfer works unevenly across model pairs and fails silently, producing fluent answers that disagree with a full prefill.
DfQ3hgmXJI.method: A first-order analysis of how cache perturbations propagate through attention shows downstream deviation depends on where reconstruction error lies relative to the receiver's query geometry. From it the paper derives the Cache Transferability Index, an offline predictor of a pair's achievable retention from second-moment statistics without fitting a mapper, and CacheCert, an online per-request risk score with conformal risk control.
DfQ3hgmXJI.key_idea: Weight cache reconstruction error by the receiver's query geometry, rather than its magnitude, to score transferability offline and per-request risk online.
DfQ3hgmXJI.evidence: A first-order attention perturbation analysis and experiments over multiple model pairs, datasets, and settings, including six cross-family pairs per reviews.
DfQ3hgmXJI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is real and important for multi-model inference, praise the principled first-order attention analysis, and find the empirical coverage of model pairs, datasets, and settings strong.
DfQ3hgmXJI.main_concern: Reviewers raise gaps in method details and cost accounting: the calibration set's role and cost in CTI, token alignment across model families, and possible reuse of the same samples for threshold and parameter selection.

W9gciOf15Z.one_liner: Tensor-core Hadamard transform kernel that assigns butterfly axes to register layouts at compile time, avoiding intermediate transposes.
W9gciOf15Z.problem: Existing tensor-core FWHT kernels sustain only 42-77% of achievable memory bandwidth at large rotation dimensions because of intermediate-layout materialization.
W9gciOf15Z.method: HyperHadamard treats butterfly stages as rotations along binary axes of a hypercube and assigns those axes to tensor-core register layouts at compile time, so intermediate transposes become metadata rather than data movement. A gather remap, a fused sign load, and a true-FP32 instantiation extend it to a billion-dimensional gradient projection.
W9gciOf15Z.key_idea: Track hypercube axis placement in tensor-core register layouts at compile time so layout changes are metadata instead of data movement.
W9gciOf15Z.evidence: Kernel benchmarks against HadaCore at large rotation dimensions, a billion-dimensional randomized gradient projection for training-data selection, and non-power-of-two support; reviews cite H100 roofline analysis and vLLM end-to-end tests.
W9gciOf15Z.claimed_gains: Up to 1.59x faster than HadaCore at large rotation dimensions and within 1.7% of achievable memory bandwidth, plus a 1.75x speedup on a billion-dimensional randomized gradient projection while remaining bit-exact.
W9gciOf15Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compile-time layout-tracking design is a clean systems insight backed by roofline-based evaluation, profiler attribution, and correctness checks.
W9gciOf15Z.main_concern: Reviewers say the gains are confined to a narrow regime (large rotations with many rows), the 14.7x headline compares against a dense FP64 fallback, end-to-end vLLM gains are only 1.02-1.05x, and ML novelty is thin for ICLR.

Z7Tw747ReZ.one_liner: Reasoning-aware supervised RL for small language model agents, with a verifier that invokes expert LLMs only for unreliable decisions.
Z7Tw747ReZ.problem: In multi-turn interactive environments, existing supervised RL for small models ignores reasoning quality in reward construction and relies heavily on costly expert LLMs.
Z7Tw747ReZ.method: RISE adds a reasoning-induced information gain reward and an adaptive supervision correction mechanism for step-wise supervision. It jointly trains a Decision Maker and a lightweight Verifier so expert LLMs are invoked only for unreliable decisions.
Z7Tw747ReZ.key_idea: Reward reasoning by its information gain on expert actions, and route only verifier-flagged unreliable decisions to an expert LLM.
Z7Tw747ReZ.evidence: Two 1.5B-scale SLMs as Decision Maker and Verifier, paired with different expert LLMs, on ALFWorld and BabyAI.
Z7Tw747ReZ.claimed_gains: Matches or surpasses expert LLMs' task performance (abstract truncated; no numbers visible).
Z7Tw747ReZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivating experiments that isolate reasoning from action persuasive and the information-gain reward principled and validated.
Z7Tw747ReZ.main_concern: Reviewers say the claim of matching or surpassing the expert is overstated: results come from single runs without error bars, and OOD success is 68.66 versus 76.87 for the expert.

mMigl82L9y.one_liner: Benchmark of 204 lab tasks testing whether image-to-video models generate procedurally correct instructional videos.
mMigl82L9y.problem: It has not been systematically studied whether video generation models can reliably communicate real laboratory procedures.
mMigl82L9y.method: LabInstruct provides 204 tasks across 5 scientific disciplines with real reference executions, instructions from human-verified procedures, and structured annotations of objects, actions, contacts, and state transitions. Eight image-to-video models are scored by human and automated checklists.
mMigl82L9y.key_idea: Score generated lab videos against annotated action, contact, and state-transition checklists instead of visual quality, exposing procedurally wrong but plausible outputs.
mMigl82L9y.evidence: 8 frontier image-to-video models evaluated with human and automated checklist scoring on 204 tasks.
mMigl82L9y.claimed_gains: not stated; the finding is that visually plausible generations frequently remain procedurally incorrect.
mMigl82L9y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a meaningful gap between visual plausibility and procedural correctness, using real lab reference videos, careful annotation, and a reasonable checklist design.
mMigl82L9y.main_concern: Reviewers cite reliability limits of automated evaluation, such as a task-level human-VLM rank correlation of only 0.364, along with a weak link between the self-driving-lab motivation and the benchmark and imbalanced coverage.

708MZ9pBGw.one_liner: Shows spectral optimizers with random or inverted singular values (Kaon, Freon) match Muon, challenging geometric explanations.
708MZ9pBGw.problem: Muon's success is typically attributed to second-order-like geometry and linear minimization oracle theory, but it is unclear whether precise geometric structure drives performance.
708MZ9pBGw.method: Freon is a family of Schatten (quasi-)norm optimizers using a QDWH-based iterative approximation that interpolates between SGD and Muon. Kaon replaces gradient singular values with random noise, and the paper argues performance is controlled by alignment and descent potential.
708MZ9pBGw.key_idea: Replace the gradient's singular-value profile with Schatten-power or random values and show that local alignment and descent potential, not exact spectral geometry, determine performance.
708MZ9pBGw.evidence: GPT-2 experiments across Freon exponents and Kaon, plus theory giving classical convergence guarantees for Kaon and a criterion for when a spectral update is an LMO.
708MZ9pBGw.claimed_gains: Kaon matches Muon's performance despite lacking coherent geometric structure, and the best Freon exponents for GPT-2 lie in the quasi-norm regime (no numbers stated).
708MZ9pBGw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question timely and the Freon and Kaon counterexamples surprising and informative, showing Muon-level results do not need an exact spectral-norm LMO.
708MZ9pBGw.main_concern: Reviewers say the conclusions are overstated: any positive spectral map is steepest descent under some norm, Kaon is Muon with spectral noise in expectation, and the convergence theory does not cover the deterministic Kaon or momentum and minibatch practice.

pQuy0XSFjd.one_liner: Agentic jailbreak that decomposes expert attacks into benign-looking subtasks, self-evolves strategies, and resumes from prior states after failures.
pQuy0XSFjd.problem: Existing jailbreaks elicit harmful instructions but overlook agent refusal to execute them and intermediate failures that force a full restart of the attack workflow, so the agent threat is underestimated.
pQuy0XSFjd.method: TRACE uses about 20 procedural decomposition schemes to split harmful expert-level tasks into executable, benign-looking subtask sequences, scored by harmfulness and difficulty to pick one for the attack. During the attack it resumes from prior states instead of restarting and, per the reviews, draws on a self-evolving strategy library.
pQuy0XSFjd.key_idea: Select a procedural decomposition by harmfulness and difficulty, then adapt to refusals and resume from the last successful state rather than restarting.
pQuy0XSFjd.evidence: Experiments on agentic benchmarks including AdvCUA (140 tasks, 26 end-to-end kill-chain tasks) per the reviews; the abstract is truncated before results.
pQuy0XSFjd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper usefully studies execution-level agent safety rather than only harmful text, reports strong gains over baselines, and has components that fit together sensibly.
pQuy0XSFjd.main_concern: No ablations isolate TRACE's components (decomposition, scoring, self-evolving library, resumption), and evaluation coverage on AdvCUA and the relation to a closely related ICLR 2026 paper are unclear.

qcRdEWsNSj.one_liner: Reconnects cross-chunk gradients in Self Forcing via shortcut gradient replay, without retaining the full autoregressive computation graph.
qcRdEWsNSj.problem: Self Forcing detaches historical KV caches to save memory, which severs backward gradient paths so later predictions cannot guide how earlier context is generated.
qcRdEWsNSj.method: Connected Self Forcing reconnects gradient paths across autoregressive chunks, passing gradients through generated latents into the computations that produced them, and uses shortcut gradient replay to recover cross-chunk gradients without storing the rollout graph. It is integrated with distribution matching distillation.
qcRdEWsNSj.key_idea: Replay shortcut gradients from later chunks into the computation that generated earlier latents, so historical chunks are trained for both direct supervision and their use in later predictions.
qcRdEWsNSj.evidence: Autoregressive video generation experiments on long-horizon visual quality and temporal consistency; per reviews, controlled comparisons with Self Forcing, SGF and full BPTT on Wan2.1-1.3B.
qcRdEWsNSj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the replay mechanism directly addresses the missing future-to-history supervision, with controlled comparisons supporting it.
qcRdEWsNSj.main_concern: Novelty is seen as limited, an incremental extension of Self Gradient Forcing, with evaluation restricted to Wan2.1-1.3B and mainly SF and SGF baselines.

CM3XZUtW4l.one_liner: Adds stage-wise process rewards and caption and grounding perception rewards to RLVR to improve visual faithfulness in small multimodal LLMs.
CM3XZUtW4l.problem: RLVR objectives emphasize answer correctness or output-level consistency, leaving intermediate multimodal reasoning weakly supervised for visual faithfulness, and visual attention drops sharply when generation moves from captioning to reasoning.
CM3XZUtW4l.method: Builds MCoT-ViG, a four-stage rationale dataset with controlled visual variants and object-level grounding annotations, and trains with PaIPO, which combines stage-wise process rewards with a Caption Perception Reward (sensitivity to controlled visual variants) and a Reasoning Grounding Reward (object references verified against annotated regions).
CM3XZUtW4l.key_idea: Reward captions for sensitivity to controlled image edits and reasoning steps for grounding object references in annotated regions, alongside stage-wise process rewards.
CM3XZUtW4l.evidence: Five benchmarks and three Qwen3-VL model scales, with controlled comparisons under matched data and training settings and added-reward ablations (per reviews).
CM3XZUtW4l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that answer-level RL rewards do not ensure visually grounded reasoning and that process-level perception rewards are a meaningful, well-motivated remedy supported by controlled comparisons.
CM3XZUtW4l.main_concern: Novelty is limited because PaIPO combines existing techniques, and the attention-based motivation is only correlational and not directly targeted by the rewards.

86fbF6dWZt.one_liner: Proves uniform discrete diffusion estimates distributions at minimax-optimal rates governed by effective support size rather than ambient space.
86fbF6dWZt.problem: Existing generalization bounds for discrete diffusion scale with the ambient space size and are nearly vacuous for real data concentrated on a small fraction of that space.
86fbF6dWZt.method: Derives statistical guarantees for uniform discrete diffusion on [K]^d governed by the effective support size s_n(P0), with suitable network size and hyperparameters, bounding expected total variation and KL divergence and showing the TV rate is minimax optimal and the KL rate is optimal up to (truncated).
86fbF6dWZt.key_idea: Replace the ambient-space size with a sample-size-dependent effective support size in the error bounds for uniform discrete diffusion.
86fbF6dWZt.evidence: Theorems for n i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution on [K]^d; per reviews, experiments report log-likelihood and MAUVE.
86fbF6dWZt.claimed_gains: Expected TV loss scales as O(sqrt(s_n(P0)/n)) and expected KL as O((1/n) s_n(P0) log(eK^d/s_n(P0)) log n), with the TV rate minimax optimal.
86fbF6dWZt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is rigorous and clearly written, and that effective support size is a natural complexity measure giving sharper guarantees than ambient-space bounds.
86fbF6dWZt.main_concern: The guarantees may describe a training-set reproducer, since network size grows with the number of distinct training points and the proof analyzes the empirical diffusion rather than a realistically trained score network.

4pK29VXrvO.one_liner: Jointly learns unified shared anchors and a nonnegative orthogonal tensor factorization with tensor total-variation Schatten-p regularization for multi-view clustering.
4pK29VXrvO.problem: Anchor-based tensor methods rely on predefined anchors separated from tensor learning, independently learned anchors lack cross-view correspondence, and low-rank tensor regularization overlooks local smoothness among samples.
4pK29VXrvO.method: LS-UATNOF projects views into a common feature space, adaptively learns one anchor matrix shared across views, and optimizes it jointly with a tensor factorization. Tensor total variation Schatten-p regularization captures global low-rankness and sample-wise smoothness in one term, solved with an ADMM-based algorithm.
4pK29VXrvO.key_idea: Jointly optimize unified anchors with nonnegative orthogonal tensor factorization so tensor structure feeds back into anchor learning, regularized by tensor total variation Schatten-p.
4pK29VXrvO.evidence: Per reviews, experiments on eight datasets with ablation, efficiency and convergence analyses; the abstract is truncated before results.
4pK29VXrvO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint anchor-and-tensor optimization is coherently designed, and the experiments on eight datasets show competitive clustering with supportive ablations.
4pK29VXrvO.main_concern: The design rationale is under-justified (row-orthogonality constraint on anchors, Schatten-p versus nuclear norm, choice of latent dimension and anchor count) and a fixed-versus-learned anchor comparison is missing.

f7PFD39fL5.one_liner: Benchmark of 11,072 instructions on 1,212 UHR Earth-observation images, plus an active-perception method that builds spatial evidence states.
f7PFD39fL5.problem: VLMs on ultra-high-resolution Earth observation imagery face a scale mismatch between scene context and micro-scale targets, and higher input resolution does not reliably yield perception of task-relevant micro-evidence, which the paper calls a resolution illusion.
f7PFD39fL5.method: UHR-Micro evaluates micro-scale evidence in native-resolution imagery with objectively verifiable targets. MAP constructs a spatially grounded evidence state from localized observations and supplements it when the current evidence is insufficient.
f7PFD39fL5.key_idea: Build an evidence state from localized observations and actively gather more when it is insufficient, because evidence access rather than model scale is the bottleneck.
f7PFD39fL5.evidence: Experiments with representative high-resolution VLMs on UHR-Micro, a scaling analysis, and MAP applied to two backbone VLMs.
f7PFD39fL5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a real evaluation gap with tiny targets, diverse tasks and verifiable outputs, and that MAP improves both evaluated backbones.
f7PFD39fL5.main_concern: It is unclear whether models actually see native resolution (pixel and tile caps, no effective resolution reported), and MAP's methodological novelty over prior region-focused and zooming approaches is limited.

v5wk8ePtf3.one_liner: Multi-stage flow-based generator for noncanonical cyclic peptide conformations using quaternion flow and Feynman-Kac steering.
v5wk8ePtf3.problem: Existing methods such as the HighFold series and MuCO focus on canonical peptides and struggle with noncanonical amino acids that add backbone modifications, stereochemical transformations and open-ended side-chain modifications.
v5wk8ePtf3.method: MuCO2 represents open-set noncanonical amino acids by aligning Uni-Mol2 atomic representations with ESM-2 residue embeddings, and uses curriculum learning driven by conformational energy and symmetries to train a quaternion flow-based cyclic backbone generator. A structure-guided Feynman-Kac steering mechanism and conditioning on chirality parity and N-methylation support efficient sampling.
v5wk8ePtf3.key_idea: A quaternion flow cyclic-backbone generator trained with an energy- and symmetry-driven curriculum, steered by structure-guided Feynman-Kac sampling over Uni-Mol2 and ESM-2 aligned residue representations.
v5wk8ePtf3.evidence: Evaluations on canonical and noncanonical benchmarks.
v5wk8ePtf3.claimed_gains: High-throughput cyclic peptide sampling with near-perfect stereochemical preservation, outperforming prior methods in physical stability and structural metrics, with no numbers stated.
v5wk8ePtf3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending cyclic peptide conformation generation to noncanonical amino acids is a valuable, practically relevant problem, and the framework supports N-methylation, mixed chirality and noncanonical side chains.
v5wk8ePtf3.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish the claimed ensemble diversity and coverage (it measures cyclization, energy, stereochemistry and C-alpha RMSD to one reference), and novelty relative to MuCO is limited.

CS0Sx3gpKP.one_liner: Distills a strong student on-policy from a proxy teacher built from a weak positive-negative model logit difference.
CS0Sx3gpKP.problem: On-policy distillation assumes a teacher at least as capable as the student, which fails at the frontier when no larger teacher exists, while consolidating domain experts requires costly training at the student's scale.
CS0Sx3gpKP.method: W2S-OPD constructs a proxy teacher in logit space from a contrast pair of a positive and a negative model, both smaller than the student, whose logit difference isolates a capability direction that is added to the student's own base model. The student minimizes per-token reverse KL to this proxy teacher on its own rollouts.
CS0Sx3gpKP.key_idea: Add the logit difference between a positive and a negative weaker model to the student's base distribution, forming a proxy teacher near the student.
CS0Sx3gpKP.evidence: Three types of contrast pairs (including a post-RL expert against its pre-RL initialization and a larger against a smaller model) on math reasoning and code generation across Qwen3 model sizes.
CS0Sx3gpKP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical for improving a strong model from weaker, cheaper supervision, with consistent gains across contrast-pair types and settings.
CS0Sx3gpKP.main_concern: All experiments use the Qwen3 family, so generalization across model families with different pretraining and vocabularies is untested.

pbqIoeKbnN.one_liner: TimeDPE predicts a detector's per-instance VUS-PR from label-free surrogate features of its anomaly scores and the raw series.
pbqIoeKbnN.problem: Benchmark averages say little about how a given anomaly detector will perform on one unlabeled deployment instance, and performance varies substantially across instances even within one data source.
pbqIoeKbnN.method: TimeDPE builds a compact, label-free surrogate representation from the detector's anomaly-score sequence and the raw time series, then learns its relationship to detector performance from historical evaluation records (a Gaussian process with a rational-quadratic kernel, per reviews).
pbqIoeKbnN.key_idea: Map the anomaly-score sequence and raw series to a small label-free surrogate feature vector and regress detector performance on it using historical evaluation records.
pbqIoeKbnN.evidence: Evaluated across 17 data sources and 10 anomaly detectors with leave-one-instance-out evaluation, mainly on univariate TSB-AD-U, plus a sample-efficiency analysis of the surrogate representation.
pbqIoeKbnN.claimed_gains: Reduces the macro-averaged mean absolute error of instance-level VUS-PR estimation by 40.2% relative to predicting each target with the mean performance from historical benchmark evaluations.
pbqIoeKbnN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the deployment-time performance estimation task is clearly defined and practically valuable, distinct from unsupervised model selection, with a rigorous evaluation protocol and convincing analyses.
pbqIoeKbnN.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (handcrafted proxy features plus an established Gaussian process) and experiments are mostly univariate, within-source instances, leaving multivariate and distribution-shift settings untested.

07RxqkEWHg.one_liner: RD-Solver learns per-interval stochasticity coefficients, predictor-corrector weights, and score-evaluation times for few-step diffusion sampling.
07RxqkEWHg.problem: Fixed reverse dynamics (PF-ODE or reverse SDE) trade off distribution-mismatch correction against score-error amplification, and the better choice differs from step to step.
07RxqkEWHg.method: RD-Solver jointly learns an interval-wise stochasticity coefficient, multistep predictor-corrector weights, and calibrated score-evaluation times with the network frozen. The parameters are trained with an endpoint loss that upper-bounds the squared 2-Wasserstein distance to a high-accuracy teacher in supervision space.
07RxqkEWHg.key_idea: Make the reverse process's stochasticity step-dependent and learnable, and optimize it together with the solver's discretization weights against a teacher endpoint loss.
07RxqkEWHg.evidence: Experiments on diffusion and flow models across multiple datasets with pixel-space and latent-space ablations at 3-5 NFEs, plus a continuous-time KL dissipation analysis.
07RxqkEWHg.claimed_gains: Achieves FID scores of 2.71 on CIFAR-10 and 4.62 on ImageNet-64 with five function evaluations (5 NFEs).
07RxqkEWHg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well motivated by the distribution-mismatch versus score-error analysis, evaluated broadly across datasets, and cheap to train compared with baselines.
07RxqkEWHg.main_concern: The continuous-time KL theory does not guarantee gains at 3-5 NFEs, and ablations do not separate learned per-interval stochasticity from simply adding stochasticity or from the calibration effect.

VqlLg2Hug1.one_liner: PathLapPE builds real-valued spectral positional encodings for directed graphs from the path Laplacian, giving node and edge features.
VqlLg2Hug1.problem: Directed-graph learning often symmetrizes edges or uses positional encodings that only partly capture direction, and Magnetic Laplacian encodings need per-dataset tuning of directionality hyperparameters.
VqlLg2Hug1.method: PathLapPE derives spectral encodings from the path Laplacian of the directed path complex, using an explicit orthonormal basis of the 2-path space to compute the edge Laplacian efficiently. The node- and edge-level encodings plug into standard graph learning architectures.
VqlLg2Hug1.key_idea: Use eigenvectors of the path Laplacian, including an edge Laplacian with down and up terms from 2-paths, as direction-aware node and edge positional encodings.
VqlLg2Hug1.evidence: Node- and graph-level benchmarks (WebKB graphs, Roman-Empire, OCB/HLS per reviews) across several architectures, compared with Magnetic Laplacian encodings, plus a computational-cost analysis.
VqlLg2Hug1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the path-Laplacian motivation is convincing, the encoding avoids tuning a phase or charge parameter, and the experiments are broad with performance similar to or better than Multi-q-LapPE.
VqlLg2Hug1.main_concern: The gain is not isolated to 2-path structure (no down-Laplacian-only ablation), improvements over strong encodings are modest in several settings, and node-classification benchmarks and graph sizes are small.

Sjya9An93H.one_liner: SpurFlow distills few-step image editors using learned token-wise reference coefficients that separate preserved content from edit residuals.
Sjya9An93H.problem: Full-field distillation objectives let preserved tokens dominate spatially and in gradient contribution, diluting the sparse edit signals that image editing needs.
Sjya9An93H.method: SpurFlow learns token-wise reference coefficients that control reference preservation per location and steer residual learning toward regions needing edits. The same coefficients guide an edit-aware adversarial objective that concentrates perceptual supervision on edited regions.
Sjya9An93H.key_idea: Split the student's prediction into reference-preserving content and a residual weighted by learned per-token coefficients, which also localize the adversarial loss to edited regions.
Sjya9An93H.evidence: Experiments on three foundation models (including FLUX.1-Kontext and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 as teachers) across multiple benchmarks, with ablations and an edit-localization IoU comparison.
Sjya9An93H.claimed_gains: With only two sampling steps, it closely approaches the FLUX.1-Kontext teacher and surpasses the Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 teacher on both benchmark overall scores.
Sjya9An93H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and grounded in a measured gradient imbalance between preserved and edited regions, and that gains hold across three foundation models and multiple benchmarks.
Sjya9An93H.main_concern: Learnable reference coefficients alone give limited gains while localized adversarial training drives most of the improvement, so each component's contribution and the effect of imperfect localization (IoU 0.496) are not fully isolated.

K8PWb781VM.one_liner: Lumi Map, a material-decoupled illumination representation, maps hand-drawn scribbles to relighting targets for stroke-controlled image relighting
K8PWb781VM.problem: Existing scribble-guided relighting methods lack a consistent mapping between scribble inputs and relighting results, limiting control over illumination intensity, chromaticity, and complex spatial distributions.
K8PWb781VM.method: Introduces the Lumi Map, an explicit material-decoupled illumination representation linking scribbles to illumination. A renderer synthesizes source image, Lumi Map, and relit image triplets to train a model conditioned on the Lumi Map, followed by reconstruction training on real relighting pairs to reduce the synthetic domain gap; Dior-Light is the resulting stroke-controlled method.
K8PWb781VM.key_idea: Represent illumination as a material-decoupled map that scribbles specify directly, trained on rendered triplets and then adapted by reconstruction on real relighting pairs.
K8PWb781VM.evidence: Experiments against existing approaches on in-the-wild images; reviewers note there is no standard benchmark for scribble-driven relighting.
K8PWb781VM.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says it outperforms existing approaches in relighting accuracy and controls illumination intensity and chromaticity, without figures)
K8PWb781VM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find each component well designed and motivated, with impressive visual results showing control of illumination chromaticity and intensity, and a useful new lighting representation.
K8PWb781VM.main_concern: The in-the-wild comparison may be unfair without a standard benchmark, and strokes sampled from the Lumi Map in training differ from real user strokes, leaving a train-inference gap.

L8QnFobzev.one_liner: Selects and weights shared LoRA adapters for GUI agents by matching user demand to measured adapter behavior on shared tasks.
L8QnFobzev.problem: GUI agents must adapt to user-specific task distributions, but reusing independently trained LoRA adapters for a target user with few examples is hard.
L8QnFobzev.method: GUIHub builds a shared capability space from adapter behavior on shared GUI tasks, uses semantic relevance between local support examples and those tasks to specify user demand, and selects and weights adapters accordingly without local action labels. New adapters join the same space without retraining existing ones.
L8QnFobzev.key_idea: Represent each adapter by its measured behavior on shared GUI tasks and weight adapters by the user's semantic relevance to those tasks in that capability space.
L8QnFobzev.evidence: Mobile GUI trajectories from FedMABench covering personalization, generalization, mixed-task composition, and Hub expansion, on three backbones including Qwen3.5-4B.
L8QnFobzev.claimed_gains: Improves offline Step Success Rate by up to 5.61 pp over the strongest baseline, gives a 2.08x speedup in recorded setup-plus-execution time, and gains 6.16-7.61 pp when the Hub grows from 8 to 32 adapters.
L8QnFobzev.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scoring adapters by measured behavior rather than semantic similarity is well supported, with routing diagnostics showing behavioral scores track adapter performance better than semantic scores.
L8QnFobzev.main_concern: The evaluation is offline only, with no real-environment tests such as AndroidWorld, and the advantage over a user's own adapter is not cleanly attributed.

gYxNUXYgDI.one_liner: Fair representation learning regularizer using Cartan-Hadamard sliced-Wasserstein distance to match group distributions on curved manifolds.
gYxNUXYgDI.problem: Fair representation learning measures group discrepancy in Euclidean coordinates, which misleads when representations live in curved spaces such as hyperbolic space where geodesic and ambient distances differ.
gYxNUXYgDI.method: They measure discrepancy intrinsically on Hadamard manifolds with the Cartan-Hadamard Sliced-Wasserstein (CHSW) distance, which aggregates one-dimensional Wasserstein distances along geodesic projections, and use it as a differentiable regularizer.
gYxNUXYgDI.key_idea: Average one-dimensional Wasserstein distances along geodesic projections on Hadamard manifolds to align group distributions in the model's own geometry.
gYxNUXYgDI.evidence: Theoretical bounds (cut off in the abstract; reviewers cite demographic-parity bounds) and Table 1 experiments against Euclidean baselines such as MMD, Sinkhorn, and sliced Wasserstein.
gYxNUXYgDI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that matching the fairness geometry to the representation geometry is well motivated and yields a computationally practical slice-wise regularizer backed by theory.
gYxNUXYgDI.main_concern: The contribution is incremental since CHSW already exists, and empirical gains are small (demographic-parity improvements within standard deviations) with only binary-classification evaluation.

dmvjB0WJK1.one_liner: Edge-aligned O(2) convolution that gives each O(3) irrep a reflection sign, making quantum operator prediction exactly O(3)-equivariant.
dmvjB0WJK1.problem: Edge-aligned SO(2) convolutions guarantee only SO(3) equivariance, so under reflections or inversion they cannot force operator components to vanish or protect electronic degeneracies.
dmvjB0WJK1.method: EACO is a message-passing layer with local O(2) equivariance, strict locality, and high efficiency; each O(3) irrep of degree l and parity p gets the sign tau = p(-1)^l describing its behavior under reflection in the edge-aligned frame. The authors prove local O(2) equivariance is necessary and sufficient for global O(3) equivariance within this construction.
dmvjB0WJK1.key_idea: Tag each irrep with reflection sign tau = p(-1)^l in the edge-aligned local frame, extending SO(2) convolution to O(2) so parity selection rules hold exactly.
dmvjB0WJK1.evidence: Hamiltonian prediction on five materials against a re-run SLEM baseline, plus a graphene mirror-selection-rule experiment and equivariance error measurements (per reviews).
dmvjB0WJK1.claimed_gains: With 17.2%-29.6% fewer parameters than SLEM, EACO matches or improves its Hamiltonian accuracy across five materials, with clear gains on Si.
dmvjB0WJK1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that building exact reflection and parity constraints into efficient edge-aligned convolutions is physically sensible and cleanly constructed.
dmvjB0WJK1.main_concern: The contribution is an incremental extension of SLEM with limited novelty over steerable-kernel theory, and the Table 2 gains are small and lack uncertainty estimates.

aQ1IvLU9yT.one_liner: Uses influence functions to select training examples, then rewrites their responses to behavior-aligned or opposed supervision instead of reweighting.
aQ1IvLU9yT.problem: Influence-selected examples show limited advantage over random selection under weight-based interventions, raising the question of whether they lack intervention value or reweighting fails to realize it.
aQ1IvLU9yT.method: Influence-guided response rewriting uses influence functions to identify targets and replaces their responses with behavior-aligned or behavior-opposed supervision while keeping instructions fixed, compared with reweighting on the same examples using epistemic abstention as the main testbed.
aQ1IvLU9yT.key_idea: Keep influence-based selection but change what the selected examples teach by rewriting their responses, rather than changing how heavily they are weighted.
aQ1IvLU9yT.evidence: Four open-weight LLMs on epistemic abstention, with comparisons to semantic and concept-based selectors (on OLMo2-1B per reviews) and safety refusal.
aQ1IvLU9yT.claimed_gains: Rewriting reveals strong, persistent, bidirectional behavioral leverage where reweighting of the same examples is weak and inconsistent; no numbers are visible in the abstract.
aQ1IvLU9yT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the empirical insight useful: influential examples steer abstention and refusal better when their responses are rewritten than when they are reweighted or removed, and code is released.
aQ1IvLU9yT.main_concern: The advantage of rewriting is not surprising given prior relabeling work, and the reweighting baseline may be understated because the released code normalizes the weight, with stronger-selector comparisons limited to OLMo2-1B.

63OoLgC19E.one_liner: Shows mid-training data schedules interact with learning-rate schedules, motivating joint design of data shift timing and LR decay.
63OoLgC19E.problem: Mid-training is treated as a practical technique rather than as a data-distribution schedule, and its coupling with the learning-rate schedule is underexplored.
63OoLgC19E.method: Views pretraining and mid-training as one data scheduling problem, compares replaying pretraining data in mid-training against directly shifting the distribution under warmup-stable-decay and constant LR schedules, then aligns the onset of the data shift with the LR schedule (abstract truncated).
63OoLgC19E.key_idea: The benefit of replaying pretraining data in mid-training depends on the LR schedule, so the onset of the data shift should be coordinated with LR decay.
63OoLgC19E.evidence: A 630M dense model and a 2.99B-total-parameter MoE model on DCLM and FineMath, with a theoretical characterization, evaluated mainly on target-domain validation loss.
63OoLgC19E.claimed_gains: Partially replaying pretraining data in mid-training substantially outperforms directly shifting the distribution under warmup-stable-decay, but the advantage diminishes under a constant LR; no numbers are visible in the abstract.
63OoLgC19E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is practically relevant and the comparisons across dense and MoE models, data budgets, and training horizons show that data and LR schedules are coupled.
63OoLgC19E.main_concern: The contribution over prior work on data order and LR schedules (Kotha and Liang; Luo et al.) is unclear, and model scale, datasets, and downstream evaluation are limited.

SNNbegFcjH.one_liner: Internalizes zoom-in visual privilege into a remote-sensing VQA model via on-policy self-distillation, filtering unreliable teacher signals.
SNNbegFcjH.problem: Ultra-high-resolution remote sensing VQA must resolve small evidence in very large images, and existing token pruning, visual search, or tool-augmented methods add inference-time cost.
SNNbegFcjH.method: RS-OPSD distills a privileged teacher view into the student using Context-Preserving Visual Privilege (CPVP), which avoids context loss from tight crops, and Correctness-Aligned Distillation (CAD), which filters conflicting teacher supervision. It is trained with GeoEvidence-6K (6,750 VQA samples, seven task categories, evidence-region annotations) built with Human Feedback-Guided Skill Refinement.
SNNbegFcjH.key_idea: Train the student with a context-preserving zoom-in teacher view as training-only privilege and keep only correctness-aligned teacher signals, so no search or tools are needed at inference.
SNNbegFcjH.evidence: Evaluation on XLRS-Bench, MME-RealWorld-RS, and LRS-VQA against open-source models of comparable size, with an ablation table comparing naive OPSD, LoRA fine-tuning, and the full framework.
SNNbegFcjH.claimed_gains: The abstract reports best performance among compared open-source models of comparable size on XLRS-Bench, MME-RealWorld-RS, and LRS-VQA, and says the 2B variant surpasses most 8B-scale models with the fastest measured inference speed, without giving scores.
SNNbegFcjH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree RS-OPSD outperforms compared methods on all three benchmarks without inference-time search or tools, the motivation is practical, and GeoEvidence-6K is a reusable resource.
SNNbegFcjH.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty over Vision-OPD is unclear, the student sees red-box annotated images in training but not at inference, and a full-parameter SFT baseline and training-cost comparison are missing.

AeeDOCePAA.one_liner: Training-free LLM reasoning that caches high-entropy anchors and revises them with graded actions chosen by delayed influence diagnosis.
AeeDOCePAA.problem: Latent-reasoning methods activate continuous representations at high-entropy tokens, conflating uncertainty with the need for intervention.
AeeDOCePAA.method: PASER caches predictive anchors at high-entropy tokens instead of activating latent reasoning immediately, then restores each anchor and evaluates the same realized suffix under discrete CoT and predictive soft histories to see whether latent intervention has an effect. Impact evidence accumulated over a longer horizon maps to hierarchical reflective actions (KEEP, GUIDE, ROLLBACK per reviewers).
AeeDOCePAA.key_idea: Cache anchors at high-entropy tokens, replay the same suffix under discrete and soft histories to measure downstream influence, and scale the revision action to that influence.
AeeDOCePAA.evidence: Mathematical, STEM, coding, and general reasoning benchmarks across model families and scales against training-free baselines such as SwiR, with threshold ablations on Qwen3-8B per reviewers.
AeeDOCePAA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between uncertainty and downstream influence is well motivated and supported by ablations, and the training-free method shows the highest average accuracy across models and tasks.
AeeDOCePAA.main_concern: Reviewers say hyperparameters appear tuned on the evaluation benchmarks with sensitivity shown only on Qwen3-8B, closely related feedback-driven latent methods (STIR, LatentSeek, Soft Reasoning) are insufficiently compared, and replay costs are unclear.

aClJTb5GQ4.one_liner: SPORT disentangles prototypes into orthogonal shared and view-specific parts and imputes missing views by global prototype and local neighbor matching.
aClJTb5GQ4.problem: Prototype-based incomplete multi-view clustering overlooks view-specific semantics in prototypes, fails to preserve cluster-level relational structure, and relies on global prototypes without local geometry, causing inaccurate imputation.
aClJTb5GQ4.method: Prototypes are decoupled into orthogonal shared and view-specific components; only shared components are aligned across views while view-specific ones are decorrelated. A structure-aware contrastive loss models cluster-level relations, and hybrid imputation combines global prototype matching with local neighborhood matching.
aClJTb5GQ4.key_idea: Align only the shared component of each prototype across views, decorrelate the view-specific component, and impute missing views by mixing prototype-based and neighborhood-based estimates.
aClJTb5GQ4.evidence: Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets, with ablation studies noted by reviewers.
aClJTb5GQ4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving view-specific information during prototype alignment is a meaningful design and that the hybrid imputation and extensive experiments show competitive clustering performance.
aClJTb5GQ4.main_concern: Incremental contribution: the motivation and the use of view-specific and neighborhood information are already explored in prior incomplete multi-view clustering, and orthogonality alone does not guarantee semantic separation.

YsGJY9LPgl.one_liner: Selects SFT reasoning traces for diverse step sequences using a CPU-only rule-based fingerprint, improving post-RL coverage.
YsGJY9LPgl.problem: Verified solutions are not equally useful for preparing reasoning models for RL, and how variation in reasoning-step sequences (route diversity) in SFT data affects post-RL performance needs study.
YsGJY9LPgl.method: A lightweight rule-based fingerprint of each trace's reasoning-step sequence is used to select diverse rather than similar routes from one candidate pool at one budget, with matched training recipes and checkpoints, before RL.
YsGJY9LPgl.key_idea: Fingerprint each trace by its rule-labeled sequence of reasoning steps and select SFT data that spreads across routes, giving group-relative RL more prompts with both successes and failures.
YsGJY9LPgl.evidence: Matched-protocol comparisons on synthetic puzzle environments and 10 mathematics benchmarks, single-model and multi-teacher pools, and 3 open-source corpora.
YsGJY9LPgl.claimed_gains: Route-diverse SFT raises OLMo3-7B's pass@8 by 16.9 points on environments held out from SFT, and diverse selection gains up to 6.2 points of mean pass@8 across 10 mathematics benchmarks in the single-model condition.
YsGJY9LPgl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical study is broad and well controlled with matched pools, budgets and recipes, and that the CPU-only selector is simple, cheap and easy to adopt.
YsGJY9LPgl.main_concern: The conceptual contribution over prior divergent-solution selection (Ju et al., 2025) is incremental with no direct comparison, and diversity may be confounded with prompt coverage.

hkX1f0ft1b.one_liner: MANTA linearizes pretrained softmax LLMs with query-routed multi-center Taylor attention, low-rank compressed states, and joint normalization with sliding-window attention.
hkX1f0ft1b.problem: Taylor-based linearization expands all keys around one global center, which is inaccurate when pretrained keys form broad, anisotropic distributions, while softmax attention has quadratic cost and a growing KV cache.
hkX1f0ft1b.method: Query-aware routing makes the softmax approximation local, with an additive recurrent state per routed group whose total size is independent of context length. The memory-dominant matrix in each state is projected onto a learned low-rank basis, and joint normalization combines the compressed history with sliding-window attention.
hkX1f0ft1b.key_idea: Expand the softmax Taylor approximation around multiple centers chosen by query-aware routing, keeping a fixed-size recurrent state per group that is low-rank compressed.
hkX1f0ft1b.evidence: Six language-modeling benchmarks plus LongBench against Liger on a Llama-3.1-8B softmax model, with ablations on number of centers, sliding-window attention and joint normalization.
hkX1f0ft1b.claimed_gains: Recovers softmax-model quality with an average score of 73.2 across six benchmarks and up to 27.3x the throughput of the softmax baseline.
hkX1f0ft1b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-center Taylor construction is a natural, well-explained extension with ablation support, offering substantial efficiency gains at low conversion cost.
hkX1f0ft1b.main_concern: Quality recovery is overstated and under-isolated: MMLU drops (58.3 and 62.4 versus 65.3 for softmax), the joint-normalization effect is confounded with sliding-window attention, long-context results lack the original model, and only one model size is tested.

RTWY6kLvW7.one_liner: HRoPE injects per-patch plane-induced homographies into attention as relative transformations, encoding local surface orientation for multi-view transformers.
RTWY6kLvW7.problem: Geometric relative positional encodings for multi-view transformers describe only where a token is observed from, leaving the surface geometry that the patch depicts unmodeled.
RTWY6kLvW7.method: Each patch is represented as a slanted 3D plane, following the slanted support-window assumption of multi-view stereo, and its plane-induced homography is injected into attention so the transformer can rectify perspective distortion and align patch features across views. The encoding requires no ground-truth geometry.
RTWY6kLvW7.key_idea: Encode each patch as a slanted plane and use the induced homography as the relative transform in attention, adding surface tilt to position-only encodings.
RTWY6kLvW7.evidence: Novel view synthesis on several datasets including RealEstate10K, with ablations on transformation parameterization and feature sources, transfer to EscherNet, and comparisons with PRoPE, URoPE and RayRoPE per reviews.
RTWY6kLvW7.claimed_gains: not stated in the available abstract (a review cites 27.410 PSNR on RealEstate10K with VGGT features versus 26.836 for URoPE).
RTWY6kLvW7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adding patch-level surface orientation to relative positional encoding is well motivated, with a clean closed-form design and broad experiments and ablations on novel view synthesis.
RTWY6kLvW7.main_concern: The geometric claims are under-validated: the predicted mode gives target tokens no camera pose, the orientation benefit is not isolated, gains depend on pretrained VGGT features, and originality over GTA and PRoPE is limited.

VSmfsEaxTC.one_liner: Learns a flow-matching conditional proposal approximating the optimal particle-filter proposal, with likelihood-tractable importance weights and a localized variant.
VSmfsEaxTC.problem: Classical filters assume linear-Gaussian-like structure, particle filters collapse in high dimensions, and generative data-assimilation methods inject observations by approximate guidance so errors accumulate over long horizons.
VSmfsEaxTC.method: Flow Proposal Particle Filters (FPPF) learn a conditional generative proposal approximating the variance-minimizing optimal proposal; conditioning on observations steers particles toward high-likelihood regions before weighting, and a tractable proposal density gives accurate importance weights. L-FPPF adds localization to scale to high-dimensional systems.
VSmfsEaxTC.key_idea: Use an observation-conditioned generative proposal with tractable density inside a particle filter, so weights stay exact, and localize it to avoid weight collapse in high dimensions.
VSmfsEaxTC.evidence: Chaotic dynamical systems and multimodal observations of severe convective storms; reviews cite Lorenz-96, SQG and SEVIR with LBPF and LETKF baselines.
VSmfsEaxTC.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports improved accuracy and calibration over several baselines but is cut off before any numbers).
VSmfsEaxTC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing a learned observation-informed proposal with particle filtering is well motivated, handles nonlinear and multimodal settings, and beats bootstrap and global particle filters in broad experiments.
VSmfsEaxTC.main_concern: The computational cost of iterative flow sampling and density evaluation is not characterized by wall-clock comparisons, and gains over strong localized baselines such as LBPF are sometimes modest.

GyJFmBegWL.one_liner: Removes chain-of-thought tokens in geometric chunks aligned with a task hierarchy, with a proof that a transformer learns k-parity.
GyJFmBegWL.problem: Explicit chain-of-thought raises inference cost, and it is unclear whether a transformer can still learn efficiently as intermediate reasoning steps are progressively removed during training.
GyJFmBegWL.method: Log-ICoT takes a given hierarchical decomposition of the task and a curriculum that removes intermediate steps in geometric chunks aligned with its levels. The analysis covers a simplified L-layer transformer learning k-parity with k = 2^L.
GyJFmBegWL.key_idea: Remove intermediate reasoning steps level by level in geometrically growing chunks matching the task's hierarchical decomposition, so each training stage internalizes one more layer.
GyJFmBegWL.evidence: Theory giving sufficient conditions for a simplified L-layer transformer to learn k-parity, plus experiments on parity showing layer-wise internalization and on structured reasoning tasks with pretrained GPT-2.
GyJFmBegWL.claimed_gains: Learns k-parity with a number of samples polynomial in input length n and L = log_2 k training stages; reaches high answer accuracy with fewer training updates than token-wise ICoT and lower inference latency than explicit CoT (no further numbers).
GyJFmBegWL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is well chosen and the multi-stage polynomial-sample guarantee for internalizing chain-of-thought is substantial, extending prior one-layer explicit-CoT parity results.
GyJFmBegWL.main_concern: Scope is narrow: the method needs a balanced-tree decomposition with intermediate supervision, and the theory is hand-designed around parity with fixed positional structure, so the guarantee may hold largely by construction.

Qm0jSix3us.one_liner: Training-free token pruning for omni-modal LLMs that allocates retention budgets top-down across pre-LLM and decaying layer-wise stages.
Qm0jSix3us.problem: Omni-modal LLMs process tens of thousands of visual and audio tokens throughout the LLM, and non-textual token redundancy varies across stages and layers.
Qm0jSix3us.method: Given an overall token retention rate, SEATS allocates budgets top-down in an input-dependent way: a larger rate for pre-LLM selection, all tokens kept in shallow layers, decreasing rates in middle layers, and non-textual tokens fully removed in late layers.
Qm0jSix3us.key_idea: Allocate one global token budget top-down across pre-LLM and inner-LLM stages with a depth-decaying retention schedule that fully drops audio-visual tokens in late layers.
Qm0jSix3us.evidence: Three omni-modal LLMs and six benchmarks, with a layer-wise token removal study; reviews cite comparisons against FastV, DivPrune-style and other pruning baselines.
Qm0jSix3us.claimed_gains: Retaining only 10% of visual and audio tokens preserves 94.9% of full-token performance on Qwen2.5-Omni with a 9.3x FLOPs reduction and a 4.9x prefill speedup.
Qm0jSix3us.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the observation-to-design logic is coherent, the layer-wise removal study supports delaying pruning, and SEATS saves substantial compute while keeping most performance across three models and six benchmarks.
Qm0jSix3us.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to FastV, PyramidDrop, DivPrune and especially OmniFit, which is discussed in related work but not compared experimentally.

YsJAJT5YS3.one_liner: Genome-grounded LLM predicts microbial life-boundary phenotypes by refining proposals with phenotype-specific genomic representations and Sufficiency-to-Decision GRPO.
YsJAJT5YS3.problem: Predicting microbial life-boundary phenotypes from genomes is hard under sparse genomic observations and diverse phenotype types, and existing approaches leave complementary signals and intermediate phenotype proposals underused.
YsJAJT5YS3.method: GGBound learns phenotype-specific genomic representations and grounds them in a language decoder through phenotype-oriented reasoning supervision, yielding interpretable rationales. Sufficiency-to-Decision GRPO strengthens use of genomic evidence beyond auxiliary proposals, and a strain-centric benchmark covers 17 phenotypes from IJSEM strains and BacDive annotations.
YsJAJT5YS3.key_idea: Frame prediction as proposal-conditioned refinement and reward the decoder for depending on genomic evidence rather than on the auxiliary proposals alone.
YsJAJT5YS3.evidence: A new benchmark of 17 microbial life-boundary phenotypes, compared with genome-based baselines and LLMs, with ablations and a conflicting-prediction analysis per reviewers.
YsJAJT5YS3.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says GGBound consistently outperforms genome-based baselines across phenotype categories (cut off) without numbers.
YsJAJT5YS3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the pipeline well justified by ablations, the genomic-utility contrast a strength, and the benchmark a substantial curation effort.
YsJAJT5YS3.main_concern: The components are largely standard (prefix tuning, reconstruction regularizer, projector interface) around one new ingredient, the genomic model is limited to Evo 2, and the theory is hard to follow.

SS2iAOHhyz.one_liner: Trains motion customization with stochastic optimal control to steer generation toward reference motion while staying inside the pretrained prompt-conditional distribution.
SS2iAOHhyz.problem: Motion customization suffers content leakage, where appearance from the reference video propagates into outputs, because direct regression on the reference makes the generative process collapse toward it.
SS2iAOHhyz.method: Control-based Motion Customization (CMC) formalizes steering generative dynamics toward the desired motion with Stochastic Optimal Control. It removes the need for an explicit reward and adds a timestep-adaptive motion cost that acts only on early generative stages.
SS2iAOHhyz.key_idea: Replace direct regression on the reference video with a stochastic optimal control objective that rewards reference motion while penalizing deviation from the pretrained generative dynamics.
SS2iAOHhyz.evidence: Experiments reported as extensive; per reviewers, full CMC is evaluated on CogVideoX-2B with appendix motion analysis on Wan2.2, and Table 1 compares motion fidelity and diversity against baselines such as MotionDirector and MotionClone.
SS2iAOHhyz.claimed_gains: Accelerates training by 2.5×, and the abstract claims it mitigates content leakage with competitive motion fidelity and preserved diversity, without further numbers.
SS2iAOHhyz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the stochastic optimal control view of content leakage principled, with convincing motion transfer and diverse, prompt-consistent appearances.
SS2iAOHhyz.main_concern: Validation is thin: full CMC is tested only on CogVideoX-2B, and its motion distance is worse than MotionDirector's (0.1093 versus 0.0781), so higher diversity may reflect looser motion constraints.

veP5OqaqeG.one_liner: Vision-language-action model pretrained at scale on robot-base-frame pointmaps jointly with 3D spatial VQA for metric geometry and manipulation.
veP5OqaqeG.problem: Vision-language-action models struggle with precise manipulation because image observations do not directly provide the metric 3D geometry of the physical environment.
veP5OqaqeG.method: PointmapVLA jointly pretrains on pointmap-augmented robot demonstrations and 3D spatial VQA, supervising 3D grounding, metric localization and spatial relation reasoning alongside action prediction. It uses a pointmap-paired corpus of 76.3M robot demonstration frames and 10.7M 3D spatial VQA examples.
veP5OqaqeG.key_idea: Express pointmaps from all cameras in the robot base frame and jointly pretrain on pointmap-augmented demonstrations and spatial VQA so the VLM backbone learns to read pointmaps.
veP5OqaqeG.evidence: Three simulation benchmarks (including LIBERO-Plus and RoboCasa per reviewers) and three real-world tasks under unseen target heights, lighting and camera viewpoints, with a spatial VQA ablation.
veP5OqaqeG.claimed_gains: 92.4% success rate on LIBERO-Plus, and 1.8× the success rate of the strongest geometry-aware baseline in real-world manipulation under unseen target heights, lighting and camera viewpoints.
