veP5OqaqeG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the substantial pointmap-paired data construction, the well-motivated robot-base frame, and competitive results in simulation and on real robots.
veP5OqaqeG.main_concern: Conceptual novelty is limited (it combines and scales known pointmap and 3D-supervision ideas) with no data-scaling analysis, and the RoboCasa comparisons are unmatched (300 MimicGen versus 50 human demonstrations).

TD7R9XqQ1u.one_liner: RL for human swimming from one reference motion using a VQ-VAE-tokenized body-water force state and a GPU rigid-fluid solver.
TD7R9XqQ1u.problem: Robust motion policies for dense fluid environments such as swimming are unsolved, because swimming needs full-body coordination under fluid forces and fully coupled rigid-fluid simulation is too slow for RL.
TD7R9XqQ1u.method: SWIM learns from a single reference motion with a dual-branch graph-convolutional VQ-VAE that tokenizes per-link body-water forces and torques into a compact environment representation. It is paired with a GPU-based Lagrangian solver with rigid-fluid coupling.
TD7R9XqQ1u.key_idea: Tokenize per-link body-water forces and torques into a low-dimensional discrete state that is informative for control and stable under rapid force changes, then train in a fast GPU fluid solver.
TD7R9XqQ1u.evidence: Hundreds of training runs and several hundred zero-shot conditions (unseen goals, fluid densities, external flows, perturbations, altered morphologies, four swimming styles) against MimicKit-DeepMimic, MimicKit-AMP, ADD and alternative force representations.
TD7R9XqQ1u.claimed_gains: 10–15× faster training from the GPU rigid-fluid solver, with generalization to unseen goals, trajectories, fluids, flows, perturbations, body morphologies and all four competitive swimming styles.
TD7R9XqQ1u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard it as a practical first RL system for humanoid swimming with extensive zero-shot generalization tests and a useful GPU fluid solver.
TD7R9XqQ1u.main_concern: The benefit of the tokenized environment representation is not isolated: simpler raw whole-body forces reach higher success (69.8% versus 63.9%), and the raw-versus-token comparison also changes temporal smoothing.

iFKCpogvxq.one_liner: Few-step diffusion distillation where a learned critic compares student and teacher velocity fields and returns their disagreement as feedback.
iFKCpogvxq.problem: Distribution-matching distillation depends on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution, but at intermediate steps student-score estimation is difficult and common estimators may describe a different distribution from the one used to update the student.
iFKCpogvxq.method: Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD) uses a learned critic to compare student and teacher velocity fields built from the student's sampling process. VA-TDM follows trajectory distribution matching, adding transition-aware online velocity learning and dual-form VAD supervision across intermediate student transitions.
iFKCpogvxq.key_idea: Supervise intermediate student transitions with velocity fields built from the student's own sampling process, using a critic to measure teacher-student disagreement, which unifies score, Fisher and moment matching.
iFKCpogvxq.evidence: Image and video generation on several base models (SD, FLUX and MiniMax H3 per reviewers), with sizes up to 33B at 4 NFE, plus a small user study.
iFKCpogvxq.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off at a qualitative claim that VA-TDM is powerful for learning few-step generators.
iFKCpogvxq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the extensive experiments across image and video backbones up to 33B parameters and the principled analysis of mismatches in prior distribution-matching distillation.
iFKCpogvxq.main_concern: The compatibility of the dual-form supervision is not established, the unification claim overstates the match between theory and implementation (detached critic, gains from extra components), and the video evaluation is thin.

12NxQTIgFU.one_liner: Conformal framework that builds the maximal budget-feasible decision set per input, then certifies failure risk on an independent set.
12NxQTIgFU.problem: Conformal robustness control returns uncertainty sets at a fixed coverage or robustness level, which may violate pointwise deployment requirements such as per-decision cost limits or set-size budgets.
12NxQTIgFU.method: BCRC works backward from the hard budget to construct the maximal feasible candidate set for an observed input, in continuous and discrete regimes. It gives a finite-sample upper bound on the failure probability of the exact deployed rule using an independent certification set.
12NxQTIgFU.key_idea: Learn the deployment rule induced by the hard budget first, then bound that exact rule's failure probability afterward on an independent certification set.
12NxQTIgFU.evidence: Three experimental setups against baselines adapted to the budget by truncation (per reviewers), plus a finite-sample failure bound.
12NxQTIgFU.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract says BCRC consistently satisfies the deployment budget and achieves lower failure risk than several baselines under the same budget.
12NxQTIgFU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find hard-budget adherence well motivated, the framework general across continuous and discrete settings, and BCRC better than baselines in all three experiments.
12NxQTIgFU.main_concern: The conformal component is unclear (the guarantee follows from concentration of independent failures of a fixed rule), the surrogate objective's link to failure risk is unexplained, and the baselines are crudely adapted so margins are small.

dlx0XIyQF1.one_liner: Training-free task routing for parameter-efficient class-incremental learning that calibrates task scores with subspace filtering, residual likelihood and prototype affinity.
dlx0XIyQF1.problem: Class-incremental inference must choose among task-specific parameter-efficient modules without task identity, creating a routing error beyond forgetting from feature-, task- and class-level misalignment.
dlx0XIyQF1.method: Feature Distribution Calibration (FDC) is a post-hoc plug-in with three parts: Task Subspace Filtering suppresses feature components outside each task's principal subspace, Residual Likelihood Calibration evaluates the typicality of the subspace residual, and Prototype Affinity Calibration measures compatibility with the task's class prototypes.
dlx0XIyQF1.key_idea: Score each task's fit to an input at inference by combining its principal-subspace projection, residual typicality and class-prototype affinity, without retraining or a separate router.
dlx0XIyQF1.evidence: Eight parameter-efficient class-incremental methods with a shared encoder, five datasets and three training seeds per reviewers, with before-and-after comparisons on the same checkpoints.
dlx0XIyQF1.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before the figure, and reviewers cite gains on all 40 method-dataset pairs with an average of 4.45 points when all components are enabled.
dlx0XIyQF1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the routing bottleneck well diagnosed and the plug-in comparisons on identical checkpoints easy to assess across several methods and datasets.
dlx0XIyQF1.main_concern: The component configurations behind the headline 40-of-40 result were selected using the reported evaluation results, and the components resemble established subspace-residual, likelihood and prototype scoring.

s7QNdzNiA8.one_liner: Boundary-first hierarchical latent diffusion: sketch to 3D boundary curves, then surfaces, then boundary-surface relations to assemble a B-Rep.
s7QNdzNiA8.problem: Existing sketch-to-B-Rep methods infer coupled geometry and topology from sparse sketches and often fail to produce B-Reps that are both geometrically precise and topologically valid.
s7QNdzNiA8.method: Sketch2BRep has three stages: Shape-Layout Coupled Sketch Diffusion infers a structured 3D boundary from partial sketch cues, Boundary-Conditioned Joint Surface Diffusion lets face and edge tokens interact to synthesize consistent surfaces, and Geometry-Aware RelationNet models pairwise boundary-surface relationships to assemble the B-Rep.
s7QNdzNiA8.key_idea: Use boundary curves as the intermediate that links sketch cues to B-Rep faces: generate 3D boundaries first, condition surface generation on them, then model boundary-surface relations explicitly.
s7QNdzNiA8.evidence: DeepCAD and ABC datasets with ablations, with the main sketch-conditioned comparison against HoLa on DeepCAD per reviewers, using synthetic sketches rendered from CAD models.
s7QNdzNiA8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the boundary-first design well motivated and clearly presented, with promising improvements and supporting ablations on DeepCAD and ABC.
s7QNdzNiA8.main_concern: Evaluation relies on synthetic sketches and a single sketch-conditioned baseline (HoLa on DeepCAD), and how edge and face counts are set at inference is unclear.

R8wMAyZPwj.one_liner: Benchmark extending embodied world model evaluation to visuotactile modality, world models as RL environments, and real-robot platforms.
R8wMAyZPwj.problem: Existing embodied world model benchmarks are largely confined to vision-only prediction, offline embodied applications and simulator-based evaluation.
R8wMAyZPwj.method: WorldArena 2.0 broadens evaluation along modality (vision to visuotactile), functionality (policy evaluation and planning to interactive RL environments for policy optimization) and platform (simulators to real robots with multiple embodiments) under a standardized protocol.
R8wMAyZPwj.key_idea: Evaluate world models as interactive RL environments and with visuotactile inputs on simulated and real robots, rather than only by visual prediction quality.
R8wMAyZPwj.evidence: Per reviewers, seven world models and three reward families under a shared GRPO pipeline, tactile experiments on the UniVTAC dataset, RoboTwin and LIBERO tasks, and real-robot trials.
R8wMAyZPwj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the extension beyond visual quality to tactile sensing, world models as RL environments and physical execution, with useful diagnostic observations.
R8wMAyZPwj.main_concern: The evidence is thin for the conclusions drawn (single-seed peak-checkpoint RL results, one or two tasks per evaluation, few real-robot trials), and WMPO and VLA-MBPO are not compared.

oASnPVaH6V.one_liner: Feed-forward video-to-4D generation with structured 4D Gaussians that share sparse motion-occupied voxel anchors across frames in a temporal window.
oASnPVaH6V.problem: Existing feed-forward video-to-4D methods treat 3D representations as the atomic unit and add temporal modeling externally, through canonical-shape deformation or per-frame generation, which limits motion expressivity or leaves a quality-efficiency trade-off.
oASnPVaH6V.method: MoVE-4D uses structured 4D Gaussians on motion-occupied voxels, reusing sparse voxel anchors across frames in a temporal window with time-dependent Gaussian attributes. It first predicts motion-occupied regions by voxel-wise occupancy merging, then decodes Gaussians from a Compact Temporal Structured LATent that aggregates multi-frame features at each voxel.
oASnPVaH6V.key_idea: Share sparse voxel anchors across time at the representation level and let time-dependent Gaussian attributes carry local dynamics, instead of deforming one canonical shape or generating each frame independently.
oASnPVaH6V.evidence: Comparisons with feed-forward baselines and a fine-tuned SS4D baseline on reconstruction quality and inference time, with ablations on motion occupancy, temporal attention and aggregation functions per reviewers.
oASnPVaH6V.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims a Pareto-optimal quality-efficiency trade-off surpassing existing feed-forward methods (the sentence is cut off).
oASnPVaH6V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find representation-level temporal sharing well matched to the redundancy, with favorable reconstruction quality and inference time against feed-forward baselines.
oASnPVaH6V.main_concern: Novelty over known voxel supports and temporal aggregation is unclear, aggregation by fixed voxel coordinate may mix unrelated features under large motion, and predicted occupancy lowers PSNR sharply versus ground truth (18.525 versus 24.849).

gylc519jq8.one_liner: Linear-time doubly stochastic attention that composes two entropic transport couplings through a learned low-rank pivot measure.
gylc519jq8.problem: Softmax attention is row-stochastic and quadratic in sequence length, while doubly stochastic attention, which also controls aggregate key participation, is typically expensive to compute.
gylc519jq8.method: LOTFormer routes interactions through a learned low-rank pivot measure and composes two entropic transport couplings. The ideal operator is doubly stochastic, has rank at most r, and applies to values in O(nr) time without forming the full pairwise matrix, as a replacement in pretrained embedding models or trained in vision Transformers.
gylc519jq8.key_idea: Factor attention through a learned low-rank pivot measure with two entropic transport couplings, giving a doubly stochastic operator applied in O(nr) time without an n-by-n matrix.
gylc519jq8.evidence: Pretrained embedding models of 1.5B to 7B parameters on retrieval including four LongEmbed tasks, vision Transformers under limited supervision, and a matched two-softmax pivot control.
gylc519jq8.claimed_gains: Preserves 98.3% to 98.9% of original softmax retrieval quality across embedding models from 1.5B to 7B; gte Qwen2 7B retains 98.9% of its nDCG@10 on four LongEmbed tasks and runs 2.05× faster end to end than FlashAttention-3 at 32k context (4.2× in a throughput-only test at 128k).
gylc519jq8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the construction sound and computationally well motivated, with a practical pretrained-conversion setting.
gylc519jq8.main_concern: The contribution of the doubly stochastic constraint is not isolated from the low-rank pivot factorization, and novelty over OTKE and positive-feature Sinkhorn constructions is unclear.

UQOHAJY9PK.one_liner: Diagnostic for flow matching posterior estimation based on the N^-1/2 scaling of endpoint variability across training-set sizes.
UQOHAJY9PK.problem: Flow matching posterior estimation is hard to diagnose with conventional posterior-accuracy metrics alone, because their values and trends are difficult to interpret across training-set sizes.
UQOHAJY9PK.method: The paper derives the predicted N^-1/2 scaling of endpoint variability, builds a statistical test for whether sample-size-driven behavior matches it, and adds a pseudo-dataset strategy that reduces repeated simulator runs.
UQOHAJY9PK.key_idea: Test whether endpoint variability of the learned flow shrinks at the predicted N^-1/2 rate as training-set size grows, flagging configurations that deviate from the theoretical scaling.
UQOHAJY9PK.evidence: Experiments including epidemiological simulators that probe limited network capacity, insufficient optimization and inaccurate numerical integration, with theory for an idealized infinite-width regularized two-layer network per reviewers.
UQOHAJY9PK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the careful theoretical analysis (ridge solution, influence-function expansion, endpoint central limit theorem) and the diagnostic as a complement to accuracy metrics.
UQOHAJY9PK.main_concern: The test may not separate limited data from a suboptimal configuration, since estimators with approximation or optimization bias can still show N^-1/2 fluctuations, and the idealized theory may not transfer to the architectures used.

uNPFwmZIYn.one_liner: Hierarchical LLM recommender mixing feed, search and ad histories under scenario quotas and extracting multiple interest vectors for two-tower retrieval.
uNPFwmZIYn.problem: Feed, search and advertising histories differ in frequency and temporal structure, so combining them requires deciding which events enter the model and how they are represented for retrieval.
uNPFwmZIYn.method: RED-Rec uses a scenario-aware 2-D mixing policy (per-scenario history quotas with blockwise temporal ordering) and learnable interest queries that extract multiple user representations. An item-aware gate distributes training supervision across queries, and at serving each query retrieves from precomputed item embeddings with results merged by maximum similarity.
uNPFwmZIYn.key_idea: Allocate per-scenario history quotas with blockwise temporal ordering, then read out several interest queries that retrieve independently and merge by maximum similarity, keeping user encoding independent of candidates.
uNPFwmZIYn.evidence: Public benchmarks and an industrial dataset, controlled mixer-by-query comparisons on a common backbone, matched-budget comparisons with MIND and ComiRec readouts per reviewers, and a one-week online A/B test.
uNPFwmZIYn.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims consistent retrieval-accuracy gains, largest for advertising, and an online A/B test whose result is cut off.
uNPFwmZIYn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the design practically coherent for multi-scenario retrieval, with candidate-independent encoding, industrial deployment and useful controlled comparisons.
uNPFwmZIYn.main_concern: The gain from blockwise interleaving over simpler orderings is not isolated, the closest related work (HyMiRec) is not compared, and fixed scenario quotas under sparse user histories are under-specified.

y0xfo60SPB.one_liner: Theory and activation patching showing in-context learning acts through a low-dimensional concept subspace stored in attention weights.
y0xfo60SPB.problem: It is unclear whether structured demonstrations induce low-dimensional concept inference in in-context learning, beyond regression and Bayesian accounts and mechanistic work on compact steering directions.
y0xfo60SPB.method: The paper models tasks as varying along intrinsic concept coordinates: for ridge and least-squares proxies, prediction decomposes into concept-coordinate regression and off-subspace leakage, and an idealized optimal single-layer linear attention head stores the concept subspace in its weights. It tests this by activation patching in Llama-3-8B on CounterFact-derived multi-relation prompts.
y0xfo60SPB.key_idea: Model ICL as estimation within an intrinsic concept subspace, so patching the subspace a head writes carries its full clean-corrupted effect while the complementary subspace carries none.
y0xfo60SPB.evidence: Theory for ridge and least-squares proxies and a linear attention head, plus activation patching in Llama-3-8B with concept swaps and random and cross-task matched-rank controls.
y0xfo60SPB.claimed_gains: A 73-dimensional subspace of the 4096-dimensional residual stream restores 78.8% of the clean-corrupted accuracy gap in a four-shot setting, whereas patching the complementary subspace restores 0%.
y0xfo60SPB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical framing that splits ICL into concept-coordinate estimation and off-subspace leakage and yields testable predictions about internal interventions.
y0xfo60SPB.main_concern: The patching results may reflect late-layer output steering or transfer of an already-computed answer representation rather than query-independent concept inference, and the idealized linear-attention model is not tied to real Transformer components.

r6QZahgnJY.one_liner: End-to-end streaming speaker-attributed ASR that interleaves audio chunks with previously generated speaker labels and text in one autoregressive context.
r6QZahgnJY.problem: End-to-end speaker-attributed ASR models generally process complete recordings, while streaming LLM-based ASR focuses on single-speaker transcription and lacks speaker attribution.
r6QZahgnJY.method: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming interleaves fixed-duration audio chunks with previously generated speaker labels and text in a single autoregressive context. This preserves speaker identities across chunks and gives speaker-attributed transcripts without a separate diarization stage.
r6QZahgnJY.key_idea: Place fixed-duration audio chunks, prior speaker labels and prior text in one autoregressive context so the model carries speaker identity across chunks without a diarization stage.
r6QZahgnJY.evidence: Five recognition benchmarks and 13 speaker-attributed settings against streaming systems including deployed services, with ablations on streaming conversion versus offline initialization and speaker label position per reviewers.
r6QZahgnJY.claimed_gains: The 7B model achieves the lowest mean recognition error among compared streaming systems on five benchmarks and the best or tied-best cpWER/cpCER in 12 of 13 speaker-attributed settings, with an expected latency of 2.00s.
r6QZahgnJY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a strong, simple open-source system with wide experiments across datasets and languages and a promised weight release.
r6QZahgnJY.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited because the chunk-wise speech-text interleaving follows prior streaming speech-LLM work, and cascaded diarization-plus-ASR baselines are missing.

T7HBx7rOnM.one_liner: Adversarial prompt tuning for CLIP against joint pixel and residual-stream feature perturbations, with activation-scale-calibrated budgets and vulnerability-weighted loss.
T7HBx7rOnM.problem: Adversarial prompt-learning methods defend only against image-space perturbations, although prompts live inside the model and an adversary could also perturb internal activations.
T7HBx7rOnM.method: JPFAT uses alternating projected gradient ascent over a fixed product threat set, Relative Activation Budgets that calibrate feature radii to layerwise activation scale, and entropy-regularized effort allocation across attack paths. A vulnerability-adaptive consistency loss emphasizes samples with larger output and internal representation drift.
T7HBx7rOnM.key_idea: Train prompts against an adversary that perturbs pixels and residual-stream activations together, with feature budgets scaled to each layer's activation magnitude and loss weighted toward vulnerable samples.
T7HBx7rOnM.evidence: Eleven datasets with base-to-new generalization and cross-dataset transfer per reviewers, evaluated under fixed-budget non-adaptive pixel, feature, sequential and joint attacks.
T7HBx7rOnM.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract says JPFAT improves accuracy under the joint pixel-feature adversary and its individual components while keeping competitive clean base-to-new generalization.
T7HBx7rOnM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear joint pixel-feature threat model and the layerwise calibration of feature budgets, backed by comprehensive experiments.
T7HBx7rOnM.main_concern: The internal-activation threat model assumes white-box write access that is hard to justify, and joint robust accuracy stays low (harmonic mean around 5%–6%).

Se8ZrBUsLb.one_liner: Casts diffusion noise schedule design as optimal control over Fisher information to obtain closed-form schedules with O~(d/n) sampling error.
Se8ZrBUsLb.problem: Existing theory proving Õ(d/n) sampling error bounds holds for specific noise schedules that differ from those used in practice.
Se8ZrBUsLb.method: The paper recasts schedule design as an optimal control problem whose objective is a functional from an upper bound on the KL sampling error involving the Fisher information and its time derivative. It derives sufficient conditions and a class of schedules, including forms used in practice, that reach Õ(d/n) when parameters follow the analysis.
Se8ZrBUsLb.key_idea: Track the scalar Fisher information along the diffusion and minimize a KL-error bound functional by optimal control, which yields closed-form schedules and parameter guidance.
Se8ZrBUsLb.evidence: Theory with sufficient conditions and a corollary covering VE-exponential, VP-sigmoid and VP-linear schedules, plus Section 5 experiments with held-out datasets per reviewers.
Se8ZrBUsLb.claimed_gains: Schedules in the derived class achieve the Õ(d/n) sampling error bound, where d is the data dimension and n is the number of discretization steps; no empirical numbers are stated.
Se8ZrBUsLb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find tracking the scalar Fisher information an elegant device that turns schedule design into a one-dimensional control problem with closed-form solutions covering schedules used in practice.
Se8ZrBUsLb.main_concern: The contribution is unclear against prior results (the bound matches earlier non-uniform-grid work and related KL-bound and grid-optimization papers are missing), the guarantee may need exponentially large n, and the experiments do not test it.

bQFObHOAfe.one_liner: Synthesizes diverse target-domain sequences for cross-domain recommendation from transferable preference profiles and sampled intent trajectories.
bQFObHOAfe.problem: Existing cross-domain sequence synthesis methods generate overly similar target sequences for users with similar preferences (Target-Intent Collapse), leaving other plausible intents underrepresented.
bQFObHOAfe.method: IntExpo has a Transferable Preference Profiler that uses discriminator-guided RL to extract transferable profiles from source histories, an Intent Generator that learns a conditional distribution over intent trajectories using neighbors' trajectories as extra supervision, and a Behavior Generator that produces multiple target sequences.
bQFObHOAfe.key_idea: Condition synthesis on a transferable profile plus a sampled discrete intent trajectory, supervised by neighbors' trajectories, so one source history yields several distinct target sequences.
bQFObHOAfe.evidence: Multiple cross-domain scenarios including cold-start settings and ablations against two cross-domain sequence synthesis baselines per reviewers, with qualitative embedding plots on Movie to Book.
bQFObHOAfe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the one-to-many framing of a source history mapping to several target intents a valid perspective and the decomposition with a diversity regularizer well motivated, with extensive experiments.
bQFObHOAfe.main_concern: Target-intent collapse is shown only qualitatively with no diversity statistics, the multi-stage pipeline is heavy without a simple diverse-sampling LLM baseline, and the baselines are dated.

lzS3RNdVJP.one_liner: Measures per-task dollars and joules across 18 model tiers; escalates only local-model failures to open-weight, then provider models.
lzS3RNdVJP.problem: Agentic tasks run hundreds of model turns, yet deployments are evaluated per model query rather than per completed task in dollars and joules.
lzS3RNdVJP.method: The paper defines the Intelligence Control Plane (models, middleware, machines) and an Intelligence System instance in which a local model attempts every task and observed failures escalate first to an open-weight model on owned accelerators, then to a provider model.
lzS3RNdVJP.key_idea: Local-first escalation: a local model attempts every task and only its observed failures move up a cost-ordered chain of larger models.
lzS3RNdVJP.evidence: Completed-task cost in dollars and joules is measured for 18 model tiers on TerminalBench V2.1, SWE-bench Verified, GAIA, and Terminal-Bench 4.0; the result repeats on SWE-bench Verified but not on GAIA.
lzS3RNdVJP.claimed_gains: On TerminalBench V2.1 the system keeps 75.1% of tasks on a laptop, sends 7.6% to a closed-source provider, and reaches 86.3% at 53× lower cost than the Claude Fable 5.1 anchor on owned hardware.
lzS3RNdVJP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pricing whole completed tasks, including discarded local work, with careful wall-level energy accounting is the right unit and is well executed.
lzS3RNdVJP.main_concern: The 53x saving rests on owned hardware whose purchase price is not charged (4.7x when rented), and the escalation judge is underspecified and tuned on the evaluation tasks.

qH7JM42Thw.one_liner: Estimates batch-level sample influence and reverses the gradient direction of detrimental samples during training instead of discarding them.
qH7JM42Thw.problem: Data valuation methods flag harmful samples but usually discard or downweight them, which wastes available data.
qH7JM42Thw.method: DIVE dynamically estimates sample values at the batch level and, at the optimization level, reverses the gradient directions of samples judged harmful, leaving the raw data untouched and fitting into standard training with minimal overhead.
qH7JM42Thw.key_idea: Flip the sign of the gradient contribution of batch samples with negative estimated influence, so harmful samples still supply a useful training signal.
qH7JM42Thw.evidence: According to reviewers, noisy-label classification on six image benchmarks with a ResNet-9 backbone plus LoRA fine-tuning of Gemma-3-12B-IT on verbalized classification tasks, compared against data valuation and dynamic batch curation baselines.
qH7JM42Thw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, intuitive, and low-overhead, with results that generally improve over vanilla training.
qH7JM42Thw.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the influence estimator is essentially TracIn-style gradient inner products, gains from gradient reversal over sample removal are small, and strong noisy-label baselines are missing.

cUXjICrRnt.one_liner: Studies when image-to-image generation training improves image-to-text understanding, mapping transfer across 19 generation tasks and 25 understanding capabilities.
cUXjICrRnt.problem: It is unclear when and how visual generation supervision improves visual understanding in unified multimodal models.
cUXjICrRnt.method: The authors compare controlled I2I/I2T task pairs (e.g., Jigsaw and Zoom-In) under six training recipes, then build OmniTaskonomy, a taxonomy of 19 I2I generation tasks and 25 I2T capabilities, and analyze gradient alignment between generation and understanding tasks.
cUXjICrRnt.key_idea: Measure transfer from each I2I generation task to each I2T capability using I2I-then-I2T training, and explain it through gradient alignment between the tasks.
cUXjICrRnt.evidence: Controlled paired tasks with varied I2I and I2T data budgets, then a transfer map on BAGEL-7B-MoT (roughly 50k I2I examples then 50k I2T per source model, per reviews), plus a gradient-alignment analysis.
cUXjICrRnt.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports that I2I training improves I2T performance under the correct recipe, with larger gains as I2I data grows.
cUXjICrRnt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear progression from controlled task pairs to the broad taxonomy, the extensive experiments, and an informative appendix.
cUXjICrRnt.main_concern: All core findings come from one architecture (BAGEL-7B-MoT), and the transfer study mixes dataset domain with task objective while under-discussing negative transfer.

5ZHGx146Hq.one_liner: Trains one omni model to propose actions and generate imagined next-state images before acting, using SFT then RL.
5ZHGx146Hq.problem: Irreversible actions with sparse feedback, such as a single Sokoban push, require anticipating consequences before acting, which action-only planners handle poorly.
5ZHGx146Hq.method: Agima uses a single omni model that both proposes actions and generates images of where they lead, treating imagined frames as observations to follow a plan, test an alternative, or compare plans; SFT teaches imagination and RL optimizes the textual planning decisions with binary task-success rewards.
5ZHGx146Hq.key_idea: Interleave action proposals with self-generated imagined next-state images used as observations, then RL-tune the textual planning decisions on binary success reward.
5ZHGx146Hq.evidence: Four environments (Maze2D, Sokoban, Pacman, PushT) with harder or unseen configurations excluded from training, compared with an action-only planner from the same backbone and proprietary VLMs.
5ZHGx146Hq.claimed_gains: With SFT alone on two-box Sokoban it solves 40% of four-box puzzles while seeing the real board once every five moves, versus 2% for an action-only planner fine-tuned from the same backbone.
5ZHGx146Hq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework clear and simple, with SFT on imagination traces and RL both helping and RL producing adaptive look-ahead behavior across varied long-horizon environments.
5ZHGx146Hq.main_concern: Novelty is limited since imagine-then-plan is established, and baselines are only the authors' own no-imagination models and proprietary VLMs, without comparison to model-based planning methods.

T2vmqzV4MD.one_liner: Diagnoses composition sensitivity in spatial-reasoning benchmarks and reweights items to balance task-agnostic factors such as answer value and object type.
T2vmqzV4MD.problem: Aggregate scores on spatial-reasoning benchmarks implicitly weight conditions by frequency, so skewed factor distributions can reorder VLM leaderboards.
T2vmqzV4MD.method: The Composition Sensitivity Test (CST), an information-theoretic diagnostic, identifies factors whose performance dependencies persist after adjusting for entangled factors; the Factor-Balanced Score (FBS) then reweights benchmark items to reduce the dominance of frequent levels of the diagnosed factors.
T2vmqzV4MD.key_idea: Compare a model's observed score with a factor-balanced counterpart, select factors by conditional dependence on performance, and reweight items so frequent factor levels do not dominate.
T2vmqzV4MD.evidence: Four video spatial-reasoning benchmarks (VSI-Bench, ReVSI, VSTI-Bench, OSI-Bench) and 14 VLMs, reusing existing item-level predictions without new inference.
T2vmqzV4MD.claimed_gains: Balancing changes the ranks of 53% of model-task pairs and the top-ranked model on 10 of 29 affected tasks.
T2vmqzV4MD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that benchmark composition is an important, understudied validity threat that is convincingly shown across four benchmarks and 14 models.
T2vmqzV4MD.main_concern: Balancing on factors such as answer value may change the evaluation target rather than remove bias, with no independent justification of the target distribution, and the object-type proxy depends on an evaluated model.

Ozl2QtZgxL.one_liner: Compresses video-diffusion KV caches by predicting later-layer keys and values from reconstructed earlier layers and quantizing the residuals.
Ozl2QtZgxL.problem: Autoregressive video diffusion KV caches grow with video length, and clustering-based quantization lets small reconstruction errors compound as later frames attend to compressed history.
Ozl2QtZgxL.method: Reconstructed cache states predict keys and values in subsequent layers through block-diagonal-plus-low-rank (block-DPLR) predictors, and the prediction residuals are quantized at low bit width; predictors can be reused across videos or lightweight block-diagonal parts refit to the current video.
Ozl2QtZgxL.key_idea: Predict next-layer KV from reconstructed current-layer KV with block-diagonal-plus-low-rank predictors, then low-bit quantize only the prediction residual.
Ozl2QtZgxL.evidence: Evaluated on HY-WorldPlay and MAGI-1 with disjoint calibration, selection, and evaluation prompts, parameter-matched predictor comparisons, and quantizer ablations against clustering-based baselines such as QVG.
Ozl2QtZgxL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting cross-layer dependencies through a compact block-DPLR predictor is a well-motivated, practical design with better memory-quality trade-offs than baselines.
Ozl2QtZgxL.main_concern: There is no granular runtime or latency breakdown, and evidence covers only two video models with small gains on HY-WorldPlay and extra latency for the video-adapted variant there.

qp444S4MBN.one_liner: Unified source-free domain adaptation using CLIP and a variational mutual-information objective to discover latent invariant factors.
qp444S4MBN.problem: Existing source-free domain adaptation methods target one scenario (closed, open, partial, open-partial, or generalized), so none handles all settings without knowing the source-target category relationship.
qp444S4MBN.method: CausalDA formulates adaptation from a structural causal model perspective, uses a pre-trained vision-language model such as CLIP to help form latent invariant factors, and optimizes a tractable Gaussian variational lower bound whose learnable covariance also weights pseudo-labels.
qp444S4MBN.key_idea: Discover latent invariant factors tied to model decisions by maximizing a Gaussian variational lower bound on mutual information with CLIP guidance, using learned covariance to weight pseudo-labels.
qp444S4MBN.evidence: Per the abstract and reviews, evaluation covers closed-set, open-set, partial-set, open-partial-set, and generalized SFDA settings, with comparisons to DIFO and ProDe and measures of source retention.
qp444S4MBN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a single method covering all SFDA scenarios is a practically important, well-motivated problem and that the variational bound with covariance weighting is interesting.
qp444S4MBN.main_concern: The unified-SFDA claim and the causal invariant-factor interpretation are not established clearly, and the optimization objectives (Eqs. 5-9) need clarification.

zeLrHMStfH.one_liner: Adds an image-pair fundamental-matrix prior, learned from camera pose, as a gated geometric bias on fine-stage semi-dense feature matching.
zeLrHMStfH.problem: Fine-stage localization in semi-dense matching relies on local appearance and lacks pairwise geometry, so it fails under weak texture, repetitive patterns, and large viewpoint changes.
zeLrHMStfH.method: GeMiL's Structured Geometry Head, supervised by camera pose, consolidates confident correspondences into a fundamental matrix that biases fine candidates, while Correspondence-Grounded Cross-Attention and Sharp Relation Injection sharpen and propagate correspondence-aware features across scales.
zeLrHMStfH.key_idea: Infer a fundamental matrix from confident matches and apply it as a gated, bounded bias that suppresses geometrically inconsistent fine-match candidates.
zeLrHMStfH.evidence: Multiple geometric tasks (including ScanNet and MegaDepth pose and InLoc localization, per reviews), ablations, and plug-in tests on other matchers.
zeLrHMStfH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adding geometry to the final matching stage is well motivated, the gated bounded bias is sensible, and accuracy is competitive at low runtime and memory across several tasks.
zeLrHMStfH.main_concern: The learned geometry head's value is not isolated (no same-refinement comparison with RANSAC-estimated geometry or direct matching accuracy), and methodological novelty is limited.

sXgBvlYEjD.one_liner: Refines a flow language model's clean estimate jointly with its induced state via Picard iteration (implicit-midpoint sampling).
sXgBvlYEjD.problem: First-order flow language model samplers hold the denoiser estimate fixed within a step, which is inaccurate for large steps because the estimate changes the transported trajectory and the state of later predictions.
sXgBvlYEjD.method: AIM-FLM builds the induced intermediate state from a candidate estimate by closed-form affine transport, re-evaluates the denoiser there, and repeats Picard iteration toward a joint fixed point; under linear schedules this is an implicit-midpoint step solved in denoising-estimate space.
sXgBvlYEjD.key_idea: Treat the denoising estimate as a state variable and solve for the fixed point where the estimate and the intermediate state it induces are consistent.
sXgBvlYEjD.evidence: Training-free sampling on pretrained flow language models, with convergence theory (geometric under local contraction, token stabilization under a margin condition), measured by generative perplexity under GPT-2 Large and entropy against native Euler/SDE samplers.
sXgBvlYEjD.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a reviewer reports 1.7–8× fewer network evaluations at matched entropy (Table 3).
sXgBvlYEjD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sampler is simple, training-free, and theoretically grounded, and that treating the estimate as a state variable is cleanly tested against fixed-state refinement.
sXgBvlYEjD.main_concern: With one iteration it reduces to an explicit second-order midpoint scheme yet is compared only with first-order native samplers, with entropy confounds and a perplexity-only quality metric.

2x6sowUqxz.one_liner: Pre-aligns inherited track queries' feature and spatial states with current-frame evidence before joint decoding in query-propagation multi-object tracking.
2x6sowUqxz.problem: Propagated track queries become temporally misaligned with the current observation, causing ownership conflicts where a detection query represents an existing target better than its track-query owner.
2x6sowUqxz.method: MATR adds a Motion-Aware Transformer (MAT) module that uses current-frame evidence to pre-align the feature and spatial states of inherited track queries before joint decoding with detection queries, and a geometric ambiguity measure links ownership-conflict risk to state difficulty.
2x6sowUqxz.key_idea: Correct inherited track queries with current-frame evidence before they interact with detection queries, applying larger corrections to more ambiguous states.
2x6sowUqxz.evidence: DanceTrack, SportsMOT, and BDD100K, with ablations against a strengthened MOTR baseline and an ambiguity versus ownership-conflict analysis on DanceTrack.
2x6sowUqxz.claimed_gains: On DanceTrack, 71.3 HOTA with 43M parameters and 179 GFLOPs; on BDD100K, 54.7 mTETA and 41.6 mHOTA without additional tracking data or external detector proposals.
2x6sowUqxz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the failure mode is clearly identified and the pre-alignment module is intuitive, with consistent association gains across three datasets at low overhead.
2x6sowUqxz.main_concern: Gains are entangled with a strengthened baseline and inconsistent ablation splits, and it is not shown that a consequential query error survives MOTR's six joint decoder layers.

59ZM3vNklp.one_liner: Turns lookahead rollout rankings into prompt-specific supervision and updates a residual critic online with FTRL for test-time alignment.
59ZM3vNklp.problem: Test-time alignment planners use lookahead rollout comparisons for one decision and then discard them, leaving later decisions to the same offline critic.
59ZM3vNklp.method: For each prompt, OVAL propagates rollout-induced rankings back to candidate segments, accumulates them as prompt-specific supervision, and uses Follow-the-Regularized-Leader to learn a lightweight residual correction to an offline critic while the LLM stays frozen.
59ZM3vNklp.key_idea: Accumulate lookahead rollout rankings across generation steps and fit a residual correction to the offline critic online with FTRL.
59ZM3vNklp.evidence: Experiments across multiple LLM backbones (Llama-3-8B and Qwen3-8B per reviews), benchmarks, and preferences with ablations, plus theory giving bounded decision regret under informative prompt-level signals and O(sqrt(T)) predictive regret for the FTRL update.
59ZM3vNklp.claimed_gains: not stated numerically in the abstract; a reviewer reports average scores of 66.41 vs. 64.97 for TPO on Llama-3-8B and 68.48 vs. 65.32 on Qwen3-8B (Table 1).
59ZM3vNklp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing lookahead information to adapt the critic per prompt without changing the LLM is an interesting idea with gains across models.
59ZM3vNklp.main_concern: The benefit of cross-step accumulation is small (74.51 vs. 74.17 without it), and comparisons are confounded by ArmoRM serving as both training signal and metric, differing reward sources, and unmatched compute.

vRvlhaux8I.one_liner: Adds a velocity flow-matching expert to a frozen VLA, denoising velocity jointly with position from shared noise for dynamic manipulation.
vRvlhaux8I.problem: VLA models predict where a robot should move but not how fast, and position tracking distorts the contact velocity that decides outcomes in tossing, flipping, sliding, or pushing.
vRvlhaux8I.method: VIPER attaches a velocity expert to a pretrained VLA with a flow-matching action expert, keeps the backbone frozen, and denoises velocity jointly with the position expert from shared noise so the noise-free position and velocity actions stay temporally aligned.
vRvlhaux8I.key_idea: Predict velocity with a second flow-matching expert denoised jointly with the position expert from shared noise, so position and velocity actions are temporally aligned.
vRvlhaux8I.evidence: Three VLA backbones and six dynamic manipulation tasks, from tossing and flipping to catching and handover, in simulation and on a real robot.
vRvlhaux8I.claimed_gains: VIPER raises mean success from 32% to 51%.
vRvlhaux8I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well chosen and grounded in control theory, with the flaw of position-only tracking clearly analyzed and empirical improvements that are substantial and fairly consistent.
vRvlhaux8I.main_concern: VIPER is tested only on six dynamic tasks, so the claim that it reduces to the base policy on quasi-static manipulation is never verified.

bfkltsEDHx.one_liner: Models preferred, rejected, and tied preference outcomes with an annotation-noise model for text-to-image preference optimization.
bfkltsEDHx.problem: Text-to-image alignment methods assume strict, noise-free binary preferences, yet about 11% of Pick-a-Pic annotations are ties and human labels are noisy.
bfkltsEDHx.method: NTPO explicitly models three preference outcomes (preferred, rejected, tied) while accounting for noisy and inconsistent annotations, preserving tie information instead of discarding it.
bfkltsEDHx.key_idea: Extend binary preference optimization to a ternary likelihood with tie outcomes and a noise-transition model so noisy ternary labels still recover the true preference distribution.
bfkltsEDHx.evidence: Experiments across multiple benchmarks with both UNet-based and MM-DiT backbones (per reviews), compared with binary preference optimization methods, plus a derivation showing that standard ternary optimization under noise is biased.
bfkltsEDHx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ties and annotation noise are well-motivated practical issues and that the method is simple, with clear and solid derivations.
bfkltsEDHx.main_concern: The noise-transition model is restrictive (flips only between opposite preferences, noise-free ties), and the evaluation uses dated backbones and limited baselines.

nJUpmGrHr5.one_liner: A single shared-weight world model acting as policy, action-conditioned simulator, and value evaluator in a closed loop for dexterous manipulation.
nJUpmGrHr5.problem: Existing world models append an action head to a world simulator without coupling them into a closed decision-and-learning loop for policy improvement.
nJUpmGrHr5.method: One model with shared weights exposes a policy that proposes action chunks, a simulator that predicts their visual consequences, and an evaluator that scores the predicted outcomes; data scaling moves from monocular egocentric data to stereo egocentric data, then robot-domain adaptation with robot trajectories and human-robot alignment data.
nJUpmGrHr5.key_idea: Couple policy, action-conditioned simulator, and value model in shared weights so predicted consequences of candidate action chunks are scored to drive policy improvement.
nJUpmGrHr5.evidence: Per reviews, real-world tasks on three bimanual dexterous platforms, a scaling trend for stereo egocentric human data (about 130K raw hours of human data and over 100 hours of robot data), and model-based RL and planning tests on two tasks with 20 rollouts each.
nJUpmGrHr5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the system is comprehensive and a substantial engineering effort, with large-scale data curation, a multi-stage training pipeline, scaling trends for egocentric human data, and higher real-world success than baselines.
nJUpmGrHr5.main_concern: Novelty is unclear because the components (policy and simulator interfaces, value formulation, optimizer, memory, tactile expert) are existing methods assembled together, and the self-evolution gains rest on very few rollouts.

XXErbp05BV.one_liner: Simulates Scale, Mask, and Perturb merging operations during expert fine-tuning so independently trained experts merge better.
XXErbp05BV.problem: Standard expert training optimizes task loss alone, so merged performance is not guaranteed, and existing merge-aware training ignores common merging operations and adds training cost.
XXErbp05BV.method: SMAT jointly optimizes expert loss and expected loss at simulated merged parameters built from sampled scaling coefficients, masks, and additive noise, and adds periodic scheduling, kernel fusion, and parameter storage switching to need one forward and one backward pass per step.
XXErbp05BV.key_idea: View merging from an expert's side as Scale (reweight own update), Mask (drop coordinates), and Perturb (add other experts' updates), and train on randomly simulated versions.
XXErbp05BV.evidence: Four language and vision-language backbones and five merging methods, with ablations of each component.
XXErbp05BV.claimed_gains: SMAT improves the mean score across five merging methods by 1.07–2.16 points over the strongest baseline for each backbone, with less than 2% training-time overhead over standard fine-tuning.
XXErbp05BV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Scale/Mask/Perturb decomposition is simple and intuitive and applies to independently trained experts without access to other experts' checkpoints.
XXErbp05BV.main_concern: Randomly sampled scale, masks, and i.i.d. noise may not approximate real structured merges, so Perturb behaves like a generic flatness regularizer rather than a merge simulation.

6TN5XjXY6B.one_liner: Synthesizes executable occupational work from real public files and repairs task or rubric defects found by executing reference deliverables.
6TN5XjXY6B.problem: Expert-authored occupational work is costly and slow to produce, while unconstrained synthesis yields tasks with weak factual grounding or inconsistent requirements.
6TN5XjXY6B.method: Evidence-Based Work Construction retrieves public files guided by O*NET occupational knowledge and synthesizes context, companion materials, a work request, and an itemwise rubric around them; Execution-Guided Consistency Verification renders a reference deliverable, attributes each unsatisfied rubric item to the agent, task, or rubric, and repairs task and rubric defects iteratively.
6TN5XjXY6B.key_idea: Ground each work unit in retrieved real files, then attribute failed rubric items to agent, task, or rubric and repair task and rubric defects until the audit passes.
6TN5XjXY6B.evidence: WorkGenesis-35B is trained with SFT on 20K synthesized work units and evaluated on GDPvalAA-v2, APEX-Agents-AA, and further benchmarks (abstract truncated); reviewers note coverage of 65 occupations.
6TN5XjXY6B.claimed_gains: WorkGenesis-35B, trained with SFT on only 20K synthesized work units, achieves the highest scores among comparable-scale baselines on five reported metrics across GDPvalAA-v2, APEX-Agents-AA, and further benchmarks; no score values are stated.
6TN5XjXY6B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction and verification pipeline is described in detail, with prompts and case studies in the appendix, and yields consistent downstream improvements.
6TN5XjXY6B.main_concern: The error-attribution and repair components are not tested against simpler alternatives, and there are no comparisons with other data synthesis methods, RL experiments, or contamination checks.

zjAvB0X1hX.one_liner: Maps the graph spectrum onto the unit circle via the Joukowski relation, implemented as a second-order recurrence for stress prediction.
zjAvB0X1hX.problem: Message passing smooths away the high-frequency components that finite element stress concentrations need, and unitary propagation that preserves magnitudes costs O(Ked) through matrix functions and high-order approximations.
zjAvB0X1hX.method: LiftGCN maps the real spectrum of a normalized graph operator onto the unit circle through the Joukowski relation and realizes it as a second-order recurrence needing one sparse aggregation per layer (O(ed) complexity), with lightweight local nonlinear residuals added.
zjAvB0X1hX.key_idea: Apply the Joukowski map to lift the graph operator's real spectrum onto the unit circle, giving an energy-preserving linear backbone as a simple second-order recurrence.
zjAvB0X1hX.evidence: Finite element stress datasets (including a Mines Paris set with 20 test meshes, per reviews) against various graph architectures including UniGCN, plus a proof of unit-modulus characteristic roots and energy preservation for the linear backbone.
zjAvB0X1hX.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a reviewer reports a small LiftGCN matching UniGCN's PSNR@1% (20.327 vs 20.096) at roughly 10× lower latency (1.528 vs 15.000 ms, Table 1).
zjAvB0X1hX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the recurrence is simple, computationally efficient, and mathematically motivated for preserving the high-frequency information needed for stress prediction.
zjAvB0X1hX.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the Joukowski recurrence resembles the Chebyshev recurrence (no ChebNet comparison), and evaluation uses low-variability linear-elasticity datasets with checkpoints chosen by test-set MSE.

h71u6TlGot.one_liner: Reuses one reference PDE solution to generate a family of exact design-state pairs through residual inheritance, avoiding new state solves.
h71u6TlGot.problem: PDE-constrained optimization repeatedly solves a design-dependent state equation, which is expensive.
h71u6TlGot.method: For separable elliptic PDEs, one reference solution induces coefficient-state pairs satisfying the residual-inheritance identity R_theta = c_theta R_0, enabling hard-constrained design updates from cached fields; a full-space check at restricted stationarity builds a Wendland-RBF candidate, and an acceptance gate decides whether to refresh the reference.
h71u6TlGot.key_idea: Use the residual-inheritance identity R_theta = c_theta R_0 to turn one reference solution into a family of PDE-consistent states, refreshing the reference only when the family limits progress.
h71u6TlGot.evidence: Thermal experiments comparing analytical updates with independent PINN re-solves, and end-to-end physics-informed optimization under a common adaptive retraining protocol with an independent FVM audit of the objective.
h71u6TlGot.claimed_gains: Analytical updates take 0.12 - 0.14 s versus 165 - 493 s for independent PINN re-solves; end-to-end the method uses 2 rather than 16 state PINNs and reaches a 30.75% lower independently FVM-audited objective in 251.1 rather than 1683.8 seconds of algorithm time.
h71u6TlGot.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting the governing equation's analytical structure to reuse reference solutions is a valuable optimization perspective with a clear theoretical basis.
h71u6TlGot.main_concern: The construction needs separable coefficients and keeps flux directions fixed within a reference family, restricting reachable designs, and the discrete-residual validity and wall-clock gains are not fully shown.

YDsz140Di9.one_liner: Benchmarks whether auditors can verify agent-harness run records, showing harness-written records are unverifiable and a second outside writer restores checking.
YDsz140Di9.problem: An agent's run record is written by the harness that drives the agent, so an auditor who was not there can read it but cannot check it.
YDsz140Di9.method: Hearsay has five harnesses run fourteen tasks while model examiners from three vendors and a human panel answer questions from the records, with every cited passage labeled mechanically by who wrote it; a sandbox ledger of what passes between harness and model acts as a second writer.
YDsz140Di9.key_idea: Label every citation in an auditor's answer by who wrote the cited text, and add a sandbox ledger as a second writer outside the harness.
YDsz140Di9.evidence: Five harnesses, fourteen tasks, model examiners from three vendors, a human panel, deliberate record alterations, and an audit finding that in all sixteen deployed frameworks the harness is the only writer.
YDsz140Di9.claimed_gains: Model examiners claim corroboration for 18 to 55 points more of their evidence than the labels support, and the best of them notices only half of the alterations made to a record; with one writer, readers can name the fault in up to nine runs in ten but cannot check the record.
YDsz140Di9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is relevant and clearly motivated, that the citation-level provenance instrument is reusable, and that the outside log catches falsified entries the harness's own hash chain accepted.
YDsz140Di9.main_concern: Several headline results follow by construction from the design (the harness is the only writer under the native record), and it is unclear how the outside log becomes a practical solution.

wLeBitbnbM.one_liner: Single-pass reference-conditioned RGBA video generator with a visibility router that skips transparent tokens' later DiT updates.
wLeBitbnbM.problem: Game-style RGBA video datasets are scarce and generate-then-matte pipelines blur semi-transparent regions, while existing joint RGB-alpha models are mostly text-conditioned and inefficient.
wLeBitbnbM.method: They build GameAlpha-2.4K, a 2.4K-clip game-style RGBA dataset made with matte-friendly synthesis, multi-hypothesis alpha recovery, and compositing-based quality gates, train a reference-conditioned generator that produces RGB and alpha in one pass, and add a visibility router that identifies transparent tokens early and bypasses their later DiT updates.
wLeBitbnbM.key_idea: Use predicted transparency to route transparent tokens around later DiT updates, locking them to self-predicted x0 endpoints along the original flow-matching schedule.
wLeBitbnbM.evidence: The GameAlpha-2.4K dataset, comparisons by FVD against matched two-stage baselines, and a backbone speedup measurement for the visibility router.
wLeBitbnbM.claimed_gains: Lower FVD than matched two-stage baselines and a 1.2× backbone speedup with comparable quality; no FVD values are stated.
wLeBitbnbM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that single-pass RGBA generation for compositable game assets is practically relevant and that the transparency-routing strategy is simple and gives a speedup.
wLeBitbnbM.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (it reuses the Wan-Alpha VAE, Wan I2V conditioning, and DoRA), the speedup is modest and not compared with faithful regional-sampling baselines, and the game-asset domain is narrow.

sNzMoG8Zxe.one_liner: Scores KV-cache entries by gradient-based downstream sensitivity of the model's final output, enabling query-agnostic eviction.
sNzMoG8Zxe.problem: Existing KV eviction methods score entries by their local contribution to the same layer's attention output and ignore their downstream impact on later layers.
sNzMoG8Zxe.method: KVgrad uses a first-order Taylor approximation and the chain rule to factorize a cached value's impact into a linear local component and a gradient-based downstream sensitivity term, adds a magnitude-aware scoring scheme for stability, and can distill the score into a lightweight MLP that predicts it from local hidden-state features.
sNzMoG8Zxe.key_idea: Score each cached entry as its local contribution times a gradient-based sensitivity of the model's final hidden state, derived from a first-order Taylor expansion and the chain rule.
sNzMoG8Zxe.evidence: RULER and LongBench evaluations across several models and tasks against local-only baselines (including KVzip+), ablations of the magnitude-aware and probe-specific components, and a distilled MLP scorer.
sNzMoG8Zxe.claimed_gains: KVgrad achieves an average maximum compression ratio of 5.9x with negligible performance loss (<2%) on RULER and LongBench.
sNzMoG8Zxe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adding downstream sensitivity to local scoring is a meaningful, well-motivated extension, supported by broad experiments across models and tasks and by component ablations.
sNzMoG8Zxe.main_concern: Exact KVgrad scoring is costly (about 872 s at 256K context) and the cheap MLP surrogate loses quality, so the benefit depends on amortizing scoring cost over reused contexts.

aWeQpzTH0Q.one_liner: Retargets the loss with overlap weights to build Neyman-orthogonal learners for heterogeneous long-term treatment effects under low overlap.
aWeQpzTH0Q.problem: Estimating heterogeneous long-term treatment effects from combined short-term and long-term observational data is unstable when treatment assignment or long-term outcomes have limited overlap in some subpopulations.
aWeQpzTH0Q.method: LT-O-learners retarget the loss with custom overlap weights that downweight low-overlap samples in the canonical surrogacy setting; the retargeted loss recovers the true HLTE pointwise and satisfies Neyman-orthogonality.
aWeQpzTH0Q.key_idea: Reweight the orthogonal learning loss with overlap weights that downweight low-overlap samples, giving a retargeted loss that stays Neyman-orthogonal.
aWeQpzTH0Q.evidence: Theory showing nuisance error enters only through higher-order terms and, under a linear function class, that the weights control asymptotic variance, plus synthetic and real-world experiments (a real-data application per reviews).
aWeQpzTH0Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is meaningful and the theory is clear and substantial, covering orthogonality, nuisance robustness, and variance control, with supporting simulations.
aWeQpzTH0Q.main_concern: The robustness and optimality claims are narrower than presented (variance stabilization needs a correctly specified linear model, and the link between the weights and efficient HLTE estimation is unclear), and benchmarked meta-learners are dated.

Ak87ljzQb3.one_liner: Shows that models relying more on generalization suffer greater retain-set damage under unlearning than memorization-heavy models.
Ak87ljzQb3.problem: Little research has examined how the way a model learned, through memorization or generalization, shapes how it later unlearns.
Ak87ljzQb3.method: The authors classify memorization- and generalization-heavy models using grokking in modular addition, introduce bucketed modular addition to control the mix of the two strategies along a spectrum, and test the same relationship in LLM unlearning on verbatim and factual recall.
Ak87ljzQb3.key_idea: Control the memorization-generalization mix with bucketed modular addition and measure retain-set damage after unlearning along that spectrum.
Ak87ljzQb3.evidence: Modular addition with grokking, bucketed modular addition across the memorization-generalization spectrum, and LLM unlearning in verbatim and factual recall settings.
Ak87ljzQb3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular-addition model organisms are well chosen and the controlled experiments are well designed, with well-scoped claims on a new angle for unlearning.
Ak87ljzQb3.main_concern: The headline claim may follow by definition (unlearning a shared mechanism hurts every example that uses it), and the paper gives no tested, actionable guidance.

MBZ6JVdHkt.one_liner: Replaces importance-weight clipping with a smooth two-branch sequence-level kernel to fix gradient starvation of under-generated positive responses in off-policy RLVR.
MBZ6JVdHkt.problem: With reused rollouts in RLVR, clipping suppresses under-generated positive responses in the low-importance-weight tail while letting over-generated negative responses dominate the high-weight tail.
MBZ6JVdHkt.method: ReSPO uses a smooth two-branch sequence-level kernel derived from an alpha-divergence variational objective and an exponential variance-control tilt; the positive branch keeps a nonzero gradient weight for under-generated positives and the negative branch suppresses heavily over-generated negatives.
MBZ6JVdHkt.key_idea: Replace hard clipping with a smooth two-branch weight kernel: a positive branch that keeps gradient for low-weight positives and a negative branch that suppresses extreme-ratio negatives.
MBZ6JVdHkt.evidence: Dense and MoE Qwen3 models under rollout reuse with three staleness settings, compared with GRPO, GSPO, and VESPO, plus held-out benchmarks and tail analysis.
MBZ6JVdHkt.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports faster early optimization, better final training scores, and higher held-out benchmark performance under rollout reuse.
MBZ6JVdHkt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is clearly motivated and explained, with tail behavior tied to the two branches, explicit parameter reasoning, and an implementation that is easy to follow.
MBZ6JVdHkt.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the positive and negative branches, and related asymmetric-update methods such as SAPO and BAPO are not compared.

P9ePSTsLkj.one_liner: Corrects foreground degradation in video background replacement by recasting the edited state to the source background and transferring the residual.
P9ePSTsLkj.problem: Instruction-guided background replacement and relighting must preserve foreground identity, structure, texture, and motion, but training-free pipelines restrict natural lighting and directly trained models degrade foreground details.
P9ePSTsLkj.method: A forward branch predicts the video under the target background and lighting, and a backward recasting branch places the edited foreground state back into the source background domain, where its discrepancy from the source trajectory captures foreground degradation; that residual is transferred to the target prediction, and a joint VLM-DiT parses the instruction into semantic-, foreground-, and background-centric token groups.
P9ePSTsLkj.key_idea: Recast the current edited state into the source background domain so its discrepancy from the known source trajectory isolates foreground degradation, then add that residual to the target prediction.
P9ePSTsLkj.evidence: Comparisons with prior methods (FlowPortal per reviews) on instruction alignment, lighting quality, structural fidelity, and detail preservation, with ablations of the recasting mechanism and conditioning design.
P9ePSTsLkj.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims superior overall performance in instruction alignment, lighting quality, structural fidelity, and fine-detail preservation with only modest added cost.
P9ePSTsLkj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the recast idea is intuitive and well motivated for the trade-off between flexible relighting and foreground preservation, and that ablations show recasting improves identity, structure, and detail metrics.
P9ePSTsLkj.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate the components (conditioning is ablated only as a whole, with no matched source-reconstruction residual baseline), and the residual is applied unmasked without checking that it stays on the foreground.

k0suIalZsf.one_liner: Optimizes personalized canonical geometry with vertex-bound Gaussians, then models dynamic offsets with triangle-bound Gaussians for monocular head avatars.
k0suIalZsf.problem: Coarse canonical geometry and limited motion information in Gaussian head avatars hinder faithful reconstruction of expression-dependent appearance details.
k0suIalZsf.method: GDAvatar first optimizes the canonical mesh with a vertex-bound Gaussian representation, then uses triangle-bound Gaussians to model dynamic attribute offsets by jointly encoding canonical and dynamic features balanced by an attention fusion module, and builds a continuous editable Gaussian map for texture editing.
k0suIalZsf.key_idea: Progressively release Gaussian degrees of freedom: constrained vertex-bound Gaussians fix canonical geometry first, then full triangle-bound Gaussians model dynamic appearance.
k0suIalZsf.evidence: Experiments on multiple datasets against state-of-the-art methods with ablations, using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS plus qualitative cross-identity reenactment (per reviews).
k0suIalZsf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the progressive allocation of Gaussian degrees of freedom is well motivated, with consistently strong reconstruction results and an editable UV representation.
k0suIalZsf.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the pipeline is a staged combination of familiar components, and the geometry-appearance disentanglement claim is only indirectly validated, with no quantitative cross-identity evaluation.

XScKMmbFmx.one_liner: Open-source pipeline synthesizing executable GUI, MCP, and CLI computer-use environments and verifiable tasks, filtered by execution-based quality gates.
XScKMmbFmx.problem: Scaling agent learning in real computer systems is hard and risky, and existing environment synthesis typically specializes in a single interaction interface.
XScKMmbFmx.method: WildAWM builds executable environments that jointly support GUI, MCP services, and CLI using only open-source models, and filters tasks with execution-based quality gates combining heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes of judgment robustness.
XScKMmbFmx.key_idea: Synthesize persona-driven multi-interface worlds and keep only tasks passing execution-based gates: solvable by rollouts, hard enough, and with verifiers robust to counterfactual probes.
XScKMmbFmx.evidence: Synthesized environment-task pairs, a verifier check with 95% agreement on 100 rollouts, and training evaluations on two model scales (per reviews).
XScKMmbFmx.claimed_gains: The pipeline synthesizes 341 long-horizon environment-task pairs that can require over 100 agent steps to solve; the visible abstract is truncated before reporting training gains.
XScKMmbFmx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline is comprehensive and timely, covering diversity, cross-interface support, solvability, difficulty, and verifier reliability, with plans to release code, environments, tasks, and verifiers.
XScKMmbFmx.main_concern: Gains are confounded with GLM-5.2 distillation and lack controlled comparisons with competing environment pipelines or with agents trained on single environments.

mDNXLt7gYB.one_liner: Trains a world action model with outcome tokens, then applies contrastive denoising guidance toward success and away from failure.
mDNXLt7gYB.problem: Fine-grained manipulation produces many failed real-robot trials, which standard practice discards or compresses into a scalar reward, preference, or advantage.
mDNXLt7gYB.method: CALM trains a world action model with outcome tokens and applies contrastive denoising guidance that attracts actions toward success and repels them from failure; the analysis shows every two-weight guidance rule acts along one contrast direction that aligns with the task-critical correction when a measurable scaffold ratio is below one.
mDNXLt7gYB.key_idea: Most failures are last-mile deviations from successful motion, so the success-versus-failure contrast direction localizes the correction using one outcome label per trajectory.
mDNXLt7gYB.evidence: Six real-robot tasks, a failure audit across operators and a public dataset (127 of 132 procedure-complete failures were last-mile, per reviews), a contamination experiment, and longer-horizon and simulation tests.
mDNXLt7gYB.claimed_gains: On six real-robot tasks, CALM improves average success by 12.8 points over a baseline named in the truncated abstract.
mDNXLt7gYB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the last-mile failure observation is useful and supported by audits across operators, tasks, and a public dataset, with convincing real-robot results.
mDNXLt7gYB.main_concern: The audit excludes 20 of 152 raw failures, relies on fixed task procedures, and is not shown to predict beforehand when CALM will help, while the claim that gains vanish for scaffold ratios above one exceeds the proposition.

qmn19MKk7e.one_liner: Introduces FlexBench and a penalty-aware score, then weights DPO margins by severity of limb-action errors to reduce caption hallucination.
qmn19MKk7e.problem: VLMs often misidentify which person performs an action or which limb is involved in video captions, especially across camera cuts, and evaluation and training do not distinguish missing information from incorrect assertions.
qmn19MKk7e.method: FlexBench (3,105 shots and 18,161 evaluation queries) provides human-verified identities and reference-derived checklists, the Graded Physical Alignment score (GPA) credits correct content and deducts incorrect or fabricated actions, and GM-DPO assigns larger preference margins and training weight to more severe action errors.
qmn19MKk7e.key_idea: Scale the DPO preference margin and sample weight by the severity of action errors, graded by a rubric that credits correct content and deducts fabricated actions.
qmn19MKk7e.evidence: Three VLM backbones on FlexBench, compared with other preference objectives including DPO, plus additional multimodal benchmarks.
qmn19MKk7e.claimed_gains: GM-DPO improves GPA over DPO by 2.02–3.40 points across three VLM backbones and, on Qwen3-8B, reduces the weighted hallucination rate by 21.3% relative to DPO.
qmn19MKk7e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that FlexBench targets an important, under-measured failure mode of fine-grained limb actions across persons and shots, and that the graded-margin loss is well motivated.
qmn19MKk7e.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate severity weighting from stronger generic preference optimization, with no constant-margin, matched-weight, or shuffled-severity controls.

R3QBIp9ayL.one_liner: Refines personalized query rewrites iteratively: a behavioral reward model picks the winner, an LLM turns the difference into text feedback.
R3QBIp9ayL.problem: Query enhancement quality is hard to measure because direct satisfaction feedback is sparse and the abundant indirect behavioral signals are only noisy proxies.
R3QBIp9ayL.method: A hierarchical model links sparse direct satisfaction signals with denser behavioral feedback to yield a reward model; reward-guided feedback descent then uses that reward model and the enhancement objective to pick the preferred candidate numerically and to synthesize textual feedback that guides the LLM enhancer.
R3QBIp9ayL.key_idea: Use the reward model, not the LLM, to choose the preferred candidate, and have the LLM only write textual feedback explaining the difference to guide the next rewrite.
R3QBIp9ayL.evidence: Public benchmarks and real-world e-commerce data, with ablations, human evaluations, and statistical tests (per reviews).
R3QBIp9ayL.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says the algorithm consistently improves user satisfaction.
R3QBIp9ayL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically significant and the framework coherently connects sparse satisfaction labels, behavioral signals, and iterative refinement, with broad evaluation on e-commerce and public data.
R3QBIp9ayL.main_concern: The e-commerce evaluation is circular, since GPT-5.2-generated satisfaction labels train the reward model and also serve as the main metric, and the method largely extends Feedback Descent.

ZwAqnNaEFS.one_liner: Compresses medical VLM visual tokens by merging similar, spatially consistent token groups and keeping one representative token per group.
ZwAqnNaEFS.problem: The large number of visual tokens from medical images raises compute and inference cost, and existing compression relies on internal attention signals that conflict with FlashAttention or targets only 3D imaging.
ZwAqnNaEFS.method: MedScissor combines semantic-similarity and neighborhood-consistency scores to find redundant token relationships, progressively merges related groups until the compression budget is met, then keeps one representative token per group using local centrality and global deviation scores.
ZwAqnNaEFS.key_idea: Group tokens by semantic similarity plus neighborhood consistency, then keep in each group the token with the best local-centrality and global-deviation score, without using attention maps.
ZwAqnNaEFS.evidence: Six representative 2D medical imaging benchmarks, plus eight benchmarks and eight baselines overall with depth-connectivity ablations covering planar and volumetric settings (per reviews).
ZwAqnNaEFS.claimed_gains: On six 2D medical imaging benchmarks MedScissor reduces visual tokens by 50% while retaining 98.6% of original performance, with a 1.4× prefill speedup and a further 49.2% figure that is cut off in the truncated abstract.
ZwAqnNaEFS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical because it works on projected features without internal attention maps and gives a competitive accuracy-compression balance across many baselines and ablations.
ZwAqnNaEFS.main_concern: Novelty over prior graph-based token merging such as ST-SimDiff is not established, and the method description does not fully match the released code's group-size repair step.

XSoAH3GPyx.one_liner: Predicts a query-specific 3D point inside a matched Gaussian through a closed-form decoder rather than using its center.
XSoAH3GPyx.problem: 3DGS-based direct matching assigns the matched Gaussian's center to the query keypoint, so a correct match can still yield an inaccurate 3D coordinate and hurt PnP pose estimation.
XSoAH3GPyx.method: ReCoLoc separates region retrieval from point prediction: contribution-weighted identity encoding aggregates multiview descriptors using rendering contributions for retrieval, query-conditioned coordinate decoding predicts the 3D position inside the retrieved Gaussian from the query descriptor, and correspondence-aware landmark selection jointly assesses retrieval and coordinate reliability.
XSoAH3GPyx.key_idea: Give each Gaussian landmark a query-conditioned coordinate function (a lightweight affine decoder fitted by closed-form ridge regression) that predicts where inside the Gaussian the keypoint lies.
XSoAH3GPyx.evidence: Three standard visual localization benchmarks with extensive ablations, using GS-CPR pose refinement (per reviews).
XSoAH3GPyx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that center-based correspondence is a clear, well-motivated error source and that separating region retrieval from query-conditioned coordinate prediction is simple and effective.
XSoAH3GPyx.main_concern: Gains are shown only through pose and reprojection metrics, with no direct validation of 3D accuracy and no SfM-point baseline showing that the 3DGS map is needed.

cjRmmfE7A2.one_liner: Post-training LoRA method that keeps learned directions, rebalances singular-value gains with a fixed nonlinear map, and restores nuclear norm.
cjRmmfE7A2.problem: Trained LoRA updates are dominated by a few singular directions and are overly strong, which can compromise capabilities beyond the target task.
cjRmmfE7A2.method: LoRA-Norm keeps the learned LoRA directions, rebalances their gains with a fixed nonlinear transformation (Newton-Schulz as in Muon, per reviews), and restores the original nuclear norm, so each module is attenuated according to its own imbalance with no calibration data, extra training, or inference overhead.
cjRmmfE7A2.key_idea: Keep LoRA singular directions, flatten their singular-value spectrum with a fixed nonlinear map, then rescale to the original nuclear norm, which attenuates imbalanced modules more.
