cjRmmfE7A2.evidence: Two backbones and three tasks, compared with post-hoc spectral pruning and gradient-guided editing configurations, with energy-matched scaling and flat-spectrum controls.
cjRmmfE7A2.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; LoRA-Norm improves average specialization and retention across two backbones and three tasks over the evaluated spectral pruning and gradient-guided editing configurations.
cjRmmfE7A2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, data-free, applies directly to trained adapters with no added inference cost, and gives average gains in both target performance and retention.
cjRmmfE7A2.main_concern: Simple energy-matched scaling recovers much of the benefit, so the necessity of the specific two-stage normalization is not established.

nkWf0oVWBW.one_liner: Benchmark pairing spoken smart-home requests with visual and spatial-audio context, plus a procedural-memory agent baseline, PROME.
nkWf0oVWBW.problem: Existing smart-home benchmarks express requests only in language, leaving context-dependent requests that point at objects or refer to what is seen or heard unevaluated.
nkWf0oVWBW.method: OmniSmartHome pairs each spoken request with its surrounding visual and spatial-audio context in 1,360 synthetic and 272 real-world episodes, and PROME equips agents with specialized audio-visual perception tools and procedural memory for orchestrating their use.
nkWf0oVWBW.key_idea: Make requests underspecified in speech alone so the target device can only be resolved by combining gesture, sound, space, and speaker cues, with procedural memory guiding tool use.
nkWf0oVWBW.evidence: Evaluation of 16 omnimodal LLMs, with PROME tested on six of them; reviews cite grounding accuracy, goal accuracy, and LLM-as-judge scoring.
nkWf0oVWBW.claimed_gains: PROME generally improves performance across six Omni-LLMs; no numeric gains are stated in the abstract.
nkWf0oVWBW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that resolving underspecified spoken requests from multimodal context is a well-motivated problem, with a useful grounding taxonomy and substantial benchmark validation.
nkWf0oVWBW.main_concern: Some nominally multimodal categories are solvable from text alone (87.5% text-only vs. 82.6% multimodal grounding on G1 episodes), so the benchmark's dependence on multimodal evidence is not well established.

AeotKSTZrH.one_liner: Retrieves only reliable historical frame features and conditions restoration on physics-inspired degradation cues for endoscopic video enhancement.
AeotKSTZrH.problem: Generic temporal propagation aggregates historical frame information that may already be degraded and lacks awareness of endoscopy-specific degradations such as blood haze, specular reflection, motion blur, and low contrast.
AeotKSTZrH.method: A reliable trajectory memory retrieval mechanism (RTMR) selects trustworthy historical features and suppresses unreliable ones, and a physics-inspired degradation conditioning mechanism (PIDC) uses visual cues (color, contrast, gradient, and motion proxies per reviews) to adapt restoration to local degradation.
AeotKSTZrH.key_idea: Evaluate motion-aligned historical candidates for reliability before aggregating them, and condition restoration on analytic physics-inspired degradation cues.
AeotKSTZrH.evidence: Ablations in a full 2x2 factorial with a learnable-token control, five baselines on STSVD (a synthetic smoke dataset), and real-world datasets scored with no-reference IQA and temporal metrics (per reviews).
AeotKSTZrH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating temporal correspondence from temporal reliability is a clear insight, and that ablations support the claim that the physics cues rather than extra parameters drive the gains.
AeotKSTZrH.main_concern: Evidence for multi-degradation restoration is indirect, since full-reference results come only from a synthetic smoke dataset, and the baselines omit closest competitors such as STANet, PromptIR, and AirNet.

omnX6mksBA.one_liner: Evaluates LLM agents cheaply: selects tasks and reruns sequentially until a calibrated score-error estimate meets a requested tolerance.
omnX6mksBA.problem: Efficient benchmarking methods cannot set the number of tasks for a requested tolerance, need historical results from thousands of LLMs while agentic benchmarks have fewer than two hundred agents, and assume one outcome per task.
omnX6mksBA.method: TITRATE converts a requested score tolerance into a number of executions: it selects one task at a time and stops when its calibrated estimate of score error meets the tolerance; for repeated attempts it runs every task once and then chooses which tasks to rerun, with two variants for little history or a formal guarantee.
omnX6mksBA.key_idea: Select tasks one at a time using regularized task models and stop when a calibrated estimate of full-benchmark score error reaches the requested tolerance.
omnX6mksBA.evidence: Six agentic benchmarks and six baselines with calibration on historical agents; reviews mention time-based splits and 35 SWE-bench submissions for monetary savings.
omnX6mksBA.claimed_gains: On six agentic benchmarks and against six baselines it lowers score error by up to 30% at the same task budget, meets a four-point tolerance for at least 91% of agents on every benchmark (the strongest adaptive baseline reaches as little as 73%), and needs about 20% fewer runs than uniform rerunning.
omnX6mksBA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically important and the method directly controls an interpretable score error, with well-justified design choices evaluated across several agent benchmarks.
omnX6mksBA.main_concern: Reliability depends on evaluated agents resembling the historical calibration distribution, with coverage of only 0.85–0.88 against the stated 0.95 under time-based splits with later, stronger agents.

mYKXddhUeO.one_liner: Splits each neuron into concept-specific subunits by re-routing preceding-layer contributions so subunit activations sum exactly to the original.
mYKXddhUeO.problem: Sparse autoencoders and similar methods disentangle polysemantic neurons but introduce approximation errors, creating a Pareto trade-off between monosemanticity and functional faithfulness.
mYKXddhUeO.method: DUNE identifies concept-specific contributions from the preceding layer and re-routes them into separate subunits whose aggregation exactly recovers the original activation; it applies directly to pretrained models without labels or training an auxiliary model.
mYKXddhUeO.key_idea: Partition each neuron's incoming contributions by concept, via clustering, into additive subunits so the original activation is recovered exactly by construction.
mYKXddhUeO.evidence: Several models including DINOv2 (5+ models against 10+ methods per reviews), with top-activating examples and concept-steering experiments.
mYKXddhUeO.claimed_gains: Monosemanticity that is best or competitive across several models including DINOv2 while preserving faithfulness exactly; no numbers are stated.
mYKXddhUeO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the neuron-level decomposition is well motivated, that exact additive preservation of activations is a clear advantage over lossy SAE-style methods, and that the baseline coverage is strong.
mYKXddhUeO.main_concern: Novelty is unclear relative to PURE and to cross-layer transcoders that add back residual error, and faithfulness is exact by design rather than measured.

EhutNBs58R.one_liner: Speeds on-policy distillation of autoregressive image generators with asynchronous speculative rollout and cross-step prefetching verified by the updated student.
EhutNBs58R.problem: Student rollout is the training bottleneck in on-policy distillation of autoregressive image generators, and a batch-synchronous speculative implementation can even reduce efficiency because sequences obtain different amounts of verified progress.
EhutNBs58R.method: AOSR preserves sequence-specific verified progress and adaptively removes completed sequences, and Cross-Step Speculative Refill (CSR) reuses completed batch positions to pre-generate next-rollout sequences that are re-verified with the updated student, resampling mismatched tokens.
EhutNBs58R.key_idea: Let each sequence advance by its own verified speculative progress instead of batch-synchronously, and reuse idle slots to prefetch next-step tokens that are re-verified after the student update.
EhutNBs58R.evidence: LlamaGen and Janus-Pro with GKD and VarKD distillation (Janus-Pro on COCO per reviews), with a CSR ablation showing the harm of reusing tokens without verification.
EhutNBs58R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated by a quantitative observation that synchronous speculative rollout is slower, and that asynchronous execution gives substantial end-to-end training speedups.
EhutNBs58R.main_concern: The contribution is largely a system-level scheduling redesign, CSR adds only about 0.11 of extra end-to-end speedup, and comparisons with other GPU scheduling and speculative-rollout methods are missing.

ebqRLiKG4l.one_liner: Proves a capacity-feasibility trade-off in hyperbolic entailment cones and relaxes transitivity with a violation budget to remove it.
ebqRLiKG4l.problem: Ganea-style hyperbolic entailment cones cannot define aperture near the origin, and the size of this infeasible ball trades off against cone capacity, degrading performance at both extremes.
ebqRLiKG4l.method: The authors formalize the trade-off for any transitive cones with outward axes and radius-dependent aperture, introduce (epsilon, delta)-transitivity with an infeasible-region radius and an allowance for transitivity violations, and build cones defined everywhere except the origin that have at least the original capacity and generalize the original cones.
ebqRLiKG4l.key_idea: Relax exact transitivity to (epsilon, delta)-transitivity, trading a bounded violation budget for removal of the infeasible region around the origin.
ebqRLiKG4l.evidence: Hierarchical word embeddings (WordNet, MCG, Hearst) and the hyperbolic vision-language models MERU, HyCoCLIP, and UNCHA, plus a proof of the trade-off.
ebqRLiKG4l.claimed_gains: On hierarchical word embeddings (WordNet, MCG, Hearst) the proposed method outperforms the original entailment cones in 10 of 12 settings, with gains of up to 27.6 points.
ebqRLiKG4l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formal account of the trade-off is clean and the transitivity relaxation is natural, giving simple drop-in cones that remove the empty region near the origin.
ebqRLiKG4l.main_concern: Shadow Cones (Yu et al., 2024) already remove the infeasible region and outperform the proposed cones under their training setup, so the gains and the open-problem framing are questionable.

DMeOaBA5hO.one_liner: Formulates multi-agent traveling officer dispatch as an event-driven semi-MDP with a semi-autoregressive decoder and per-agent adaptive objective preferences.
DMeOaBA5hO.problem: Existing multi-agent resource collection methods optimize only collected volume with uniform-step formulations that add no-op transitions and ignore coupling among agents dispatched together, while real dispatch must also balance timeliness and fairness.
DMeOaBA5hO.method: PRISM treats MTOP as an event-driven asynchronous multi-agent SMDP where decisions trigger only on agent availability; a state-aware context encoder models agents, resources, and dispatch history, a semi-autoregressive decoder generates joint assignments, and an adaptive preference head infers per-agent weights over Resource Volume, Timeliness, and Fairness.
DMeOaBA5hO.key_idea: Trigger decisions only when agents become available and let a preference head set each agent's weights over volume, timeliness, and fairness.
DMeOaBA5hO.evidence: Four public datasets spanning crime, emergency medical services, and traffic, against multi-objective variants of strong baselines.
DMeOaBA5hO.claimed_gains: PRISM outperforms the strongest multi-objective baselines by 16.98%, 6.19%, and 4.81% on Volume, Timeliness, and Fairness, respectively.
DMeOaBA5hO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the event-driven formulation fits the task's temporal structure and the architecture is well designed, with evaluation on heterogeneous datasets with multiple runs.
DMeOaBA5hO.main_concern: The benefits of the new mechanisms are not isolated, baselines are somewhat old, and the SMDP formulation is only loosely tied to the network components.

pWlccZIhb8.one_liner: Derives local graphical criteria for when background knowledge on edges at treatment X improves causal-effect identifiability in MPDAGs.
pWlccZIhb8.problem: It is unclear how and when local background knowledge about edges incident to a treatment X improves the identifiability of the effect of X on an outcome Y beyond what the Markov equivalence class gives.
pWlccZIhb8.method: The paper derives a necessary and sufficient condition for the validity of proposed orientations of edges incident to X, local orientation rules that decide whether an adjacent undirected edge can be directed without enumerating all DAGs in the equivalence class, and, via possible mediators, a polynomial-time necessary and sufficient criterion for when knowledge improves identifiability.
pWlccZIhb8.key_idea: Use possible mediators of X on Y to decide in polynomial time whether orienting edges incident to X changes which causal effects are identifiable.
pWlccZIhb8.evidence: Theorems and proofs for the graphical criteria, validated on benchmark networks.
pWlccZIhb8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical results and proofs look solid and that the question of when background knowledge improves identifiability is natural and satisfactorily answered.
pWlccZIhb8.main_concern: Practical relevance is unclear and the scope is narrow (knowledge only on edges incident to X), and the decision procedure is not fully local because it searches paths from possible mediators to Y.

q4RabT4YYh.one_liner: Writes DeltaNet memory along a preconditioned key from inverse past-key covariance to minimize interference on past-key responses.
q4RabT4YYh.problem: DeltaNet's update rule leaks the correction signal into every past key that is not orthogonal to the current key, interfering with stored associations.
q4RabT4YYh.method: IA-DeltaNet decouples the key used for error evaluation from the write direction, which is chosen by a constrained quadratic program that minimizes squared interference on past-key responses while preserving the current-key correction; the closed form is a preconditioned key from the inverse uncentered covariance of past keys, approximated with a diagonal covariance to stay chunk-parallelizable.
q4RabT4YYh.key_idea: Choose the memory write direction as the preconditioned key (inverse uncentered past-key covariance applied to the current key) that minimizes interference on past-key responses while keeping the current-key correction.
q4RabT4YYh.evidence: Multi-query associative recall, streaming video understanding, and language modeling (a single 374M model per reviews), compared with recurrent-memory baselines.
q4RabT4YYh.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says interference-aware writing improves retention under high associative load and improves over recurrent-memory baselines.
q4RabT4YYh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is clear and principled, with an interpretable closed-form solution that reduces to DeltaNet for isotropic key covariance and a diagonal variant that is economical and chunk-parallel.
q4RabT4YYh.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from the interference view or from generic preconditioning, since preconditioned delta-rule methods are not compared, and language-model evidence is limited to one 374M model.

DVF7CrxPyM.one_liner: Pure-exploration bandit algorithm identifying the player-optimal socially stable matching when preferences form through a social network.
DVF7CrxPyM.problem: Learning models for matching markets treat preferences as fixed lists, ignoring that stability-governing preferences emerge after intrinsic evaluations propagate through a social network, so uncertainty in one player's ranking can stem from others' evaluations.
DVF7CrxPyM.method: They derive an instance-dependent lower bound from a network-weighted information-allocation problem over intrinsic source pairs and design a Source-Aware algorithm guided by that variance structure.
DVF7CrxPyM.key_idea: Sample intrinsic source player-arm pairs according to a network-weighted information allocation, because uncertainty in a player's final ranking originates in other players' intrinsic evaluations.
DVF7CrxPyM.evidence: Theory: an instance-dependent lower bound and a Source-Aware algorithm designed from it; experiments are not stated in the available abstract.
DVF7CrxPyM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the socially formed preference setting well motivated and interesting, with Example 1 clearly showing the source-destination mismatch.
DVF7CrxPyM.main_concern: The paper does not discuss how performance depends on the key parameter Gamma, and the assumption that the designer knows who talks to whom needs better motivation.

h238OYfi1p.one_liner: Reward-free RL pretraining learns a latent scheduling-strategy space, then test-time latent search adapts it to new JSSP objectives and scales.
h238OYfi1p.problem: Deep RL for job-shop scheduling trains separate policies for fixed objectives and settings, limiting reuse when the instance distribution, scale, objective or scheduling setting changes.
h238OYfi1p.method: Stage one learns a reusable latent strategy space by factorizing long-horizon successor occupancies from diverse scheduling trajectories, without a downstream scheduling reward. Stage two freezes the model and searches the latent space, scoring each candidate by the downstream objective of its complete rollout.
h238OYfi1p.key_idea: Factorize successor occupancies of diverse scheduling trajectories into a latent strategy space, then search that space at test time using full-rollout objective values.
h238OYfi1p.evidence: A single JSSP-pretrained frozen model is evaluated on unseen distributions and scales, flexible job-shop scheduling and unseen objectives against learning baselines, with optimizer comparisons and rollout-budget experiments per reviewers.
h238OYfi1p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating scheduling-strategy learning from downstream optimization is well motivated and that one frozen checkpoint is shown to transfer across sizes, distributions and objectives.
h238OYfi1p.main_concern: Evidence gaps: ablations do not isolate reward-free pretraining from architecture and test-time search, runtime and compute comparisons are missing or heterogeneous, and the successor-measure Equation (1) conflicts with discount factor gamma = 1 in Table 5 (raised by two reviewers).

KYbAQd3y68.one_liner: Navigates a lightweight semantic-structural codebase map to find targets without loading code bodies, then selects context by cost.
KYbAQd3y68.problem: Coding agents repeatedly process full code accumulated in their exploration history, so repository-scale code reasoning trades accuracy against context cost.
KYbAQd3y68.method: FastCode decouples repository exploration from content consumption: a structural scouting mechanism traces dependencies on a semantic-structural map without loading code bodies, and cost-aware context selection then builds the context for final reasoning.
KYbAQd3y68.key_idea: Exploration runs over a structural map of the repository instead of code text, and only high-value code is loaded into the final reasoning context under a cost-aware selection.
KYbAQd3y68.evidence: Evaluated on SWE-QA, LongCodeQA, GitTaskBench, and LOC-BENCH against multiple baselines (including Cursor and SWEQA-Agent per reviews), with backbone comparisons.
KYbAQd3y68.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of cost-efficient repository-scale code reasoning is practical, the evaluation spans four benchmarks with multiple baselines, and the paper is easy to follow.
KYbAQd3y68.main_concern: Gains over baselines are small and lack variance estimates (43.28 vs 43.17 for Cursor on a 3-repository SWE-QA subset), and the context-selection objective (relevance, cost, trade-off coefficient) is not clearly defined.

eg16jDMikI.one_liner: Subtracts a scalar multiple of the vocabulary-row mean from output-head rows before quantization, preserving softmax predictions exactly.
eg16jDMikI.problem: Large vocabularies make output heads a substantial inference cost in small language models, and quantizing them can distort predictions.
eg16jDMikI.method: Softmax reparameterization searches over functionally equivalent output heads by subtracting a scalar multiple of the vocabulary-row mean from every output row and choosing the coefficient by validation KL. For linear-softmax heads full-precision predictions are unchanged, and a rank-one correction extends the construction to nonlinear logit paths.
eg16jDMikI.key_idea: Softmax is invariant to a shared shift across logits, so a searched per-row mean shift changes the weights quantization sees without changing full-precision outputs.
eg16jDMikI.evidence: Seven output heads and three quantizers, a W2 stress test, GPTQ on Phi, an untouched holdout on Phi and BLOOM, and transfer of WikiText-selected coefficients to C4 and OpenWebMath.
eg16jDMikI.claimed_gains: At W4, test KL falls by 93% on XGLM under RTN and by 73-77% on Phi, BLOOM, and BLOOMZ under activation-weighted MSE.
eg16jDMikI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, rests on the translation invariance of softmax, needs no retraining or decoder change, and is tested across many heads and quantizers with KL-based evaluation.
eg16jDMikI.main_concern: Relevance is unclear: only the output head is quantized, benefits are model-dependent (fixed mean centering already matches the search on XGLM), and there is no comparison of bits saved versus KL damage against simply keeping the head at higher precision.

injepGU6q2.one_liner: BReSC is a training-free MCMC-based remasking sampler for masked diffusion models using entropy-balanced rates and online staleness control.
injepGU6q2.problem: Remasking under parallel token updates induces transition kernels that deviate from the desired sampling dynamics, through drift bias from unbalanced transitions and staleness bias from updating coupled tokens from stale contexts.
injepGU6q2.method: An entropy-balanced remasking policy satisfies coordinate-wise detailed balance, and an online optimization routine reduces a staleness proxy by suppressing high-interference parallel updates. Both biases are characterized theoretically under idealized assumptions.
injepGU6q2.key_idea: Make remasking rates satisfy coordinate-wise detailed balance via entropy balancing, and choose parallel updates online to minimize a staleness proxy of interference between coupled tokens.
injepGU6q2.evidence: OpenWebText unconditional generation and downstream LLaDA tasks (LLaDA-8B per reviews), mainly compared against ReMDM.
injepGU6q2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the MCMC view a useful way to reason about remasking and the paper well written, with substantial unconditional-generation gains over ReMDM from a training-free method.
injepGU6q2.main_concern: Few baselines are tuned (mainly ReMDM), and the guarantees hold only under idealized assumptions, with the controller validated through a proxy cost and no direct bias measurements.

iKJaj914cG.one_liner: Solves early-universe Boltzmann equations with neural distribution functions, Monte Carlo importance sampling, and natural-gradient time evolution.
iKJaj914cG.problem: Grid-based quadrature solvers for early-universe Boltzmann equations scale poorly to complicated processes and parameter scans.
iKJaj914cG.method: Encodes particle properties in physics-inspired neural distribution functions, evaluates phase-space integrals by Monte Carlo with importance sampling tools from collider physics, and evolves the system with the natural gradient method.
iKJaj914cG.key_idea: Replace fixed momentum grids with parametrized, exactly samplable distribution functions whose collision integrals are estimated by importance-sampled Monte Carlo and whose parameters evolve by natural gradient.
iKJaj914cG.evidence: Demonstrates the individual components, then computes the effective number of relativistic neutrino degrees of freedom N_eff in the Standard Model; reviewers note agreement with the literature and a solver uncertainty estimate.
iKJaj914cG.claimed_gains: Claims the most numerically precise calculation to date of N_eff in the Standard Model; no numeric value is stated in the abstract.
iKJaj914cG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and motivated, with a real scientific result (N_eff agrees with the literature) and a general framework where a new process needs only its matrix element.
iKJaj914cG.main_concern: The neural networks play a small role (the headline N_eff calculation does not use the MadNIS neural importance sampling), so ML contribution and fit to ICLR are questioned.

LzmDvXTKvH.one_liner: One-step latent flow-matching harmonizer conditioned on depth, normals, albedo, roughness and illumination to fix edited neural driving-scene renders.
LzmDvXTKvH.problem: Neural reconstructions of driving scenes produce artifacts under novel viewpoints and virtual-asset insertion, and RGB-space harmonizers need data-intensive training for each new editing operation.
LzmDvXTKvH.method: Reformulates harmonization as physical-intrinsic harmonization, using imperfect depth, normals, albedo, roughness and illumination from the reconstructed scene as a compositional interface for test-time edits. PIH is a one-step harmonizer trained with latent flow matching on predicted velocity plus perceptual supervision on the decoded clean endpoint, with mixed RGB-grounded and self-rollout histories for temporal consistency.
LzmDvXTKvH.key_idea: Condition a one-step flow-matching harmonizer on intrinsic buffers so edits compose physical factors instead of needing insertion-specific paired RGB correction data.
LzmDvXTKvH.evidence: Human preference experiments across Waymo, nuPlan and PandaSet, plus ablations on losses and history sources.
LzmDvXTKvH.claimed_gains: PIH is preferred to the prior method in 77.41% of human-preference comparisons while using fewer paired training frames, and it additionally enables illumination control.
LzmDvXTKvH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using physical scene properties as a common editing interface for insertion and relighting is a well-motivated direction with promising results.
LzmDvXTKvH.main_concern: The gain is not isolated to the intrinsic representation, since there is no RGB-conditioned control with the same backbone, data and training, and baselines use official checkpoints trained on different degradations.

PT2mFt0N68.one_liner: Training-free UAV object navigation that keeps candidate evidence as persistent state and actively acquires extra views before authorizing STOP.
PT2mFt0N68.problem: Aerial ObjectNav methods strengthen memory, exploration, and grounding but do not keep candidate-level evidence as a persistent state across search, verification, and stopping, which matters under partial, viewpoint-dependent observations.
PT2mFt0N68.method: EviNav builds a shared evidence specification separating search-supporting cues from acceptance-critical evidence, accumulates candidate evidence across observations, and actively acquires complementary views when evidence is insufficient. Unresolved evidence guides further observation, contradictions support rejection, and STOP is authorized when evidence suffices.
PT2mFt0N68.key_idea: Tracks per-candidate evidence states (unresolved versus contradicted) as persistent memory that drives viewpoint acquisition, rejection, and the stop decision.
PT2mFt0N68.evidence: Full 1,000-episode, 14-scene UAV-ON test protocol, with module ablations over search, evidence persistence, and active verification.
PT2mFt0N68.claimed_gains: SR of 27.00% and OSR of 36.60% on the 1,000-episode, 14-scene UAV-ON protocol; the SPL value is cut off in the abstract.
PT2mFt0N68.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating plausible-candidate discovery from identity verification is well motivated, and the full-benchmark evaluation with module ablations shows substantial gains.
PT2mFt0N68.main_concern: The active-verification ablation also removes candidate approach and viewpoint acquisition, and failed-episode false-acceptance statistics are missing, so the benefit of better acceptance decisions is not isolated.

JHEFtTu9aK.one_liner: Training-free TTS emotion steering that splits each emotion vector into shared and residual parts and controls them separately.
JHEFtTu9aK.problem: Emotion-conditioned TTS often fails to express the requested emotion reliably, and conventional steering (CoCoEmo) treats each emotion vector as one direction with a single global strength.
JHEFtTu9aK.method: EmoRES decomposes an emotion vector into a shared component that moves speech away from neutral and a residual component that directs generation toward the requested emotion, then controls the two without retraining the backbone.
JHEFtTu9aK.key_idea: Subtracts the across-emotion mean as a shared away-from-neutral component and separately reweights the centered residual that carries emotion identity.
JHEFtTu9aK.evidence: IEMOCAP on IndexTTS-2 and CosyVoice2 backbones with four objective emotion metrics, plus OOD and human evaluations.
JHEFtTu9aK.claimed_gains: Over CoCoEmo on IndexTTS-2 and CosyVoice2, rank correlation improves by 26.13 and 12.97 percentage points (118.8% and 33.1% relative) and emotion hit rate by 12.95 and 6.92 points (20.1% and 9.8% relative); human evaluation shows a relative improvement up to 35.0%.
JHEFtTu9aK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and practical, with norm-matched ablations and consistent gains over CoCoEmo across backbones and human evaluation.
JHEFtTu9aK.main_concern: Limited novelty and an unvalidated interpretation: the split is an algebraic mean-and-residual decomposition over a few emotions, and reading the parts as general arousal versus emotion identity is not fully shown.

T4jYIaxIcJ.one_liner: Benchmark of post-compromise incident response for LLM agents on forensic disk snapshots, plus rubric-guided agentic RL training (RETrace).
T4jYIaxIcJ.problem: Existing cybersecurity benchmarks focus on pre-compromise settings, leaving end-to-end post-compromise incident response by agents underexplored.
T4jYIaxIcJ.method: SecRespond gives agents a forensic disk snapshot plus alerts, vulnerability scans, and baseline checks from a host security product, and requires forensic reports on intrusions, baseline risks, and vulnerability risks plus a remediation plan across 10 cyber ranges. Reviews describe RETrace, an agentic RL method that uses LLM-based rubric scores and traces evidence in final reports back to earlier tool outputs for credit assignment.
T4jYIaxIcJ.key_idea: Score agents on post-compromise disk investigation with rubrics, and train them by tracing evidence in final reports back to earlier tool outputs for credit assignment.
T4jYIaxIcJ.evidence: 23 frontier LLMs evaluated on the OpenCode agent harness across 10 cyber ranges (4 entry-point types, 21 ATT&CK techniques, 5 operating systems), with training on a two-fold split of the ranges.
T4jYIaxIcJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the end-to-end post-compromise task is well motivated, uses realistic executed cyber ranges, and the benchmark covers many frontier models.
T4jYIaxIcJ.main_concern: The benchmark is small (10 ranges, mostly cryptomining) and relies on LLM-judged report rubrics with limited human validation, which may reward better-written reports rather than better investigation.

y7C085ys73.one_liner: Unified empirical study of 41 latent-action-model design choices for manipulation, plus proxy metrics for predicting downstream performance.
y7C085ys73.problem: Latent action model research is fragmented, with design choices evaluated in isolation under inconsistent settings, so the factors that determine downstream manipulation performance are unclear.
y7C085ys73.method: The authors unify representative LAM methods in a common autoencoding framework and systematically vary 41 design choices across latent action modeling paradigms, learning objectives and regularization, and integration strategies, and they examine four proxy metrics for latent action quality.
y7C085ys73.key_idea: Compare latent action designs under one shared autoencoding framework and policy pipeline, and test whether proxy metrics reliably predict downstream manipulation performance.
y7C085ys73.evidence: Three widely used benchmarks plus real-world robot manipulation tasks.
y7C085ys73.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is a substantial, well-controlled comparison of fragmented latent-action methods, with simulation and real-robot validation and useful practical guidance.
y7C085ys73.main_concern: Conclusions are drawn with other choices fixed (one VLA structure and base VLM), leaving applicability to other VLA and WAM architectures unclear, and some fine-grained rankings lack uncertainty estimates.

tDiKtIhJoT.one_liner: Trains speculative-decoding drafters with token-conditional continuation values from a Bellman recursion over prefix histories, crediting each candidate separately.
tDiKtIhJoT.problem: Weighting a local acceptance objective by a detached continuation weight shared across candidates at one prefix can raise one-step acceptance probability while lowering expected accepted length.
tDiKtIhJoT.method: D-VOLT derives a Bellman recursion over complete prefix histories and an exact gradient decomposition of expected accepted length, where each candidate's credit combines prefix reachability, immediate acceptance reward, and continuation value. In practice it approximates continuation values by dynamic programming over a compact top-K candidate graph that shares sampled earlier histories (abstract truncated).
tDiKtIhJoT.key_idea: Give each candidate token its own training credit from prefix reachability, acceptance reward, and token-conditional continuation value, estimated by dynamic programming on a top-K candidate graph.
tDiKtIhJoT.evidence: A counterexample, a Bellman recursion, an exact gradient decomposition, and experiments against baselines including DSpark (abstract truncated); reviewers cite a measured spread of continuation values across 16 candidates.
tDiKtIhJoT.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviewers cite 4.05%-9.74% higher average accepted length than DSpark at roughly 5.05x higher training-step time.
tDiKtIhJoT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and supported by a counterexample and gradient decomposition showing that candidates at the same prefix have different continuation values.
tDiKtIhJoT.main_concern: Training cost is high (about 5.05x DSpark step time), and the gap between the exact theory and the practical top-K, shared-history, detached approximation is not analyzed.

YqUjb0f1UC.one_liner: Two-stage MoE router: vector-quantized codewords shortlist experts, then exact scoring runs only on the shortlist.
YqUjb0f1UC.problem: Granular MoEs with many small experts perform better, but routing cost grows enough to dominate computation and memory.
YqUjb0f1UC.method: AIR-MoE assigns tokens to VQ codewords to build a candidate expert set (coarse shortlisting), then computes exact routing scores restricted to that shortlist. It approximates true top-K routing without full expert scoring, places no structural constraints on expert parameters, drops in for standard routers, and comes with a lower bound on mass recall.
YqUjb0f1UC.key_idea: Use an inverted-index structure in which VQ codewords map tokens to overlapping expert shortlists and exact router scores are computed only within the shortlist.
YqUjb0f1UC.evidence: Perplexity-FLOPs comparisons against existing MoE routers with up to more than a million tiny experts, plus a mass-recall lower bound; reviewers cite C5 and OpenWebText2 in a PEER-style single-MoE-layer setup with three seeds.
YqUjb0f1UC.claimed_gains: Improves the perplexity-FLOPs trade-off over existing MoE routers and gives consistent perplexity improvements over the best baseline; no numeric values are stated in the abstract.
YqUjb0f1UC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree AIR-MoE offers flexible coarse-to-fine routing without structural constraints on experts, at routing cost comparable to PEER, with consistent perplexity gains over the best baseline.
YqUjb0f1UC.main_concern: Scale and efficiency evidence is limited (single MoE layer, models under about 300M active parameters, isolated router latency, shortlist refresh overhead), and the claim that it approximates true top-K routing is weakly supported.

Ix6fuIIi1a.one_liner: Diagnoses a value-to-action shortcut in LLM bandit exploration and prompts metacognitive monitoring and control to rebalance exploration and exploitation.
Ix6fuIIi1a.problem: LLMs behave greedily in sequential decision tasks, exploring far less than humans, and thinking mode amplifies sensitivity to estimated value while limiting uncertainty-directed exploration.
Ix6fuIIi1a.method: Fits an adapted computational model of human exploration-exploitation behavior to choices of ten LLMs in three bandit settings with human reference data, and analyzes reasoning traces. It then adds minimal prompts that ask LLMs to assess their confidence and whether to explore or exploit, and to let those assessments regulate choice.
Ix6fuIIi1a.key_idea: Prompt LLMs to assess confidence and decide whether to explore or exploit before choosing, breaking the value-to-action shortcut that thinking mode amplifies.
Ix6fuIIi1a.evidence: Ten LLMs on three bandit settings with human reference data, plus reasoning-trace analysis and longer-horizon experiments according to reviews (abstract truncated).
Ix6fuIIi1a.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off; it says metacognitive reasoning systematically reshapes behavior across LLMs and settings).
Ix6fuIIi1a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical analysis is broad (ten LLMs, three human-referenced bandit tasks) and that separating value and uncertainty sensitivity with a computational model gives more insight than reward alone.
Ix6fuIIi1a.main_concern: Limited novelty over prior work on LLM exploration (Nie et al., Zhang et al., Pan et al.), and confounds such as prompts that explicitly cue exploration and fitted sensitivities that may be estimation artifacts.

vVHoEifVa7.one_liner: Converts ANNs to LIF spiking networks that reuse prior neuron state and compute only frame-to-frame activation updates for streaming inference.
vVHoEifVa7.problem: Spiking networks need an efficient way to process unbounded data streams, and it is unclear how an SNN incrementally tracks its corresponding continuous-valued network.
vVHoEifVa7.method: Proves that a discrete SNN's output continuously tracks the instantaneous ANN output implied by its input, via attractor dynamics, then builds LIF-Stream, a conversion framework where the converted SNN reuses its previous activation state and computes only updates between frames.
vVHoEifVa7.key_idea: Treat LIF dynamics as tracking a time-varying ANN attractor, so state carried across frames needs fewer time steps per frame than resetting.
vVHoEifVa7.evidence: A tracking theorem and evaluation on three large-scale streaming inference benchmarks with distinct modalities (reviews cite object detection, speech recognition, and event gestures).
vVHoEifVa7.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims the best efficiency-accuracy trade-off versus high-accuracy SNN techniques on three streaming benchmarks.
vVHoEifVa7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the attractor-tracking view of LIF dynamics interesting and the method simple, reusing neuron state without extra SNN training or calibration.
vVHoEifVa7.main_concern: Novelty over prior incremental-computation work (Sigma-Delta Networks, Delta Networks, streaming ANN-to-SNN conversion) is unclear, and the theory leaves effects of residual initial state unanalyzed.

ouAo23G7qu.one_liner: CURE-UCB selects rising-bandit arms by estimating each arm's cumulative reward over the remaining horizon.
ouAo23G7qu.problem: In rising bandits an arm's value as an investment depends on the time remaining, yet the benefit of knowing the horizon as side information has been underexplored.
ouAo23G7qu.method: CURE-UCB is a horizon-aware algorithm that estimates each arm's cumulative reward over the remaining horizon and uses it to choose arms. The paper proves dominance over a representative horizon-agnostic algorithm under structured assumptions and gives a regret upper bound for the general concave rising setting.
ouAo23G7qu.key_idea: Index each arm by its estimated cumulative reward over the remaining horizon rather than extrapolating its current reward, so arm choice depends on time left.
ouAo23G7qu.evidence: Regret proofs under structured assumptions and for general concave rising bandits, plus experiments on synthetic benchmarks and real-world model selection tasks against rising and non-stationary baselines.
ouAo23G7qu.claimed_gains: On some instances CURE-UCB incurs only O(1) regret versus Omega(T) for the horizon-agnostic algorithm, and it achieves lower regret than rising and non-stationary baselines over a wide range of horizons.
ouAo23G7qu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the algorithm simple and well motivated, the paper well written, and the horizon-aware index better aligned with the finite-horizon cumulative-reward objective than the baseline's extrapolation.
ouAo23G7qu.main_concern: The dominance theorem covers only deterministic reward curves of the form min{b_i, a_i n} and one baseline (R-ed-UCB), so the benefit of horizon awareness in general settings is unclear and the worst-case regret matches prior work.

t2dxTYa2z6.one_liner: Systematic study of textual backdoor mechanisms in Mamba, plus TASWB, which boosts trigger-aware state writes and target-class margins.
t2dxTYa2z6.problem: How textual backdoors operate in selective state-space language models is unclear, since trigger information must be written into a recurrent state, preserved through updates, and exposed at the classifier readout.
t2dxTYa2z6.method: The paper compares Mamba and Pythia at two scales on four datasets under BadNL, SynBkd, StyBkd, and BGMAttack, and analyzes mechanisms through the input-dependent time step and component replacement. It then proposes Trigger-Aware State-Write Boosting (TASWB).
t2dxTYa2z6.key_idea: Strengthen trigger-aware writes into the recurrent state and the target-class margin, guided by causal analysis showing the mixer, gate, scan-output, and state-write pathways drive backdoor activation.
t2dxTYa2z6.evidence: Four datasets, Mamba versus Pythia at two model scales, four attack types, and mechanism analysis via time-step diagnostics and component replacement.
t2dxTYa2z6.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative findings, e.g. Mamba has higher clean accuracy at small scale and larger models make non-lexical triggers more reliable).
t2dxTYa2z6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the extensive experimental setup and mechanistic analysis beyond attack success rate (trigger position, pooling, component interventions) on an under-explored problem, with controls across trigger families and scales.
t2dxTYa2z6.main_concern: Experimental rigor: conclusions rest on LoRA fine-tuning, mostly one lexical trigger and small models, a weak Pythia baseline, single seeds without variances, and TASWB is not separated from generic poison-loss reweighting.

aQweuGQ1DT.one_liner: Training-free diffusion feature caching that scores reuse by local error times scheduler step size and calibrated remaining-trajectory sensitivity.
aQweuGQ1DT.problem: Adaptive caching decides reuse from local denoiser-output differences, but the same local difference causes different terminal errors depending on the scheduler step size and the sensitivity of the remaining denoising trajectory.
aQweuGQ1DT.method: TSenCache combines a sample-adaptive local-error estimate with the target scheduler step size and a calibrated sensitivity of the remaining trajectory to estimate the terminal impact of each reuse decision. Keeping step size separate lets sensitivity profiles transfer across sampling settings through noise-level interpolation.
aQweuGQ1DT.key_idea: Weight the local error of each cache reuse by the scheduler step size and a calibrated sensitivity of the rest of the trajectory to estimate terminal error.
aQweuGQ1DT.evidence: Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Wan2.1, and LTX-Video against other caching methods at comparable inference speed.
aQweuGQ1DT.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says higher reconstruction fidelity than the evaluated caching methods at comparable inference speed, without numbers).
aQweuGQ1DT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation well justified (caching should track final-output error, not local error), the paper clearly written, and the reconstruction fidelity good across image and video models.
aQweuGQ1DT.main_concern: The source of the gain and the novelty are unclear: results are close to offline schedulers such as LeMiCa and BudCache, the sensitivity analysis may only reflect earlier-step error propagation, and the method needs a calibration set.

Zfkuo1BRcN.one_liner: Generation-time watermark uses proxy-model gradients to pick tokens whose fine-tuning updates reinforce a private watermark direction.
Zfkuo1BRcN.problem: Existing watermark methods for detecting fine-tuning on teacher-generated data are evaluated on training-related or same-prompt contexts, while owners often do not know which data was used for distillation.
Zfkuo1BRcN.method: GGRW uses a proxy model to identify and sample tokens whose induced fine-tuning updates reinforce a private watermark direction. This enables detection on disjoint held-out contexts used in neither watermark construction nor student fine-tuning.
Zfkuo1BRcN.key_idea: Link generation-time token selection to downstream fine-tuning dynamics by sampling tokens whose proxy-model gradient updates align with a private watermark direction.
Zfkuo1BRcN.evidence: Experiments show detection under dilution attacks and distillation with unknown student architectures, and on disjoint held-out contexts where baselines fail; reviews note Qwen and other students, GSM8K only, and LoRA fine-tuning.
Zfkuo1BRcN.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative: detectable under dilution attacks and distillation, and on held-out contexts where baseline methods fail).
Zfkuo1BRcN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the private probe set and proxy-gradient design, detection on held-out contexts, preserved teacher utility, and improved detectability over antidistillation fingerprinting.
Zfkuo1BRcN.main_concern: Limited evaluation: GSM8K only, LoRA fine-tuning only, no multi-key or watermark-removal tests, a large share of training data must be marked, and the wrong-key significance test is not justified.

0gHEpzGMuS.one_liner: Learns masks that route information through frozen pretrained VLM connections instead of updating weights or adding adapters.
0gHEpzGMuS.problem: Full fine-tuning can disturb pretrained representations through cross-modal gradient interference, while parameter-efficient methods with additive low-rank modules may limit adaptation capacity.
0gHEpzGMuS.method: Mask Fine-Tuning (MFT) learns masks over existing pretrained connections without modifying backbone weights, uncovering subnetworks aligned with downstream objectives. Per reviews, the masks can be merged into the weights with no extra inference overhead.
0gHEpzGMuS.key_idea: Adapt a VLM by learning masks that selectively attenuate frozen pretrained weights, selecting subnetworks rather than adding or updating parameters.
0gHEpzGMuS.evidence: Per reviews, experiments cover four compact language backbones, two vision encoders, six benchmarks, models up to 14B parameters, and five-seed means with layer-wise and masking ablations.
0gHEpzGMuS.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that MFT consistently achieves superior performance to full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning across vision-language benchmarks).
0gHEpzGMuS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, mergeable into weights without inference overhead, and evaluated broadly across backbones, encoders, larger models, and ablations.
0gHEpzGMuS.main_concern: Limited novelty over existing mask-based adaptation (learnable weight masks, KSM, Soft-TransFormers, Bit-Mask Tuning), with missing matched comparisons against them.

ttnaG7TM9A.one_liner: Spiking transformer keeps full features in a memory repository and propagates few query tokens via bidirectional spike-driven cross-attention.
ttnaG7TM9A.problem: Transformer-based spiking neural networks inherit token-intensive processing from vision transformers, which hinders deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
ttnaG7TM9A.method: MiST decouples the feature map into a memory repository and a small set of propagated query tokens. A bidirectional spike-driven cross-attention module (Bi-SDCA) retrieves content into the queries and writes enriched tokens back to the repository, and semantic-guided self-distillation (SGSD) addresses early-training disorder of the repository.
ttnaG7TM9A.key_idea: Process only a few query tokens that read from and write back to a full-feature memory repository via bidirectional spike-driven cross-attention.
ttnaG7TM9A.evidence: Per reviews, evaluation spans multiple datasets and architectures with FLOPs and GPU throughput; the results are cut off in the abstract text provided.
ttnaG7TM9A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the memory retrieval and update design as well motivated, preserving information under aggressive token compression, with competitive accuracy and improved throughput across datasets and architectures.
ttnaG7TM9A.main_concern: Efficiency and novelty are unclear: full keys and values are kept with cross-attention added to every block and no latency breakdown, and sparse-query retrieval resembles ANN token pruning and Perceiver-style designs.

fTa3IlsEFG.one_liner: Extracts refusal circuits in base LLMs by mask optimization, traces their evolution through alignment, and confines safety updates to them.
fTa3IlsEFG.problem: Safety interpretability has focused on representations, heads, or neurons after alignment, overlooking safety mechanisms in pretrained-only models and their evolution across alignment checkpoints.
fTa3IlsEFG.method: SafeEvo applies an optimization-based extraction to find weak refusal circuits in base LLMs, traces how they change across alignment checkpoints, and introduces Safety Circuit Alignment (SCA), which confines safety updates to the refusal circuits.
fTa3IlsEFG.key_idea: Learn a mask that makes a sparse subnetwork refuse harmful inputs, then restrict alignment updates to that circuit to avoid disturbing utility-related parameters.
fTa3IlsEFG.evidence: Causal ablation of the circuits eliminates base-model refusal; experiments across three LLMs and two alignment algorithms compare SCA against vanilla alignment.
fTa3IlsEFG.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract lists three advantages of SCA, starting with stronger alignment, but the text is cut off before any numbers).
fTa3IlsEFG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the circuit-based causal analysis of the alignment tax is a timely, clearly written contribution, with strong sufficiency and necessity evidence that refusal circuits exist in base models.
fTa3IlsEFG.main_concern: Overlap with prior work, notably the authors' own SafeSeek and the Superficial Safety Alignment Hypothesis paper (same circuit extraction and circuit-confined tuning), plus a simple technique and somewhat dated evaluated models.

6EnlHthjhS.one_liner: RCF scores pseudo-label reliability on predictive and semantic dimensions with a two-component Gaussian mixture for continual semi-supervised learning.
6EnlHthjhS.problem: Confidence-based pseudo-label selection in non-revisitable continual semi-supervised learning keeps overconfident but semantically inconsistent labels whose errors persist after the expert is frozen.
6EnlHthjhS.method: Decomposes pseudo-label reliability into predictive and semantic dimensions, fits a two-component GMM by EM over the reliability representations to get a distribution-relative score, and selects pseudo-labels adaptively under a target mean reliability, with temporal posterior smoothing and an asymmetric EMA threshold update.
6EnlHthjhS.key_idea: Fit a 2D Gaussian mixture over prediction-stability and semantic-agreement features to get a per-task relative reliability score that sets the pseudo-label selection threshold.
6EnlHthjhS.evidence: Reviews cite continual semi-supervised experiments on ImageNet-R and ImageNet-A at low label ratios, a CL-LoRA experiment, and ablations.
6EnlHthjhS.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a review cites ImageNet-R average incremental accuracy of 34.30% versus 21.59% for CoVar and ImageNet-A of 21.32% versus 13.40% with 1% labels.
6EnlHthjhS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining prediction stability with semantic (prototype) agreement is a reasonable improvement over confidence-only selection, with the largest gains in low-label ImageNet-R and ImageNet-A settings.
6EnlHthjhS.main_concern: The theoretical support is shaky (Proposition B.3 relies on a gradient inequality that does not generally hold and GMM posteriors are treated as correctness probabilities), and the extra compute and many hyperparameters lack cost and sensitivity analysis.

AQHvt9xCEK.one_liner: BEE-GPI solves Good Policy Identification in episodic RL, with a log(1/delta) coefficient independent of state and action space sizes.
AQHvt9xCEK.problem: Pure exploration in episodic RL targets Best Policy Identification, but when a good-enough policy suffices, a reward-threshold objective (Good Policy Identification) is under-explored.
AQHvt9xCEK.method: Proposes BEE-GPI for fixed-confidence GPI: output a policy with expected episode reward at least mu0 if one exists, or None otherwise, correct with probability at least 1-delta. Derives sample-complexity upper bounds for positive and negative instances and lower bounds showing near-optimality.
AQHvt9xCEK.key_idea: Test achievability of a reward threshold mu0 with fixed-confidence guarantees instead of searching for the optimal policy.
AQHvt9xCEK.evidence: Theoretical upper bounds for positive and negative instances and lower bounds; reviews note experiments on tabular environments against BPI algorithms adapted to GPI.
AQHvt9xCEK.claimed_gains: For positive instances the coefficient of log 1/delta in the upper bound is O(H^2/(V*-mu0)^2), with no other dependence on action and state space sizes.
AQHvt9xCEK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and practically relevant, and that the finite-sample upper and lower bound analysis is sound.
AQHvt9xCEK.main_concern: Technical novelty over the 1-identification work of Li and Cheung (2025) is not fully elaborated, and the BPI comparison (threshold mu0 versus relative tolerance epsilon), the lack of a general lower bound, and the limited experiments weaken the case.

kEbfAnKEbf.one_liner: PXDepth pairs a large-patch ViT for global context with a Pixel-Space Depth Predictor of Context-Modulated Pixel Transformer blocks.
kEbfAnKEbf.problem: Large-patch ViT encoders with convolutional decoders lose fine structure because coarse tokenization weakens pixel-level cues and convolutional decoding struggles with both low- and high-frequency regions.
kEbfAnKEbf.method: A large-patch ViT captures global scene context while a Pixel-Space Depth Predictor built from Context-Modulated Pixel Transformer blocks learns pixel-space features throughout depth estimation, in a single forward pass without iterative sampling.
kEbfAnKEbf.key_idea: Decouple global context modeling (large-patch ViT) from pixel-space feature learning (context-modulated pixel transformer blocks) in the depth predictor.
kEbfAnKEbf.evidence: Zero-shot benchmarks with many baselines and an ablation against a conv decoder; reviews note training on synthetic data starting from MoGe-2.
kEbfAnKEbf.claimed_gains: Reports substantially improved local geometric fidelity with competitive global depth accuracy and lower inference latency than multi-step generative methods, with no numbers stated.
kEbfAnKEbf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, targets a relevant fine-structure problem, and that the pixel-space transformer block improves local geometric fidelity at moderate latency cost.
kEbfAnKEbf.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are not controlled: PXDepth trains on synthetic data from MoGe-2 with its own loss, so the share of gain due to architecture is unclear, and structure preservation is measured only by boundary metrics.

Jx6ZFrztDl.one_liner: Weight-gradient interaction scores identify influential language-model parameters and probe collapse from modifying tiny parameter subsets.
Jx6ZFrztDl.problem: Parameter importance estimated from weights or gradients alone can miss parameters that disproportionately influence language-model behavior.
Jx6ZFrztDl.method: WAG combines model weights with first-order gradient information to score parameter importance and uses masking studies to examine failure modes. Applications include MoE expert allocation, targeted unlearning, mixed-precision quantization, and knowledge-editing layer selection.
Jx6ZFrztDl.key_idea: Rank parameters by their weight-gradient interaction and test how modifying selected subsets changes model behavior.
Jx6ZFrztDl.evidence: Masking experiments compare WAG with weight-only and gradient-only selection across models, alongside evaluations in multiple parameter-control applications.
Jx6ZFrztDl.claimed_gains: Modifying parameters totaling ≤ 0.5 parts per million or 0.00005% of model size causes dramatic performance degradation.
Jx6ZFrztDl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the concise importance score and empirical investigation of influential parameters useful.
Jx6ZFrztDl.main_concern: Multiple reviewers note that WAG is mathematically similar to established first-order Taylor saliency measures, limiting its methodological contribution.

9tcdEvyueh.one_liner: Sensor-coordinate graph-Matérn covariance replaces isotropic flow-matching noise with spatially coherent EEG source patterns.
9tcdEvyueh.problem: EEG generators learn spatial correlations from scratch even though fixed sensor geometry already provides relevant structure.
9tcdEvyueh.method: The method builds a nearest-neighbor graph from electrode coordinates and applies a graph-Matérn function to its Laplacian to define source covariance. It changes neither the drift network nor coupling and adds no learned parameters.
9tcdEvyueh.key_idea: Derive flow-matching source covariance from a graph-Matérn function of the sensor-coordinate graph Laplacian.
9tcdEvyueh.evidence: Experiments cover eight EEG datasets and four flow-matching methods, with graph-structure ablations and downstream evaluation on Mumtaz-MDD.
9tcdEvyueh.claimed_gains: PSD-KL falls by 11% to 25% in geometric mean over datasets depending on the method, reaching up to 40% on PhysioNet-MI.
9tcdEvyueh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the physically motivated source prior that adds spatial structure without learned parameters or changes to the flow-matching objective.
9tcdEvyueh.main_concern: Reviewers repeatedly request broader comparisons with graph-aware generators and existing brain-signal generation methods.

3fnXyA7GC3.one_liner: An LLM agent searches executable molecular-descriptor pipelines composed from formation, extraction, and compression operators.
3fnXyA7GC3.problem: Designing task-specific 3D molecular descriptors requires substantial chemical expertise and remains difficult to automate.
3fnXyA7GC3.method: Pangaea defines a Unified Construction Space of executable descriptor pipelines over chemically annotated molecular point clouds. An Incumbent Revision Agent iteratively refines the best pipeline using evaluation history, design-space semantics, and chemical priors.
3fnXyA7GC3.key_idea: Compose descriptor pipelines from stage-wise operators and use an LLM agent to revise the incumbent using predictive evaluation history.
3fnXyA7GC3.evidence: Data-limited QM9 experiments compare descriptor methods, four deep-learning baselines, alternative search strategies, and multiple target properties.
3fnXyA7GC3.claimed_gains: Pangaea reports a 24% relative reduction in test MAE and outperforms four deep-learning baselines.
3fnXyA7GC3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Formation, Extraction, and Compression decomposition provides a useful structured space for automated descriptor design.
3fnXyA7GC3.main_concern: Reviewers question baseline strength and configuration choices, which make it difficult to attribute the reported advantage to descriptor search.

kA82qMg9mc.one_liner: Independent plugin mutation and library-based recomposition recursively improve language-model agent harnesses.
kA82qMg9mc.problem: Searching over complete agent harness programs makes individual mechanisms difficult to isolate and reuse.
kA82qMg9mc.method: PluginRSI represents a harness as a composition of atomized plugins, improves plugins independently, and stores them in a shared library. Each iteration recombines library components into new harnesses, enabling reuse across optimization runs and solver models.
kA82qMg9mc.key_idea: Alternate independent plugin improvements with harness recomposition using an accumulating shared plugin library.
kA82qMg9mc.evidence: Experiments cover software engineering, command-line interaction, and question answering, with solver-model transfer, plugin reuse, and optimization ablations.
kA82qMg9mc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of plugin optimization from harness recomposition intuitive and clearly presented.
kA82qMg9mc.main_concern: Reported performance gaps lack repeated runs and uncertainty estimates, leaving their statistical reliability unclear.

2GPDxcF2sh.one_liner: Context reversals, candidate swaps, and evidence-retention tests probe long-context safety reward modeling.
2GPDxcF2sh.problem: Safety reward models may rely on isolated request priors instead of tracking permissions and constraints across long interactions.
2GPDxcF2sh.method: ContextFlip evaluates contextual preference reversal, candidate-order invariance, and situational evidence retention. The paper also studies CONTEXTRM, whose updater uses an LLM-based natural-language summary to maintain situational memory.
2GPDxcF2sh.key_idea: Vary contextual permissions and candidate order while testing whether safety preferences retain the relevant situational evidence.
2GPDxcF2sh.evidence: Evaluation compares existing safety reward models on ContextFlip, including update and revocation settings, long irrelevant histories, and external DynaBench trajectories.
2GPDxcF2sh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating whether safety judgments track contextual changes in permissions and constraints during long conversations.
2GPDxcF2sh.main_concern: Reviewers question the methodological contribution beyond prior context-aware preference modeling and existing summary-based memory techniques.

94s0csPQ5Q.one_liner: Reference-image editing and motion-controlled reconstruction combine with causal distillation for streaming character-video editing.
94s0csPQ5Q.problem: Existing video editors can alter facial expressions and require offline multi-step inference unsuitable for live interaction.
94s0csPQ5Q.method: EditaLive adapts Wan-Animate using reference-frame editing and video reconstruction on CharEdit-50K, then converts bidirectional generation to causal streaming. Aligned self-rollout distillation produces a two-step sampler with fixed RoPE, Align Forcing, and first-frame-preserving sparse attention.
94s0csPQ5Q.key_idea: Decouple appearance edits from motion, then distill causal rollouts with aligned positions and first-frame-preserving attention.
94s0csPQ5Q.evidence: Experiments compare bidirectional and streaming editors and include long-video ablations measuring editing quality, expression preservation, and appearance stability.
94s0csPQ5Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value appearance-motion decoupling and reconstruction supervision for preserving expressions during character editing.
94s0csPQ5Q.main_concern: The end-to-end real-time claim lacks a complete pipeline latency measurement that accounts for preprocessing, buffering, and evaluation-resolution differences.

HdZbtSStup.one_liner: Suppressing context heads and contrasting sparse autoencoder features detects conflicts between retrieved context and parametric knowledge.
HdZbtSStup.problem: Retrieval-augmented language models can produce hallucinations when parametric knowledge outweighs supplied context.
HdZbtSStup.method: RAGap identifies context heads through differentiable masking and suppresses them within the residual stream. It contrasts paired sparse autoencoder features to detect knowledge-context divergence.
HdZbtSStup.key_idea: Contrast sparse autoencoder features before and after suppressing context heads within the residual stream.
HdZbtSStup.evidence: Evaluations span multiple model families and RAG benchmarks, with comparisons against existing detectors and ablations of gap features and head masking.
HdZbtSStup.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong detection results and an intuitive intervention that reduces the cost of constructing context contrasts.
HdZbtSStup.main_concern: Reviewers question whether single-layer head suppression actually isolates parametric knowledge and whether the gap signal explains the gains.

s1LKsHTyUa.one_liner: Matched checkpoint probing, steering, and clamping compare emotional representations with reply changes across post-training stages.
s1LKsHTyUa.problem: Existing studies do not jointly track whether post-training changes emotional representations or responses to the same emotions.
s1LKsHTyUa.method: The study evaluates matched inputs across base, supervised fine-tuning, DPO, and available reinforcement-learning checkpoints of four models. It combines affect probes, reply judgments, phrase counts, and interventions on a fixed valence direction.
s1LKsHTyUa.key_idea: Track frozen cross-stage affect probes and reply behavior on matched inputs while steering and clamping a fixed valence direction.
s1LKsHTyUa.evidence: Four model trajectories are evaluated with multiple probe formulations, cross-stage transfer, behavioral judges, and valence-direction interventions.
s1LKsHTyUa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled comparisons across consecutive checkpoints and the extensive probing checks on matched stimuli.
s1LKsHTyUa.main_concern: Reviewers agree that stable decodability and underspecified clamping do not establish that response-policy changes occur without changes in affect representations.

mhdCRhvKOV.one_liner: Predicting all Semantic ID token probabilities in one bidirectional Transformer pass with dual-level contrastive losses enables single-step generative recommendation.
mhdCRhvKOV.problem: Autoregressive and iterative non-autoregressive Semantic ID recommenders require multiple neural forward passes per item, creating high latency in serving environments.
mhdCRhvKOV.method: Framing discrete Semantic ID generation through average probability velocity, SPRINT uses a bidirectional Transformer to predict marginal generation probabilities for all SID tokens in a single forward pass. A dual-level contrastive objective contrasting target and negative SIDs at both token and whole-item levels restores cross-position coherence.
mhdCRhvKOV.key_idea: Predict marginal probabilities for all Semantic ID positions in one bidirectional Transformer pass and enforce multi-token coherence via token-level and item-level contrastive objectives.
mhdCRhvKOV.evidence: Supported by a proof linking average probability velocity to average token probabilities and full-catalog evaluations across eight recommendation datasets over five random seeds.
mhdCRhvKOV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that single-pass Semantic ID prediction targets a real latency bottleneck and achieves consistent full-catalog accuracy gains across eight datasets backed by dual-level contrastive ablations.
mhdCRhvKOV.main_concern: All three reviewers identify a disconnect between the average-probability-velocity derivation and the actual contrastive/SID-matching objective, noting that under standard masking paths the averaged posterior collapses to ordinary one-step prediction.

D3o11BIhap.one_liner: BasinMark selects crystals by keyed structural fingerprints and audits distinct fingerprint classes after physical processing.
D3o11BIhap.problem: Relaxation erases coordinate watermarks, unstable structural bins change labels, and duplicate crystals inflate provenance false positives.
D3o11BIhap.method: BasinMark removes unstable cell-shape fingerprint bins and uses energy-budgeted selection across interchangeable output slots. Class-deduplicated binomial calibration audits deposited structures at the level of distinct fingerprints to control false positives.
D3o11BIhap.key_idea: Watermark candidate selection using stable keyed fingerprints, then calibrate detection on distinct classes rather than duplicated structures.
D3o11BIhap.evidence: The abstract reports MatterGen and CrystalFormer collections tested after independent re-relaxation, standardization, CIF deposition, bounded strain, and a changed relaxation model.
D3o11BIhap.claimed_gains: Releasing 32 structures from 256 candidates detects 499/500 MatterGen and 476/500 CrystalFormer collections at 11.9 and 37.3 meV/atom above the cheapest unmarked release, with 496/500 and 497/500 held-out detections both after bounded strain and after changing the relaxation model.
D3o11BIhap.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value physically processed crystal provenance and the empirical finding that removing cell-shape features improves fingerprint stability.
D3o11BIhap.main_concern: Reviewers say separate fingerprint-survival and detection studies do not adequately validate the complete generation, selection, processing, and deposition pipeline.

x2qt73ys2A.one_liner: Holding training information fixed separates evidence changes from Bayesian coherence failures in tabular foundation-model consistency tests.
x2qt73ys2A.problem: Consistency tests can compare predictions conditioned on different training columns and mistake changed evidence for incoherence.
x2qt73ys2A.method: The paper bounds discrepancies through posterior updates and constructs exact Bayesian counterexamples to marginalization and factorization tests. It then holds training information fixed in LimiX-2 queries and compares autoregressive mixtures with independent products using joint log loss.
x2qt73ys2A.key_idea: Fix the observed training information before comparing marginal and autoregressive predictions so evidence updates cannot masquerade as inconsistency.
x2qt73ys2A.evidence: Tests span 60 exact Bayesian tasks, LimiX-2 on six datasets and three splits, and TabICLv2 and TabPFNv2 on ten classification datasets.
x2qt73ys2A.claimed_gains: Holding information fixed reduces mean LimiX-2 marginalization and factorization gaps by 51.1% and 51.9%, respectively, with both decreasing in every split.
x2qt73ys2A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a relevant correction to consistency-test interpretation supported by Bayesian counterexamples and theoretical reasoning.
x2qt73ys2A.main_concern: Reviewers say the experiments leave the actual coherence of tabular foundation models under fixed information insufficiently resolved.

hSM0RqHSpo.one_liner: BITS standardizes irregular time-series forecasting comparisons across datasets, model families, irregularity descriptors, and multiple metric types.
hSM0RqHSpo.problem: Inconsistent protocols, narrow dataset coverage, and predominantly error-based metrics hinder fair comparison of irregular time-series forecasters.
hSM0RqHSpo.method: BITS unifies preprocessing, model integration, evaluation, and reporting for regular, irregular, and foundation forecasting models. It characterizes missingness, sampling irregularity, and skewness while reporting both error-based and non-error-based metrics.
hSM0RqHSpo.key_idea: Compare forecasting families through a common pipeline while explicitly describing dataset irregularity and evaluating multiple notions of forecast quality.
hSM0RqHSpo.evidence: The benchmark covers eleven datasets from nine domains, with reviews reporting 26 models and comparisons of model rankings across metrics and irregularity characteristics.
hSM0RqHSpo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad dataset and model coverage and reusable infrastructure for more consistent forecasting evaluation.
hSM0RqHSpo.main_concern: Reviewers find benchmark fairness difficult to audit because tuning budgets, selection rules, and protocol choices are insufficiently documented.

bqtNrg9OWy.one_liner: DToP combines low-rank token-margin sensitivities with diagonal Fisher memory to constrain cumulative parameter drift during continual reasoning.
bqtNrg9OWy.problem: Replay-free continual reinforcement learning must preserve prior reasoning behavior using compact statistics instead of stored prompts or trajectories.
bqtNrg9OWy.method: DToP selects late-settling token states and compresses sampled-token versus alternative margin gradients into a low-rank second-moment memory, while other states supply diagonal policy Fisher information. Scale-normalized memories define a joint parameter-space trust region that constrains cumulative movement during later tasks.
bqtNrg9OWy.key_idea: Protect cumulative parameter displacement using a sensitivity metric combining low-rank margin gradients from late-settling states and diagonal policy Fisher information.
bqtNrg9OWy.evidence: Reviews describe six-task experiments with three seeds, ten-task experiments with one seed, canonical and reverse task orders, component controls, and theoretical trust-region analysis.
bqtNrg9OWy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value replay-free sensitivity memories and constraining accumulated drift rather than only individual optimizer steps.
bqtNrg9OWy.main_concern: Reviewers identify per-state margin-gradient normalization in the supplied code that contradicts the manuscript and changes the stored sensitivity metric.

QjeqBj7ISi.one_liner: LION learns a shared spatial feature ranking through distance-weighted bilinear aggregation with a compact global influence vector.
QjeqBj7ISi.problem: Predictive accuracy and bag-averaged permutation importance can misrepresent shared feature influence when neighborhood size and feature variation co-vary.
QjeqBj7ISi.method: LION combines a learnable distance kernel, feature-preserving normalization, and a global influence vector through bilinear aggregation. The ranking is an explicit model parameter, with consistent recovery of strict feature comparisons under correct specification and identification conditions.
QjeqBj7ISi.key_idea: Represent the shared influence ranking directly as coefficients in a distance-aware bilinear model rather than inferring it from perturbation sensitivity.
QjeqBj7ISi.evidence: Theory shows permutation-importance reversals and ranking consistency, while seven ranking benchmarks span synthetic data and real tissue geometry.
QjeqBj7ISi.claimed_gains: LION leads or ties distance-weighted logistic regression in mean Spearman on every benchmark, with gains up to 0.22 and competitive prediction using 12 to 64 parameters against thousands for deep baselines.
QjeqBj7ISi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the compact model's competitive predictions and the experimental ablations supporting its interpretation target.
QjeqBj7ISi.main_concern: Reviewers find the central ranking advantage insufficiently established beyond simple or favorably specified benchmarks and carefully matched alternatives.

dSWDicnB8n.one_liner: RepLinUCB combines replicable ridge estimation with determinant-triggered optimistic exploration without discretizing the action space.
dSWDicnB8n.problem: Existing replicable linear-bandit algorithms discretize large action spaces and have suboptimal dimension and replicability dependence.
dSWDicnB8n.method: RepRidge constructs a replicable ridge estimator with an inflated self-normalized confidence bound, and RepLinUCB combines it with determinant-triggered batching. Avoiding action discretization permits shared time-varying action sets, with an extension through a replicable penalized GLM estimator.
dSWDicnB8n.key_idea: Round estimates in confidence-ellipsoid geometry and use them in batched optimistic exploration to synchronize action sequences across independent reward realizations.
dSWDicnB8n.evidence: The paper derives confidence and regret bounds, extends the construction to generalized linear bandits, and includes low-dimensional, low-noise experiments described in reviews.
dSWDicnB8n.claimed_gains: RepLinUCB achieves regret \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(d^3\sqrt{T}/\rho), improving prior guarantees by a factor of d/ρ with optimal dependence on ρ for large action sets.
dSWDicnB8n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the replicable estimator and improved guarantees that support continuous and time-varying action sets.
dSWDicnB8n.main_concern: Reviewers request clearer positioning against existing replicable ridge estimators, particularly Eaton et al.'s randomized-rounding construction.

e8sL4CCesk.one_liner: AutoRef uses a coding agent to rewrite multi-reference image-generation workflows while keeping reasoning and generation models frozen.
e8sL4CCesk.problem: Hand-designed multi-reference generation workflows vary widely in quality and struggle with subject omission, duplication, and unnatural composition.
e8sL4CCesk.method: AutoRef iteratively rewrites executable workflow code that controls reference interpretation, generation, diagnosis, and final selection. It separates tasks that supply proposal feedback from tasks used to select candidate workflows.
e8sL4CCesk.key_idea: Search over executable generation workflows with a coding agent, using separate feedback and selection tasks around frozen models.
e8sL4CCesk.evidence: Reviews describe MultiBanana evaluation, component ablations, human preferences, and transfer to unseen benchmarks and another generator.
e8sL4CCesk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize practical multi-reference generation gains from inspectable workflow components, supported by ablations and transfer tests.
e8sL4CCesk.main_concern: Reviewers find the optimizer's incremental contribution insufficiently isolated from established code evolution, task splitting, and beam-parent selection.

iNMwRWbhJT.one_liner: Offline distillation of local and global LLM knowledge feeds lightweight experts selected by a node-wise graph router.
iNMwRWbhJT.problem: GNN–LLM knowledge mismatch complicates fusion, while existing combinations can add substantial computation for limited gains.
