iNMwRWbhJT.method: DeKoR separates LLM knowledge into local and global views and distills them offline into lightweight experts. An adaptive router chooses each node's reliance on those experts, removing LLM inference at deployment.
iNMwRWbhJT.key_idea: Distill local and global LLM knowledge into separate lightweight experts and route their contributions adaptively for each graph node.
iNMwRWbhJT.evidence: Experiments evaluate node and subgraph classification across multiple benchmarks and GNN/LLM backbones, including ablations and efficiency comparisons.
iNMwRWbhJT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the practical inference savings from removing the LLM and the method's modular design.
iNMwRWbhJT.main_concern: Reviewers question evaluation fairness because supervision, split reporting, baseline aggregation, and omitted preprocessing costs complicate comparisons.

i6WMPcoUB4.one_liner: Shared latent brain states and ROI-conditioned expert routing reconstruct regional fMRI signals from EEG.
i6WMPcoUB4.problem: EEG-to-fMRI mapping must account for delayed neurovascular responses and regional variation without conflating shared dynamics with regional decoding.
i6WMPcoUB4.method: E2fMoE proposes a state-space mixer for slowly evolving EEG representations, followed by ROI queries routing information through shared and specialized experts. Residual prediction and low-rank connectivity-aware calibration refine reconstruction.
i6WMPcoUB4.key_idea: Infer shared latent states from EEG, then use ROI queries to route regional decoding through shared and specialized experts.
i6WMPcoUB4.evidence: Experiments span four simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets, including held-out subjects, temporal reconstruction, functional-connectivity metrics, and component ablations.
i6WMPcoUB4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the shared-state/regional-decoding design and evaluation across datasets with component ablations.
i6WMPcoUB4.main_concern: Reviewers report that the released mixer operates across pooled scale vectors rather than implementing the described recurrent temporal state updates.

GQSCDLXXTp.one_liner: Teachers continue fresh student-generated prefixes, and masked cross-entropy trains students only on those continuations.
GQSCDLXXTp.problem: Offline distillation suffers sequential distribution shift, while token-level on-policy supervision can fragment guidance and require teacher probabilities.
GQSCDLXXTp.method: OSD repeatedly samples a prefix from the current student and obtains an autoregressive teacher continuation. It applies cross-entropy only to teacher-generated tokens and uses an asynchronous implementation to reduce training time.
GQSCDLXXTp.key_idea: Refresh prefixes using the evolving student, let the teacher continue them, and supervise only the continuation tokens.
GQSCDLXXTp.evidence: Evaluations cover hard reasoning and agentic tasks, including ScienceWorld, TextCraft, and ALFWorld, with budget comparisons against offline SFT and OPD.
GQSCDLXXTp.claimed_gains: The abstract reports a 23.8% training-time reduction from asynchronous execution and a 13% ScienceWorld improvement over same-teacher offline SFT using GPT-5.4-mini text.
GQSCDLXXTp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the simple text-only continuation objective and its applicability to black-box teachers.
GQSCDLXXTp.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate evolving student prefixes from fresh teacher data and differing teacher or computational budgets.

AXg2IrbqKN.one_liner: Expert-commentary alignment trains surgical-video representations to generate video-specific workflows without commentary at inference.
AXg2IrbqKN.problem: Fixed surgical workflow classes inadequately represent procedural changes driven by patient variability and intraoperative circumstances.
AXg2IrbqKN.method: DySurg supplies dynamic workflow annotations for long surgical videos. The proposed framework aligns visual embeddings with titles and expert commentary through top-down reasoning sequences, then generates workflows from video frames alone.
AXg2IrbqKN.key_idea: Align surgical-video embeddings with title and expert-commentary semantics during training, then generate workflow descriptions from visual inputs.
AXg2IrbqKN.evidence: Evaluations use DySurg, containing over 100 hours across 7 surgical categories, with reviews discussing keystep localization and description metrics.
AXg2IrbqKN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the dataset and move beyond fixed workflow ontologies as useful contributions.
AXg2IrbqKN.main_concern: The evaluation does not adequately establish adaptive surgical reasoning, and segment-matching criteria leave the measured capability unclear.

I8H3JbqfDh.one_liner: Physical state-transition supervision trains vision-language-action models using structured variables, visual motion, and semantic differences.
I8H3JbqfDh.problem: Direct observation-to-action learning can overfit demonstrations without explicitly learning intermediate physical changes.
I8H3JbqfDh.method: VLA-Δ constructs pretraining data with task-relevant semantic and visual-motion transition annotations. Auxiliary supervision teaches physical changes while inference generates actions directly from current observations without added overhead.
I8H3JbqfDh.key_idea: Supervise intermediate representations with current-to-future physical changes through structured transition targets, optical flow, and difference descriptions.
I8H3JbqfDh.evidence: Experiments evaluate LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-robot tasks, with reviews noting an action-only pretraining control.
I8H3JbqfDh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the motivation for explicit transition supervision and evaluation beyond a single benchmark.
I8H3JbqfDh.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient quantitative evidence for transition-label accuracy and the physical information encoded by learned representations.

TVR4MGvets.one_liner: Scene-conditioned probe lifecycles route sparse-query dynamics for camera-only occupancy forecasting without future ego trajectories.
TVR4MGvets.problem: Trajectory-conditioned occupancy forecasting depends on future ego inputs that can introduce oracle dependence or upstream prediction errors.
TVR4MGvets.method: SCOPE-Occ predicts temporal support governing each sparse probe's emergence, persistence, and termination. These lifecycle signals route persistent and emerging probes through distinct dynamics updates and gate contributions to future occupancy decoding.
TVR4MGvets.key_idea: Predict temporal support for sparse probes and use lifecycle signals to route dynamics updates and gate occupancy contributions.
TVR4MGvets.evidence: Experiments on Occ3D-nuScenes compare trajectory-free baselines using ResNet-50 and DINOv3-pretrained ConvNeXt-Base, with lifecycle and temporal-support ablations.
TVR4MGvets.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 21.02 average mIoU and 42.99 average IoU with ResNet-50, and 21.68 mIoU with the ConvNeXt-Base variant.
TVR4MGvets.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the coherent lifecycle mechanism and reported gains under the trajectory-free protocol.
TVR4MGvets.main_concern: Reviewers question the driving and world-model significance of unconditional occupancy prediction without action-conditioned evaluation.

aHo9LkOkQo.one_liner: Scale-dependent low-quality suffix control adapts Infinity's visual autoregression to input-constrained blind face restoration.
aHo9LkOkQo.problem: Generative face restoration must balance realistic detail with fidelity to reliable evidence in degraded inputs.
aHo9LkOkQo.method: InfinityFace combines restored prefixes with corrected unresolved low-quality features through a scale-dependent suffix controller. A separate conditioning path injects low-quality visual memory and text through multimodal cross-attention.
aHo9LkOkQo.key_idea: Condition next-scale autoregressive restoration on a corrected low-quality suffix and text–image memory while retaining the restored prefix.
aHo9LkOkQo.evidence: Experiments cover synthetic and real-world face-restoration benchmarks, with reviews discussing CelebA-Test, LFW, Wider, oracle analyses, and user preferences.
aHo9LkOkQo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the scale-dependent conditioning rationale and reported no-reference perceptual quality.
aHo9LkOkQo.main_concern: The ablations and baseline controls do not adequately isolate the proposed conditioning design's contribution.

4IyvTJEMLJ.one_liner: Trains few-step conditional posterior samplers for test-time diffusion steering via distribution matching distillation instead of trajectory consistency.
4IyvTJEMLJ.problem: Test-time reward steering of diffusion and flow models requires posterior sampling from intermediate noisy states, where exact ODE/SDE rollouts are too slow and trajectory-distilled stochastic flow maps suffer from training instability.
4IyvTJEMLJ.method: MetaDMD trains a few-step conditional posterior sampler by matching the terminal posterior distribution rather than distilling exact integration trajectories, eliminating consistency losses, Jacobian-vector products, and pretrained flow-map initialization.
4IyvTJEMLJ.key_idea: Applies distribution matching distillation to the conditional transition kernel to learn a few-step posterior sampler without trajectory consistency objectives.
4IyvTJEMLJ.evidence: Evaluated on class-conditional ImageNet with SiT-XL/2 and text-to-image steering on SD3.5-M across DrawBench and GenEval with multiple reward functions.
4IyvTJEMLJ.claimed_gains: Converges with 2x fewer training GPU-hours than stochastic flow maps on SD3.5-M while outperforming them across various rewards on DrawBench, GenEval, and class-conditional ImageNet with SiT-XL/2.
4IyvTJEMLJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that observing test-time steering only requires matching the posterior distribution rather than the integration trajectory leads to a simple, stable, and scalable extension of distribution matching distillation to large text-to-image models.
4IyvTJEMLJ.main_concern: Reviewers view the method as a straightforward combination of DMD and GLASS conditional flows, question the fairness of baseline training comparisons against Meta Flow Maps, and ask for direct evaluation of posterior sampling fidelity.

fRIys2GjMw.one_liner: Benchmarks trustworthiness in personalized MLLM assistants across varying personal-evidence sufficiency and adds a two-layer pre/post calibration safeguard.
fRIys2GjMw.problem: Personalized MLLM assistants often fabricate a false sense of user familiarity by giving overly specific or unqualified generic recommendations when user-specific evidence in the interaction history is partial or missing.
fRIys2GjMw.method: PersonaTrust benchmarks personalized MLLM trustworthiness across four evidence-dependency question categories under Full, Partial, and None personal-evidence masking settings. The authors also introduce PR-Calibrator, a plug-and-play module that applies pre-generation question routing and post-generation history verification safeguards around existing personalization pipelines.
fRIys2GjMw.key_idea: Evaluates personalized MLLM responses under controlled masking of required personal-evidence atoms and wraps assistants in pre-query classification and post-response evidence verification safeguards.
fRIys2GjMw.evidence: Evaluates frontier MLLMs and personalization methods across four question categories (PIQ, EPQ, GPQ, NQ) under Full, Partial, and None evidence settings.
fRIys2GjMw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the benchmark design for tying personalized questions to specific evidence atoms and testing models under Full, Partial, and None evidence availability across four clear question categories.
fRIys2GjMw.main_concern: Reviewers note that PR-Calibrator is a straightforward prompting pipeline lacking comparisons against self-verification baselines and incurring extra latency, while very low accuracy even in the Full-evidence setting complicates distinguishing trustworthiness failures from poor base retrieval.

i39yus6gSZ.one_liner: Uses an ensemble of open-source LLMs to dynamically annotate words in context along a neuroscience-informed interpretable semantic feature space.
i39yus6gSZ.problem: Static interpretable semantic feature norms fail to capture context-dependent meaning shifts during naturalistic language comprehension in the human brain.
i39yus6gSZ.method: SCRIBE prompts an ensemble of open-source LLMs to dynamically score words within arbitrary textual contexts across a cognitively and neuroscientifically grounded semantic feature space, producing interpretable word-level contextual representations for brain encoding models.
i39yus6gSZ.key_idea: Generates interpretable context-sensitive word representations by using an LLM ensemble to dynamically rate words in context along brain-grounded semantic dimensions.
i39yus6gSZ.evidence: Evaluated against human behavioral ratings (500 participants), controlled synthetic contexts, and fMRI brain activity during naturalistic story listening using per-participant encoding models and variance partitioning against syntactic and static lexical embeddings.
i39yus6gSZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clarity of the paper, the interpretability of grounding contextual representations in a brain-based concept space, and the behavioral validation with a 500-participant human rating dataset.
i39yus6gSZ.main_concern: Reviewers note missing controls for low-level stimulus confounds (such as word rate and audio envelope), weak or mismatched LLM embedding baselines, and lack of ablations separating the brain-grounded feature space from the LLM ensemble.

vkShg0JBSw.one_liner: Benchmarks audio-language models on long-form and multi-audio understanding, cross-audio relational reasoning, and goal-conditioned decision making.
vkShg0JBSw.problem: Existing audio-language benchmarks fragment evaluation and underexplore fine-grained paralinguistic analysis, long-range dependencies, multi-recording comparison, and goal-conditioned decisions over long audio inputs.
vkShg0JBSw.method: LAMAR-Bench organizes 1,597 questions across 10 tasks into three capability families—fine-grained understanding, cross-audio relation reasoning, and decisions under goals and constraints—built from shared audio facts with up to 19 audio clips and 59.9 minutes of audio per question.
vkShg0JBSw.key_idea: Constructs 10 long-form and multi-audio tasks from shared traceable audio facts to jointly evaluate fine-grained perception, cross-audio comparison, and goal-conditioned decisions.
vkShg0JBSw.evidence: Evaluates 14 audio-language and omni-modal systems across 1,597 questions (up to 19 clips and 59.9 minutes per question), with paired sensitivity analyses over answer format, clip order, and goal shifts.
vkShg0JBSw.claimed_gains: Across 14 evaluated audio-language and omni-modal systems, the best paralinguistic-analysis and acoustic-localization accuracies reach 51.09% and 54.38%, respectively.
vkShg0JBSw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the 10-task capability taxonomy spanning fine-grained perception, multi-audio comparison, and goal-conditioned decisions over long recordings addresses a meaningful gap in audio-language evaluation.
vkShg0JBSw.main_concern: Reviewers point out insufficient details on automated annotation validation, subjective label agreement, and human baseline performance, as well as potential data contamination from public audio sources.

ProKkCrlaP.one_liner: Derives causal incentive certificates that bound when strategic agent adaptation to a deployed predictor guaranteedly reduces downstream decision regret.
ProKkCrlaP.problem: Decision-focused learning typically assumes a static deployment population, ignoring that deployed predictive rules induce strategic user responses that can arbitrarily degrade post-response decision loss even when historical regret is zero.
ProKkCrlaP.method: The authors introduce causal incentive certificates that map downstream-aware action returns to a strongly monotone strategic equilibrium and derive a primitive causal-decision identity separating true-state causal effects from model-induced decision distortion. Separate smooth and hard-decision branches quantify operator misspecification, anisotropic response covariance, and normal-fan switching, while an independent selected-policy test certifies deployment.
ProKkCrlaP.key_idea: Decomposes post-response decision regret slopes into true-state causal improvement and model-induced distortion at strategic equilibrium to certify a minimum beneficial-effort threshold.
ProKkCrlaP.evidence: Evaluated on 5,000 controlled effort instances and a UCI-based semi-synthetic credit study comparing CS-DFL against baselines.
ProKkCrlaP.claimed_gains: Across 5,000 controlled effort instances, the certificate had zero violations and the primitive identity closed with maximum error below 9e-11; in a UCI-based semi-synthetic study, CS-DFL achieved a worst-environment gain lower bound of 0.0496.
ProKkCrlaP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical framework connecting performative strategic behavior, causal state changes, and downstream decision regret, clearly distinguishing behavioral effort from true decision improvement.
ProKkCrlaP.main_concern: Reviewers note that the certificates assume known cost functions and prescribed causal/behavioral response structures rather than learning them from data, and that semi-synthetic empirical gains over Causal SC-DFL are minimal (0.0880 vs. 0.0875).

XQP9A9YY3F.one_liner: Demonstrates theoretically and empirically that maximizing label-error detection precision under a budget can degrade worst-group accuracy without group metadata.
XQP9A9YY3F.problem: Standard budgeted label verification prioritizes finding the most corrupted labels (detection precision), assuming that correcting more errors automatically improves downstream worst-group accuracy when group annotations are unavailable.
XQP9A9YY3F.method: The authors conduct controlled experiments holding correction count, flip direction, and post-repair class balance fixed to isolate the role of sample identity and feature geometry on post-retraining worst-group accuracy (WGA). They prove an information-theoretic minimax regret lower bound for group-blind oracle detectors and compare precision-based selection against class-balanced quotas and historical clean-validation selection.
XQP9A9YY3F.key_idea: Proves that non-identifiability of latent subgroups causes group-blind high-precision label cleaning to skew query allocation and incur up to 50 percentage points of worst-group accuracy regret.
XQP9A9YY3F.evidence: Supported by an information-theoretic minimax regret lower bound (Theorem 1) and 510 paired retraining comparisons across group-robustness benchmarks including Waterbirds and CivilComments.
XQP9A9YY3F.claimed_gains: Proves that without group metadata even an error-free oracle detector incurs minimax regret approaching 50 percentage points.
XQP9A9YY3F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear reframing of budgeted data cleaning around post-retraining worst-group accuracy rather than detection precision, supported by solid theory and careful paired experiments.
XQP9A9YY3F.main_concern: Reviewers note that under group-blind constraints the diagnosis and remedies largely reduce to observed class-imbalance handling, and that alternative policies do not consistently outperform precision-based cleaning with statistically significant margins across all datasets.

gbF9y5BH5l.one_liner: Adapts client-specific network depth and width in model-heterogeneous federated learning via a hierarchical beta-Bernoulli Bayesian framework.
gbF9y5BH5l.problem: Model-heterogeneous federated learning methods typically partition a global network using fixed heuristic rules, preventing clients from adapting sub-model architectures to the statistical properties of their non-IID local data.
gbF9y5BH5l.method: FedSAM formulates model-heterogeneous federated learning as hierarchical Bayesian inference, modeling each client's local network depth and width via beta and conjugate Bernoulli processes while placing a global beta-process hyper-prior at the server to aggregate and share structural statistics across clients via structured variational inference.
gbF9y5BH5l.key_idea: Models client sub-network depth and width with local beta-Bernoulli processes coupled through a server-level hierarchical beta-process hyper-prior.
gbF9y5BH5l.evidence: Evaluated across image and text classification tasks (including CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100) under non-IID and model-heterogeneous settings with global-prior ablations and complexity measurements.
gbF9y5BH5l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating client sub-network structure as a latent variable shared via a hierarchical beta-Bernoulli prior is a principled, low-overhead Bayesian alternative to heuristic sub-model partitioning.
gbF9y5BH5l.main_concern: Reviewers note that the Bayesian structure-learning formulation closely follows existing non-federated beta-process networks with finite truncation, omits key recent baselines (such as FedRolex/FIARSE on text or FedEL/FedLAGC), and shows minimal gains on text benchmarks.

Pz29TNsONm.one_liner: Optimizes knowledge bases offline for LLM agents by generating multi-hop probe questions from atomic claim chains and validating targeted wiki edits.
Pz29TNsONm.problem: Knowledge bases constructed via static heuristics often store relevant facts without organizing the cross-page links, search indexes, and context structure needed for LLM agents to assemble multi-hop evidence chains.
Pz29TNsONm.method: Offline-Grounded ClaimWiki (OG-ClaimWiki) extracts source-verified atomic claims and relational evidence chains to generate synthetic multi-hop probe questions before real user queries arrive. By comparing an agent's retrieval trace against the required evidence chain, it diagnoses structural defects and applies source-verified candidate edits that must pass probe, independent, and regression checks.
Pz29TNsONm.key_idea: Generates synthetic multi-hop probes from extracted source-claim chains and diffs required evidence against agent access traces to diagnose and validate offline knowledge-base edits.
Pz29TNsONm.evidence: Evaluated across four document QA datasets and two code benchmarks using five different answering models.
Pz29TNsONm.claimed_gains: Offline probing increases document macro-average F1 by 2.6-4.3 points over the initial Wiki across answering models.
Pz29TNsONm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing knowledge-base organization defects offline by comparing agent retrieval traces against required claim chains is intuitive, model-agnostic, and consistently improves downstream QA across multiple answering models.
Pz29TNsONm.main_concern: Reviewers note that the underlying claim graph is never directly evaluated for extraction precision or recall (so facts missed during graph construction are never probed) and request finer attribution across different edit types.

9d4WW152vh.one_liner: Guides 3D hand motion flow matching using early-stabilized 2D video wrist trajectories for spatio-temporally consistent video-hand generation.
9d4WW152vh.problem: Joint video and 3D hand motion generators learn cross-modal correspondence implicitly, often producing 3D hand trajectories whose 2D reprojections drift away from the hands depicted in the generated egocentric video.
9d4WW152vh.method: Uni-HaVi exploits the observation that 2D hand trajectories in generated video stabilize within the first few flow-matching steps whereas 3D hand motion stabilizes later. Its Dynamic Projective Guidance (DPG) uses a video hand locator and a learned adapter to progressively steer 3D hand motion generation toward the early 2D video wrist trajectory throughout flow matching.
9d4WW152vh.key_idea: Steers 3D hand motion flow matching toward early-stabilized 2D video hand trajectories using a video hand locator and a learned projective adapter.
9d4WW152vh.evidence: Evaluated on EgoDex and a second dataset using independent RGB-based wrist evaluators, whole-hand mask overlap, 3D motion metrics (Motion-FID, MPJPE), and a pouring demonstration.
9d4WW152vh.claimed_gains: On EgoDex, DPG reduces wrist alignment error from 42.3 to 19.0 px.
9d4WW152vh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the observation that 2D video hand trajectories stabilize earlier than 3D motion during flow matching insightful and agree that DPG substantially improves 2D spatial wrist and mask alignment.
9d4WW152vh.main_concern: Reviewers point out that 2D wrist guidance does not resolve 3D depth ambiguity or improve 3D motion quality metrics (with Motion-FID slightly worsening on EgoDex), and request quantitative comparisons against two-stage pipelines.

sWB8x3XYt5.one_liner: Fine-tunes a frozen video diffusion model with LoRA to synthesize tactile pressure videos directly from egocentric RGB video.
sWB8x3XYt5.problem: Collecting hardware tactile sensing data for dexterous manipulation is expensive and difficult to scale compared to recording egocentric RGB video.
sWB8x3XYt5.method: The authors repurpose the pretrained Wan2.1-Fun-Control video diffusion generator by keeping its base weights frozen and applying lightweight LoRA fine-tuning to predict tactile-pressure video streams—as well as joint hand configuration and hand-object segmentation—directly from egocentric RGB video inputs.
sWB8x3XYt5.key_idea: Transfers physical interaction priors from a frozen pretrained video diffusion model to egocentric RGB-to-tactile pressure video synthesis via LoRA fine-tuning.
sWB8x3XYt5.evidence: Evaluated quantitatively on the single-hand OpenTouch and bimanual EgoTouch test sets against a randomly initialized control, with qualitative transfer to in-the-wild videos.
sWB8x3XYt5.claimed_gains: On the OpenTouch test set using only video observations, achieves an MSE of 0.0080, hard IoU of 0.412, and soft IoU of 0.644 for tactile prediction.
sWB8x3XYt5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity and practicality of adapting a frozen video diffusion backbone via LoRA to predict tactile pressure maps from RGB video alone across single-hand and bimanual datasets.
sWB8x3XYt5.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the absence of quantitative baselines—such as existing vision-to-tactile predictors (EgoPressureDiff), deterministic regression models on the same backbone, or simple mean/retrieval baselines—beyond a single random-initialization control.

qcowDQOFAg.one_liner: Factorizes the MoE router matrix at low rank with a fused Triton kernel to scale expert counts at fixed active FLOPs.
qcowDQOFAg.problem: In fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts layers with a large number of experts M and hidden dimension h, the standard linear router's per-token cost Theta(Mh) becomes a computational and HBM memory bottleneck.
qcowDQOFAg.method: MoRE (Mixture of Rank-reduced-routed Experts) factorizes the router weight matrix at low rank r to reduce routing complexity to O((h + M)r) and pairs it with a fused inference Triton kernel that avoids materializing intermediate routing logits in HBM. This allows scaling the total number of experts by a factor of Theta(h/r) at matched active FLOPs.
qcowDQOFAg.key_idea: Applies a rank-r factorization to the MoE router weight matrix with a fused HBM-avoiding Triton kernel to scale total expert count under a fixed active FLOP budget.
qcowDQOFAg.evidence: Supported by theoretical expressivity and Gaussian load-balancing proofs showing rank logarithmic in M suffices, plus experiments on a synthetic phonebook memorization task, language pretraining Q&A benchmarks, and B200 GPU kernel timings.
qcowDQOFAg.claimed_gains: Reduces per-token routing cost from Theta(Mh) to O((h + M)r) and allows a factor of Theta(h/r) more experts at matched active FLOPs.
qcowDQOFAg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Combining low-rank router factorization with a fused Triton kernel and logarithmic-rank expressivity theory is well-executed and reduces routing overhead in extreme-expert regimes.
qcowDQOFAg.main_concern: Reviewers note that matching active FLOPs by scaling expert count gives MoRE 5-6x more total parameters and 15-42% slower training steps than baselines, while in standard modern MoE architectures routing accounts for less than 1-3.3% of compute.

zoVwWYXOts.one_liner: Distills sequential world-action models by aligning action scores on student-generated videos and propagating action gradients via VJP.
zoVwWYXOts.problem: Applying distribution matching distillation naively to sequential world-action models conditions action distillation on ground-truth videos rather than student-generated futures and provides no action-level gradient feedback to the video generator.
zoVwWYXOts.method: CoRe-WAM combines Condition-Aligned Distribution Matching Distillation (CA-DMD) with training-free Recurrent Action Refinement (RAR). CA-DMD conditions the action sampler and both teacher and fake action score models on the same student-generated future video, and uses a vector-Jacobian product (VJP) to backpropagate action distribution-matching gradients into the video generator.
zoVwWYXOts.key_idea: Conditions teacher and student action score matching on shared student-generated future videos and backpropagates action DMD gradients to the video generator via a vector-Jacobian product.
zoVwWYXOts.evidence: Evaluated on robot manipulation benchmarks including RoboTwin, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus against Joint DMD and Flash-WAM.
zoVwWYXOts.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that resolving the conditioning mismatch between ground-truth training videos and student-generated inference videos via CA-DMD and VJP action feedback is well-motivated and yields clear gains over naive Joint DMD.
zoVwWYXOts.main_concern: Reviewers note that performance and latency improvements over the strongest consistency-distillation baseline (Flash-WAM) are marginal, while RAR closely resembles prior training-free warm-start flow policies and is sensitive to noise-level tuning.

8fPOxtchdp.one_liner: Conditions both candidate action generation and frozen world-model rollout scoring on predicted multi-duration latent subgoals.
8fPOxtchdp.problem: Long-horizon planning with latent world models degrades as the planning horizon grows because random action proposals struggle to cover the exponentially expanding action space and final-goal scoring penalizes necessary intermediate steps.
8fPOxtchdp.method: SAGE trains a goal-conditioned generator to predict intermediate latent subgoals across multiple temporal durations and uses the predicted subgoal to condition a prior action-sequence generator. The frozen latent world model then simulates and scores candidate action proposals against that same intermediate subgoal rather than the distant final goal.
8fPOxtchdp.key_idea: Uses predicted intermediate latent subgoals of varying durations to simultaneously condition candidate action proposal generation and serve as the evaluation target for world-model rollout scoring.
8fPOxtchdp.evidence: Evaluated on PushT, OGBench Cube, and LIBERO manipulation tasks across varying planning horizons (including target offset H=150) on frozen world-model backbones.
8fPOxtchdp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that aligning the action proposal prior and the world-model evaluation target on the same intermediate latent subgoal is a coherent decomposition supported by systematic component ablations.
8fPOxtchdp.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the headline baseline is an untuned random-walk proposal that scores 0%, while the supervised subgoal and action-prior networks are not compared against standard hierarchical or goal-conditioned imitation learning trained on the same oracle data.

bLflKiEtfU.one_liner: Enables a frozen LLM agent to continually learn online by diagnosing execution failures and patching a persistent executable code policy.
bLflKiEtfU.problem: Frozen LLM agents typically reset or rely on static prompts across episodes, struggling to convert fine-grained online interaction failures into persistent, cumulative behavioral improvements.
bLflKiEtfU.method: Continual Policy Programming (CPP) represents an agent's decision procedure as a persistent executable code policy separated from working memory. During online interaction, a critic diagnoses execution discrepancies and triggers local patches to named policy functions that take effect immediately within the current episode and persist across future tasks.
bLflKiEtfU.key_idea: Represents agent behavior as a persistent executable code policy that is locally patched online within episodes upon critic failure diagnosis and retained across subsequent tasks.
bLflKiEtfU.evidence: Evaluated across ALFWorld, WebShop, MiniGrid, and AppWorld using multiple LLM backbones (including GPT-4.1 and GLM-5.3-Flash).
bLflKiEtfU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of online continual learning for frozen LLM agents practical and appreciate representing the policy as modular executable code that can be locally repaired and persisted across tasks.
bLflKiEtfU.main_concern: Reviewers note that the experiments lack a 'without cross-task persistence' ablation or performance-over-time curves to separate genuine cross-task continual learning from within-episode error repair.

7sKKYx83bJ.one_liner: Separates current-state recognition from next-label transition evidence using dedicated latent queries, dynamic routing, and EMA future-state distillation.
7sKKYx83bJ.problem: Multimodal models trained solely to classify the current observation suffer from Semantic Transition Aliasing, collapsing histories that share the same current label but lead to different future semantic transitions.
7sKKYx83bJ.method: Predictive Semantic World State (PSWS) infers a predictive state from past textual, acoustic, and visual observations by separating current-semantic and transition-oriented evidence through dedicated latent queries. It predicts modality- and interaction-specific state increments via an evidence-conditioned router and aligns predicted next states with an EMA-encoded future target during training, decoding both with a shared label decoder.
7sKKYx83bJ.key_idea: Factorizes current-label and future-transition evidence via dedicated latent queries and aligns routed state increments with an EMA-encoded future target to prevent transition aliasing.
7sKKYx83bJ.evidence: Evaluated on multimodal recognition and future-label prediction datasets (including conversational emotion transition tasks) under a causal past-only protocol with modality- and supervision-matched baselines.
7sKKYx83bJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing Semantic Transition Aliasing and encouraging representations to retain clues about upcoming semantic label transitions is an interesting formulation supported by controlled ablations.
7sKKYx83bJ.main_concern: Reviewers question whether stochastic future transitions justify forcing different latent representations for identical current labels, note missing ablations applying the transition contrastive loss to simpler architectures, and point out increased training time.

nfDoTthEHW.one_liner: Benchmarks five-step progressive SVG icon editing with target-free drift metrics and refines edits via a verifier-guided multi-trajectory agent.
nfDoTthEHW.problem: Existing SVG editing benchmarks evaluate isolated single-turn edits, missing cumulative structural drift and content degradation that propagate across sequential multi-turn edits.
nfDoTthEHW.method: The authors formulate progressive SVG editing as a trajectory-level change-and-preserve problem, introducing IconEditBench (4,000 source SVGs undergoing five sequential edits each, drawn from a 2.45M icon corpus) and 12 target-free metrics for completion, preservation, and drift. They also propose AgentIconEdit, a verifier-guided multi-trajectory framework that validates and refines candidate edits before propagating state to the next turn.
nfDoTthEHW.key_idea: Evaluates sequential SVG editing across five-step trajectories with 12 target-free change-and-preserve metrics and gates state propagation using a verifier-guided multi-candidate refinement loop.
nfDoTthEHW.evidence: Evaluated across closed-source and open-source models on IconEditBench (4,000 five-step trajectories, 20,000 editing instances) alongside human assessments.
nfDoTthEHW.claimed_gains: Across four closed-source models, AgentIconEdit preserves perfect SVG validity while improving mean Edit Coverage by 4.8% and Spatial Placement by 31.6%, and reducing geometric and topological drift by 37.5% and 35.3%, respectively.
nfDoTthEHW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value formulating progressive SVG editing as a stateful multi-turn problem and view the 4,000-trajectory IconEditBench benchmark as a substantial, practical contribution.
nfDoTthEHW.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the target-free preservation and drift metrics penalize legitimate requested edits (such as moving or deleting elements), and that AgentIconEdit is a straightforward plan-sample-verify loop that uses 12-15x more tokens than single-pass baselines.

5gA4AaEUiN.one_liner: Trains long-horizon LLM agents with a reverse-to-forward curriculum along reference trajectories and paired prefix-reach/suffix-completion advantages.
5gA4AaEUiN.problem: Training LLM agents on long-horizon tasks with sparse terminal rewards suffers from poor exploration and coarse credit assignment across long trajectories.
5gA4AaEUiN.method: The authors define a policy-induced capability region of reliably solvable states and decompose long-horizon RL into reaching a solvable boundary state and completing the task from there. They pair a two-part advantage decomposition (separating prefix selection across endpoints from suffix completion within an endpoint) with a reverse-to-forward curriculum that expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories before exploring off-reference states on-policy.
5gA4AaEUiN.key_idea: Decomposes credit assignment into paired state-reaching and task-completing advantages while expanding the agent's solvable state region via a reverse-to-forward curriculum over reference trajectories.
5gA4AaEUiN.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct against agentic RL baselines.
5gA4AaEUiN.claimed_gains: Achieves success rates of 90.1%/96.1% on ALFWorld and 80.2%/82.6% on WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.
5gA4AaEUiN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing credit assignment into reaching a solvable intermediate state and completing the suffix is intuitive and yields strong empirical success rates on ALFWorld and WebShop across two model scales.
5gA4AaEUiN.main_concern: Reviewers note that the reverse curriculum requires pre-collected successful reference trajectories and environment state resets (overlapping heavily with Backplay), and lacks a reference-free ablation to isolate the paired advantage from reference-trajectory access.

vjhDrXIUVO.one_liner: Characterizes the capacity, spectrum, and sample complexity of projected quantum kernels through the data-to-readout quantum channel interface.
vjhDrXIUVO.problem: Projected quantum kernel methods access high-dimensional quantum states only through a prescribed local readout, leaving unclear how the circuit interface constrains the information and effective dimension available for learning.
vjhDrXIUVO.method: The authors formalize the data-to-readout interface as a transfer channel restricted to the encoder span, proving that reachable readout dimension is bounded by the squared operator Schmidt rank of the fixed quantum process. For sector-preserving controlled interfaces and CNOT crossings, they derive an exact factorization into input-dependent probabilities and fixed readout geometry, yielding closed-form Fisher information, population-kernel spectra, finite-sample/measurement bounds, and classical hardness results.
vjhDrXIUVO.key_idea: Factorizes sector-preserving data-to-readout quantum channels into input-dependent control probabilities and fixed readout geometry to bound projected kernel spectra, effective dimension, and shot complexity.
vjhDrXIUVO.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs (operator Schmidt rank bounds, closed-form CNOT parity Fisher information, spectral and finite-shot guarantees, and complexity-theoretic hardness) alongside numerical experiments including finite-shot simulations.
vjhDrXIUVO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that analyzing how much encoded information reaches a projected readout and characterizing its finite-sample and measurement costs addresses a fundamental question in quantum kernel learning, supported by thorough finite-shot experiments.
vjhDrXIUVO.main_concern: Reviewers find the presentation dense and hard to follow, note that several core bounds follow directly from standard channel rank and Schmidt decomposition properties or prior quantum kernel expressivity work, and observe that results are restricted to linear projected kernels.

FMWoUsitKJ.one_liner: Schedules KV cache states across full-precision, 8-bit quantized, and dropped stages under a shrinking generation horizon for visual autoregressive models.
FMWoUsitKJ.problem: Visual autoregressive model KV caches consume over 80 GB of GPU memory at high resolution, while binary pruning discards token information rather than reducing precision.
FMWoUsitKJ.method: HorizonKV uses a small offline calibration to decouple future demand from compression sensitivity for each KV state. It allocates a global physical-byte budget via Lagrangian relaxation to enforce irreversible transitions from full precision to 8-bit quantization to eviction as the remaining generation horizon shrinks.
FMWoUsitKJ.key_idea: Governs irreversible transitions between full-precision, 8-bit quantized, and dropped KV states using Lagrangian relaxation over decoupled future demand and compression sensitivity as the generation horizon shrinks.
FMWoUsitKJ.evidence: Evaluated on Infinity-2B and Infinity-8B models with component ablations and physical-byte budget comparisons against HeatKV.
FMWoUsitKJ.claimed_gains: At 1% KV storage, it approaches full-cache visual quality on Infinity-2B and Infinity-8B (and achieves up to 4x less KV-cache memory in the TL;DR).
FMWoUsitKJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating future demand from compression sensitivity and adding an intermediate quantized state yields substantial fidelity gains at small KV cache budgets.
FMWoUsitKJ.main_concern: Comparisons primarily evaluate against pruning-only baselines rather than combined pruning-and-quantization policies, and practical memory/latency trade-offs at 1% budget are insufficiently detailed.

86g6xEz1fs.one_liner: Represents 3D scenes as sparse point clouds of 3D-anchored latent features for joint scene reconstruction and camera-controlled generation.
86g6xEz1fs.problem: Conventional video-VAE latents encode viewpoint-specific appearances rather than persistent 3D scene structure, entangling camera motion with scene content and requiring video regeneration for new trajectories.
86g6xEz1fs.method: SceneAE represents scenes as an unstructured 3D-anchored latent point cloud where each latent pairs an explicit 3D position with an implicit local content feature. It projects and decodes this persistent representation into RGB-D views for target cameras, and generates scenes by synthesizing camera-controlled 3D geometry before conditioning content generation on it.
86g6xEz1fs.key_idea: Combines explicit 3D anchor coordinates with implicit content features in a sparse latent point cloud to decouple geometry generation from appearance synthesis and enable multi-view RGB-D decoding.
86g6xEz1fs.evidence: Evaluated on novel-view synthesis and camera-controlled scene generation against baselines including Gen3R, GLD, SceneTok, and LVSM.
86g6xEz1fs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the scene-centric 3D-anchored latent representation and geometry-first generation design provide a sensible unifying structure for multi-view decoding and camera controllability.
86g6xEz1fs.main_concern: Geometry comparisons use inconsistent reference depth sources across baselines (VGGT vs. DA3), and total multi-stage sampling costs and novel-view rendering on generated latents are unclear.

aCbk3ZVCX7.one_liner: Applies a dynamics-aware information bottleneck between one-step video features and action policies to improve robot manipulation generalization.
aCbk3ZVCX7.problem: Video representations contain excessive visual detail and noise that can cause coupled action policies in video-action models to overfit and fail under distribution shifts.
aCbk3ZVCX7.method: IronMan introduces a dynamics-aware information bottleneck at the video-action interface to compress single-step video features into compact world representations. This bottleneck suppresses irrelevant visual details while retaining action-relevant dynamics cues for the downstream action policy.
aCbk3ZVCX7.key_idea: Places a dynamics-aware variational information bottleneck between one-step video backbone features and the action generation head to filter out task-irrelevant visual details.
aCbk3ZVCX7.evidence: Evaluated in simulation on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin, as well as on real-world robot manipulation tasks.
aCbk3ZVCX7.claimed_gains: IronMan achieves success rates of 99.0% on LIBERO, 79.4% on RoboTwin clean2clean, and 79.1% on LIBERO-Plus under OOD shifts, exceeding the strongest baseline by 10.4 percentage points.
aCbk3ZVCX7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that constraining information at the video-action interface is well motivated for preventing visual shortcut learning and achieves strong empirical results on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus.
aCbk3ZVCX7.main_concern: The mechanism of the information bottleneck and the specific contribution of video supervision versus generic token pooling are insufficiently isolated and analyzed.

mzHYHjcJev.one_liner: Estimates second-order KV-cache eviction damage via softmax-renormalized perturbations and matrix-free scalar probes for global budget allocation.
mzHYHjcJev.problem: Existing KV-cache eviction methods treat removal perturbation, downstream sensitivity, and budget allocation separately, producing scores that are difficult to compare globally across layers and heads.
mzHYHjcJev.method: SWIFT formulates task-free KV-cache eviction around a self-fidelity objective against detached uncompressed outputs using full-coverage context observations. It combines exact softmax-renormalized removal perturbations with matrix-free scalar probes via vector-Jacobian products to estimate second-order output damage and allocate a shared physical KV budget across layers, heads, and tokens.
mzHYHjcJev.key_idea: Computes globally comparable second-order token eviction scores by combining exact softmax-renormalized attention removal perturbations with matrix-free scalar probes against uncompressed model outputs.
mzHYHjcJev.evidence: Evaluated across 1,792 controlled interventions, three 7-8B model families, and four long-context benchmarks.
mzHYHjcJev.claimed_gains: Achieves Pearson and Spearman correlations of 0.9957 and 0.9948 with measured eviction damage, ranks first or joint-first in 22 of 24 primary comparisons, and at 20% retention provides 5x physical KV compression with a 9.7-14.1% steady-state decoding speedup.
mzHYHjcJev.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that accounting for softmax renormalization and estimating output fidelity without explicitly materializing the Jacobian or Hessian enables principled global KV budget allocation.
mzHYHjcJev.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited relative to gradient- and curvature-based KV eviction methods like KVGrad and OBCache, and the wall-clock overhead of running observation forwards and backward passes during selection is not clearly accounted for.

7LOmFpuhE9.one_liner: Couples modality-specific second-order oscillators through an availability-gated matrix inside the state-space differential equation for incomplete clinical time-series.
7LOmFpuhE9.problem: Linear state-space models that handle missing modalities via input masking leave the transition operator unchanged, making latent states additive in availability indicators and unable to represent joint modality presence interactions.
7LOmFpuhE9.method: CAMOS assigns each clinical modality a bank of second-order oscillators coupled through an availability-gated matrix inside the differential equation so the transition operator depends on observed measurements. It uses a per-channel Gershgorin budget for uniform positive definiteness across all availability patterns and time gaps, and a channel factorization to preserve exact associative parallel scans.
7LOmFpuhE9.key_idea: Gates inter-modality coupling inside a second-order oscillatory state-space transition operator by measurement availability while enforcing a Gershgorin stiffness budget and channel factorization for parallel scans.
7LOmFpuhE9.evidence: Supported by a theoretical availability-additivity proof, stability analysis across 2^M availability patterns, and empirical evaluations on ADNI and OASIS-3 clinical cohorts.
7LOmFpuhE9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that proving the availability-additivity limitation of input-masked linear state-space layers and gating transition dynamics via a Gershgorin-constrained coupling matrix is mathematically well formulated.
7LOmFpuhE9.main_concern: The additivity theorem only applies to a single linear layer rather than deep architectures with nonlinear fusion, and discrepancies in the supplementary code and cohort statistics raise concerns about potential label leakage in landmark conversion experiments.

ZHLtwOqdtD.one_liner: Shares and aggregates fixed-length normalized singular value spectra across heterogeneous federated learning clients as a structural prior.
ZHLtwOqdtD.problem: Model heterogeneity in federated learning produces incompatible parameter and representation dimensions across clients, limiting methods that require compatible model components or explicit feature alignment.
ZHLtwOqdtD.method: FedSpec applies singular value decomposition to local feature spaces to extract fixed-length normalized spectral structures representing the importance distribution of principal directions. The server aggregates these client spectra into a global spectral structure, which clients use as a structural prior for local spectral correction.
ZHLtwOqdtD.key_idea: Extracts fixed-length normalized singular value distributions from heterogeneous local feature spaces via SVD and aggregates them globally to regularize client representations without parameter matching.
ZHLtwOqdtD.evidence: Supported by convergence and information-reduction analyses and experiments across heterogeneous model architectures and data modalities including CIFAR-100.
ZHLtwOqdtD.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 7.67% accuracy improvement with substantially lower communication cost.
ZHLtwOqdtD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing normalized singular value spectra provides a simple, architecture-independent collaboration interface with low communication overhead.
ZHLtwOqdtD.main_concern: Discard of singular vectors leaves principal subspaces semantically unaligned under high non-IID data, and technical novelty is viewed as incremental given prior SVD use in federated learning.

JyZ4HeipjZ.one_liner: Combines action-conditioned next-scale autoregression with hierarchical time-scale streaming memory for long-horizon robotic world modeling and policy evaluation.
JyZ4HeipjZ.problem: Generative robotic world models often hallucinate task success, accumulate rollout errors, or suffer from excessive memory growth over long simulation horizons.
JyZ4HeipjZ.method: SWAN integrates scale-aligned action conditioning across resolutions into a next-scale autoregressive world model paired with a bounded time-scale streaming memory that retains fine recent and coarse distant states. It uses scale-wise dream forcing during training and aligns visual dynamics on rollouts using action-following and consistency rewards without task-success rewards.
JyZ4HeipjZ.key_idea: Unifies scale-aligned action conditioning, coarse-to-fine temporal streaming memory, and scale-wise dream forcing within a next-scale autoregressive generator to bound memory and prevent success hallucination.
JyZ4HeipjZ.evidence: Evaluated on streaming rollouts up to 60 seconds and 600 matched sim-to-real rollout pairs with five frozen policy checkpoints across six tasks.
JyZ4HeipjZ.claimed_gains: Demonstrates stable streaming rollouts up to 60 seconds, achieving a success-rate MAE of 0.062 and a within-task rank correlation of 0.88 across 600 matched sim-to-real rollout pairs.
JyZ4HeipjZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that long-horizon action-faithful simulation is important for robotic policy evaluation and find the 600-pair frozen-policy sim-to-real evaluation well designed.
JyZ4HeipjZ.main_concern: The paper lacks comparisons against specialized world-model policy evaluators, omits concrete memory schedule parameters needed for reproduction, and does not fully disentangle architectural gains from domain-specific training.

CtI4b39ESR.one_liner: Moving-anchor extragradient updates adapt step sizes and anchor coefficients without known smoothness or strong convexity parameters.
CtI4b39ESR.problem: Accelerated minimax optimization needs adaptation to unknown smoothness and strong convexity-concavity without line searches or restarts.
CtI4b39ESR.method: MA⁴EG combines extragradient steps with a moving anchor and adaptively updates both step size and anchor coefficient. Its analysis covers smooth convex-concave objectives and automatically obtains linear convergence under strong convexity-concavity.
CtI4b39ESR.key_idea: Adapt the extragradient step size and moving-anchor coefficient together to compensate for oversized steps while retaining acceleration.
CtI4b39ESR.evidence: Theory proves last-iterate convergence guarantees, and numerical experiments compare methods across settings with different local and global problem parameters.
CtI4b39ESR.claimed_gains: MA⁴EG achieves an O(1/k^2) last-iterate convergence rate for smooth convex-concave objectives and a linear rate under strong convexity-concavity.
CtI4b39ESR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that simultaneous adaptation to smoothness and strong monotonicity without prior parameter knowledge is the main strength.
CtI4b39ESR.main_concern: The adaptive guarantees leave practical constants and rate optimality insufficiently characterized.

sDG8pYzbqO.one_liner: Seed expansion and query-conditioned graph encoding retrieve knowledge-graph answers while retaining separate intermediate reasoning nodes.
sDG8pYzbqO.problem: Dense retrieval misses compositional graph queries, while unrestricted graph expansion and agent exploration can consume excessive resources.
sDG8pYzbqO.method: SeedER expands seed nodes through filtered k-hop selection and encodes a bounded subgraph with a query-conditioned Graph Transformer. It learns retrieval with reinforcement learning while keeping intermediate reasoning nodes separate from returned answers.
sDG8pYzbqO.key_idea: Encode a filtered seed-expanded subgraph per query and separate message-passing intermediates from the answer budget.
sDG8pYzbqO.evidence: A fixed-embedding lower bound motivates query-time structure access, and experiments cover three STaRK datasets with MiniLM, ada-002, and Qwen embeddings over five seeds.
sDG8pYzbqO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the bounded seed-expand-retrieve design practical and credit consistent gains across graphs and encoders.
sDG8pYzbqO.main_concern: The sparse-feedback motivation for reinforcement learning lacks direct validation or matched supervised-ranking comparisons.

WiPEof1aMa.one_liner: Functional layer grouping and importance-based pruning construct memory-budgeted client submodels for federated language-model adaptation.
WiPEof1aMa.problem: Base-model memory requirements exclude resource-constrained devices from federated LLM fine-tuning.
WiPEof1aMa.method: FedPruner groups layers by functionality and selects important layers within groups to form device-specific submodels. A finer variant independently prunes attention and feed-forward components.
WiPEof1aMa.key_idea: Group layers by functional similarity, then select important layers or components to fit each client's memory budget.
WiPEof1aMa.evidence: Experiments compare memory-aware federated methods, vary device memory constraints, and ablate the pruning components.
WiPEof1aMa.claimed_gains: FedPruner reports average accuracy gains of up to 11.11% and a 1.98% average performance improvement while reducing peak memory usage by 75%.
WiPEof1aMa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the method addresses the practical memory burden of federated LLM adaptation through structured client-specific pruning.
WiPEof1aMa.main_concern: The validity of aggregating updates from differently pruned clients and the associated global-gradient assumptions remains insufficiently justified.

ECW72HKjH8.one_liner: Absolute activation scaling and sign-mismatch penalties modify post-hoc out-of-distribution detection for backbones with negative activations.
ECW72HKjH8.problem: Positive-negative cancellation makes SCALE's activation-magnitude ratio ill-defined on backbones such as vision transformers.
ECW72HKjH8.method: An Absolute Fix computes the scaling ratio from absolute-valued activations. Anti-coherence regularization then penalizes the scale using the fraction of sign-mismatched contributions to the predicted class's maximum logit.
ECW72HKjH8.key_idea: Compute activation scaling from absolute magnitudes and penalize sign-inconsistent contributions to the predicted-class logit.
ECW72HKjH8.evidence: CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments under OpenOOD v1.5 compare AUROC and FPR@95 across activation-shaping methods and backbone architectures.
ECW72HKjH8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear presentation and broad experiments, with positive reviews also crediting the simple absolute-value correction.
ECW72HKjH8.main_concern: The rationale and independent contribution of anti-coherence beyond the absolute-value fix or simpler confidence measures remain unclear.

YL8wxvjCYf.one_liner: Controlled physical task variations and partial-credit scoring standardize real-robot manipulation evaluation.
YL8wxvjCYf.problem: Simulation misses physical deployment failures, while fragmented real-robot evaluations hinder fair comparisons and failure attribution.
YL8wxvjCYf.method: ManipArena defines matched physical tasks with structured variations, in-domain and shifted trials, subtask scoring, language annotations, and motor signals. It also pairs physical scenes with reconstructed simulation environments.
YL8wxvjCYf.key_idea: Compare policies under matched physical conditions using structured task variations and subtask-level partial credit.
YL8wxvjCYf.evidence: The resource contains 20 tasks, 10,812 expert trajectories, 13.5M frames, and approximately 188 robot hours, with evaluation of seven tabletop policy configurations.
YL8wxvjCYf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the substantial scale of real-robot data collection and evaluation.
YL8wxvjCYf.main_concern: The paper does not clearly distinguish its reusable benchmark contribution and unique evaluation questions from existing real-robot benchmarks.

sko7pDWv3n.one_liner: Cross-view reprojection rewards and progressively longer RL rollouts train video generation to replay events from new viewpoints.
sko7pDWv3n.problem: Novel-view video generation must preserve the source event's geometry and motion while changing the camera viewpoint.
sko7pDWv3n.method: ReView first adapts a pretrained video generator using synthesized monocular pairs, simulated multi-view videos, and real multi-view images. It then applies a reprojection-and-visual-matching reward through single-frame, mixed, and full-video reinforcement-learning stages.
sko7pDWv3n.key_idea: Optimize cross-view reprojection consistency while progressively extending reinforcement-learning rollouts from single frames to full videos.
sko7pDWv3n.evidence: Comparisons measure viewpoint accuracy, geometric consistency, reconstruction, and video quality, with single-frame, fixed-mixture, direct-switching, and full-video RL controls.
sko7pDWv3n.claimed_gains: Progressive-Horizon RL reaches geometric consistency comparable to full-video RL using less than one third as much training compute.
sko7pDWv3n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the geometric post-training results and progressive rollout curriculum with improved consistency and more efficient video RL.
sko7pDWv3n.main_concern: The paper insufficiently distinguishes its supervised pipeline and geometry-aware RL from closely related novel-view video methods.

aiOxqxS38n.one_liner: A separately trained memory planner diversifies valid memory choices and usage intentions before role-playing response generation.
aiOxqxS38n.problem: Role-playing LLMs repeatedly use only a few valid memory policies, limiting behavioral diversity despite individually valid responses.
aiOxqxS38n.method: A plug-in planner specifies which retrieved memories to use and how they should shape a response. Instance-specific rubrics generate diverse valid plans for diversified SFT followed by Diversity-Controlled GRPO.
aiOxqxS38n.key_idea: Separate memory planning from response generation and train the planner to retain multiple valid plan-intent types per scenario.
aiOxqxS38n.evidence: Plan and response evaluations compare SFT and GRPO variants, include use with six response models, and report human evaluation and data audits.
aiOxqxS38n.claimed_gains: DC-GRPO reaches 75.34% plan validity versus 60.16% for vanilla SFT and increases Effective Plan-Intent Types@10 from 1.651 with vanilla GRPO to 4.978.
aiOxqxS38n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between valid and diverse memory use and the inspectable planner's reported diversity gains.
aiOxqxS38n.main_concern: Shared rubric and judge dependence, weak annotation agreement, and inconsistent diversity evidence undermine evaluation reliability.

zlEesEteMm.one_liner: Shallow recurrent drafts read full-depth prefix values while parallel refinement and full-depth verification accelerate looped-transformer decoding.
zlEesEteMm.problem: Looped Transformers require many sequential recurrent passes per token, and same-depth prefix reads limit shallow draft quality.
zlEesEteMm.method: DAS decouples draft computation depth from the depth of verified-prefix representations, letting shallow queries read mature values. DAS-Wave combines these reads with carried parallel refinement, progressive block growth, and an independent full-depth verifier.
zlEesEteMm.key_idea: Let shallow draft queries retrieve full-depth verified-prefix values without additional recurrent computation.
zlEesEteMm.evidence: Channel interventions and component ablations accompany throughput tests across four recurrent-model checkpoints and mathematics, code, and general-language workloads.
zlEesEteMm.claimed_gains: DAS-Wave achieves 3.87–6.96× mean throughput speedup over paired full-depth autoregressive decoding in the same inference stack.
zlEesEteMm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the channel-wise interventions and component ablations with linking prefix depth to draft quality and consistent decoding speedups.
zlEesEteMm.main_concern: The incremental benefit of depth-asynchronous reads remains insufficiently separated from existing cache sharing and parallel-refinement machinery.

A76Jplrsgr.one_liner: Per-query normalization and query-aware key clustering improve block retrieval for sparse video-diffusion attention.
A76Jplrsgr.problem: Averaging queries before softmax and clustering keys in ordinary Euclidean space can select inaccurate attention blocks.
A76Jplrsgr.method: PARK retains original queries, normalizes each query's attention over key blocks, and averages the resulting distributions within query blocks. It also transforms keys using current-query information before clustering to preserve similarity of query-key scores.
A76Jplrsgr.key_idea: Average attention distributions after per-query softmax and cluster keys under a query-induced metric.
A76Jplrsgr.evidence: Mathematical approximation-error analyses, component ablations, and quality-latency comparisons evaluate sparse attention across four video diffusion models.
A76Jplrsgr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis of query aggregation and key-clustering mismatches well motivated and supported by mathematical analysis.
A76Jplrsgr.main_concern: The practical contribution of query-aware key clustering remains insufficiently isolated from the other retrieval changes.

BQUQtfrb1X.one_liner: Depth-shuffle reconstruction, additive binary quantization, and frozen-teacher distillation produce clinically aligned volumetric tokens without paired training reports.
BQUQtfrb1X.problem: Volumetric anisotropy and scarce scan-text pairs complicate learning medical representations with both structural fidelity and clinical semantics.
BQUQtfrb1X.method: VOLT first learns through-plane structure with Depth Shuffle reconstruction and discretizes latents through Additive Binary Spherical Quantization. A second stage applies patch-consistency matching and distillation from a frozen scan-text-pretrained teacher without paired reports for VOLT's training scans.
BQUQtfrb1X.key_idea: Learn discrete volumetric structure from scan-only reconstruction, then transfer clinical semantics through patch consistency and a frozen multimodal teacher.
BQUQtfrb1X.evidence: Reconstruction comparisons and downstream evaluations cover segmentation, classification, VQA, report generation, and synthetic data generation, including frozen-encoder BTCV protocols.
BQUQtfrb1X.claimed_gains: VOLT reports a 4.19 dB reconstruction PSNR gain over MedVAE, 6.30 points higher BTCV Dice, 2.47 lower HD95, 1.47 percentage points higher closed-ended VQA accuracy, and 1.65 higher report-generation BLEU.
BQUQtfrb1X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the relevance of scan-only volumetric learning and credit the reconstruction results and downstream coverage.
BQUQtfrb1X.main_concern: Unequal downstream protocols and insufficiently matched quantizer capacities complicate attribution of the reported advantages.

IunFOrepGi.one_liner: Matched video pairs and observation-grounded reasoning training counter semantic priors in physical video judgments.
IunFOrepGi.problem: Video-LLMs can report expected outcomes despite contradictory visual evidence in impossible or plausible but counter-intuitive events.
IunFOrepGi.method: PriorPair pairs prior-aligned events with semantically matched conflicting events across eight physical categories. PhyAR uses explicit observation-grounded reasoning chains and matched-pair supervision through LoRA fine-tuning.
IunFOrepGi.key_idea: Bind semantically matched video pairs during training and require explicit visual observations before physical attribution and judgment.
IunFOrepGi.evidence: PriorPair contains 828 video pairs, and evaluation covers physical-validity and event-verification tasks on two backbones plus external benchmarks.
IunFOrepGi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matched-pair benchmark for testing whether physical judgments follow observed events rather than familiar expectations.
IunFOrepGi.main_concern: The results do not clearly separate improved visual grounding from answer-polarity effects and losses on prior-aligned questions.

T1ycCvjTpT.one_liner: Editable typed specifications expose the personal-agent stack for model-specific optimization of on-device AI.
T1ycCvjTpT.problem: Replacing cloud models with local models in existing personal-agent stacks causes failures partly due to model-specific workflow and runtime defaults.
T1ycCvjTpT.method: OpenJarvis represents Intelligence, Engine, Agents, Tools & Memory, and Learning as independently editable fields in a typed specification. An LLM-guided optimization loop searches these system configurations around the chosen model.
T1ycCvjTpT.key_idea: Represent the entire agent stack as editable typed fields so an optimization loop can jointly adapt model-specific system choices.
T1ycCvjTpT.evidence: Experiments analyze local-model substitution on PinchBench and GAIA and evaluate optimized on-device configurations across benchmarks and component controls.
T1ycCvjTpT.claimed_gains: On-device specifications match or exceed cloud accuracy in 4 out of 8 reported cases.
T1ycCvjTpT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the explicit system abstractions and diagnosis of model-stack incompatibilities with making local-agent optimization practical.
T1ycCvjTpT.main_concern: Task-specific optimization requires curated calibration data and costly setup, leaving applicability to everyday private tasks unclear.

o4mYZtNu4D.one_liner: Scaled weight updates learned on earlier donor checkpoints transfer new capabilities into post-trained models with less interference.
o4mYZtNu4D.problem: Supervised updates to heavily post-trained models can damage retained capabilities, while on-policy self-distillation adds sampling cost and can collapse.
o4mYZtNu4D.method: The approach learns off-policy updates on earlier donor checkpoints, scales them, and applies them to the final model. It optionally protects sensitive weights and finds unfinished pretraining checkpoints effective as donors.
o4mYZtNu4D.key_idea: Learn adaptation deltas on an earlier checkpoint, then scale and graft them onto the final model while optionally masking sensitive weights.
o4mYZtNu4D.evidence: Experiments compare acquisition and retention or generalization across knowledge injection, expert-trace learning, and self-improvement, including merging sweeps for SFT and OPSD.
o4mYZtNu4D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the approach simple and practically relevant and value evaluating both acquisition and retained performance.
o4mYZtNu4D.main_concern: The additional contribution over existing donor-delta transfer methods such as Shadow-FT is limited and insufficiently isolated.

ncm4LOBJJW.one_liner: Compression-rate slopes across window sizes predict corpus data-scaling exponents through a once-fitted calibration.
ncm4LOBJJW.problem: Estimating each candidate corpus's data-scaling exponent normally requires a separate grid of model-training runs.
ncm4LOBJJW.method: The Data Manifold Oracle measures how DEFLATE compression rate changes as the window grows. A map calibrated once on 38 corpora predicts data-scaling exponents for new raw-text corpora.
ncm4LOBJJW.key_idea: Map the slope of compression rate versus window size to a data-scaling exponent using a corpus-level calibration.
ncm4LOBJJW.evidence: Evaluation includes leave-parent-family-out calibration, 11 held-out families in two prospective rounds, two training protocols, proxy models, and block-shuffling interventions.
ncm4LOBJJW.claimed_gains: DMO reports ranking correlation ρ = 0.80, ρ = 0.81 under each training protocol, and prospective mean absolute error 0.087, which is 0.032 below the calibration-set mean and level with a per-domain mean.
ncm4LOBJJW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find compression-based exponent prediction inexpensive and credit the empirical investigation with demonstrating a useful relationship.
ncm4LOBJJW.main_concern: The appendix theory is insufficiently connected to the empirical prediction of data-scaling exponents.

sACsE6qCYE.one_liner: Fast-and-slow video screening allocates reasoning selectively using influence-filtered training data and structured reasoning traces.
sACsE6qCYE.problem: Uniform use of large video-language models wastes computation on easy moderation cases while difficult temporal cases need deeper reasoning.
sACsE6qCYE.method: SafeLens combines fast screening with slower reasoning for harder videos. It filters SafeWatch data using influence estimates and augments the retained examples with structured chain-of-thought traces.
sACsE6qCYE.key_idea: Route video moderation through fast or slow reasoning stages trained on an influence-filtered subset with structured reasoning supervision.
sACsE6qCYE.evidence: Real-world and AI-generated video benchmarks compare SafeLens with SafeWatch-8B, OmniGuard-7B, GPT-5.4, and Gemini-3.1-pro, with filtering and cascade ablations.
sACsE6qCYE.claimed_gains: Influence-guided filtering retains only 2.4% of the original SafeWatch Dataset.
sACsE6qCYE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical fast-and-slow design and its reported accuracy-runtime trade-off.
sACsE6qCYE.main_concern: Dependence on SafeWatch-Real for influence selection and validation leaves generalization to unseen real videos insufficiently established.

aCRvstw8nw.one_liner: Periodic safety-subspace estimation projects solver updates away from dominant safety representation directions during agent self-evolution.
aCRvstw8nw.problem: Self-evolving agents can lose safety behavior across training rounds even while task accuracy improves.
aCRvstw8nw.method: SEGO identifies a safety subspace from model representations and re-estimates it as the model changes. It orthogonalizes solving updates against dominant subspace directions while leaving task generation unconstrained.
aCRvstw8nw.key_idea: Periodically refresh a representation-derived safety subspace and remove solver-gradient components along its dominant directions.
aCRvstw8nw.evidence: Experiments use multiple self-evolution frameworks and models with safety and capability benchmarks, comparing constrained and ordinary evolution.
aCRvstw8nw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find safety preservation during self-evolution important and credit SEGO with consistent practical safety gains.
aCRvstw8nw.main_concern: The evidence supports a useful intervention but does not establish geometry as the underlying cause of safety degradation.

iGWixHU6Mg.one_liner: Physical scene graphs, differentiable pose refinement, and simulation feedback reconstruct stable 3D scenes from a single image.
iGWixHU6Mg.problem: Individually plausible reconstructed objects can form physically inconsistent scenes with interpenetration, floating objects, and unstable support.
iGWixHU6Mg.method: ImScene corrects detected instances, builds a physical relation graph, and derives gravity-aligned metric coordinates from depth. A differentiable optimizer refines object poses and scales under visual and physical constraints, followed by simulator-guided repair.
iGWixHU6Mg.key_idea: Constrain joint object pose and scale optimization with support relations, surface contact, collision penalties, and subsequent simulation feedback.
iGWixHU6Mg.evidence: Comparisons with recent reconstruction baselines and cumulative and leave-one-out loss ablations measure geometric reconstruction and scene stability.
iGWixHU6Mg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical integration of visual alignment and physical constraints and the demonstrated stability improvements.
iGWixHU6Mg.main_concern: The method does not sufficiently isolate its technical advance over relation-guided refinement systems such as CAST and REST3D.

c0yLkLKAgz.one_liner: Layer-wise VLM anchoring and shared-observation motion-language supervision preserve generalization during robot-policy fine-tuning.
c0yLkLKAgz.problem: Behavior cloning overwrites pretrained visual-semantic representations, while separate web-data co-training leaves language and action predictions misaligned.
c0yLkLKAgz.method: Anchor-Align adds layer-wise distillation from a frozen VLM to behavior cloning. It also converts action targets into discrete motion-direction labels and trains language and action prediction on the same robot observation.
c0yLkLKAgz.key_idea: Anchor hidden representations to a frozen VLM while jointly predicting motion-direction language and actions from each robot observation.
c0yLkLKAgz.evidence: Evaluations cover eight real-world settings on xArm7 and bimanual YAM robots, two action-head types, and LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN.
c0yLkLKAgz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the objectives simple and practical and value evaluation across real robots, action heads, and simulation benchmarks.
c0yLkLKAgz.main_concern: Baseline selection and unexpected baseline degradation leave the strength and fairness of the comparisons insufficiently established.

OGCy2ElTfF.one_liner: Class-adaptive spatial debiasing and drift-aware gradient correction counter catastrophic overfitting in fast adversarial training.
OGCy2ElTfF.problem: Single-step adversarial training can abruptly lose adversarial robustness through persistent class-specific perturbations and misaligned ascent gradients.
OGCy2ElTfF.method: DC-FGSM disrupts class-specific perturbation patterns with spatial debiasing and compensates for post-initialization gradient drift with directional correction. The correction module can also augment existing fast adversarial-training methods.
OGCy2ElTfF.key_idea: Disrupt class-correlated perturbation patterns and correct the initial attack gradient using subsequent local ascent information.
OGCy2ElTfF.evidence: Experiments span multiple datasets, perturbation budgets, architectures, and attacks, including correction added to seven FAT baselines on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
OGCy2ElTfF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the practical robustness improvements and broad evaluation, including gains when gradient correction augments existing methods.
OGCy2ElTfF.main_concern: The experiments show trigger-like patterns and gradient drift accompanying catastrophic overfitting without establishing them as its causes.

cKbdVXYGqz.one_liner: Caches each rolling-window video chunk without attending to prior KV entries at test time to curb long-video drift.
cKbdVXYGqz.problem: Autoregressive video diffusion models experience color, texture, and motion drift in long rollouts because cached KV entries are written under out-of-distribution histories.
cKbdVXYGqz.method: In-Distribution Forcing (ID-Forcing) aligns test-time KV caching and KV conditioning with training configurations without retraining. Its self-caching mechanism encodes and writes each video chunk into the rolling KV cache without attending to any prior KV entries.
cKbdVXYGqz.key_idea: Encode and cache each rolling-window video chunk without attending to preceding KV cache entries during rollout so cached representations avoid compounding history drift.
cKbdVXYGqz.evidence: Evaluated at test time on standard and minute-scale long video generation benchmarks across two base models (Self-Forcing and LongLive) and four durations.
cKbdVXYGqz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that self-caching is a simple, training-free change to rolling KV-window writes that reduces visual and motion drift on pretrained autoregressive video models.
cKbdVXYGqz.main_concern: Reviewers challenge the central claim of exact training-distribution alignment, noting that caching multi-frame non-initial chunks without context still differs from the single-frame initial chunk seen in training.

TBnppdMMir.one_liner: Calibrates a global MoE router with synthetic feature distributions while restricting shared VLM backbone updates to residual subspaces.
TBnppdMMir.problem: In federated continual learning of MoE vision-language models, client heterogeneity biases routing toward dominant or recent tasks while shared-backbone updates degrade frozen historical experts.
