TBnppdMMir.method: DART summarizes client routing inputs in a fixed reference space so the server can maintain per-expert historical distributions and sample balanced synthetic features to calibrate a global router without raw replay. Meanwhile, historical experts are frozen and shared-backbone updates are restricted to a bootstrapped residual subspace to limit representation interference.
TBnppdMMir.key_idea: Sample balanced synthetic features from server-maintained per-expert distributions in fixed reference coordinates to calibrate routing while projecting shared-backbone updates onto a residual subspace.
TBnppdMMir.evidence: Evaluated on federated continual vision-language learning benchmarks with component ablations and routing diagnostics.
TBnppdMMir.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms baselines with performance improvements of up to 7.18%.
TBnppdMMir.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly addressing MoE routing drift and shared-backbone interference without raw replay targets a real coupled forgetting problem in federated continual VLM learning.
TBnppdMMir.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns over diminishing plasticity and ~14.02 GiB server storage from expanding protection subspaces across tasks, alongside under-justified energy thresholds and communication accounting.

agK22lRpG8.one_liner: Benchmarks personalized item recommendation from long-term multimodal assistant interaction histories across explicit, implicit, and evolving user preferences.
agK22lRpG8.problem: Personalized recommendation benchmarks rely on platform behavioral logs rather than recovering sparse, incidental user preferences scattered across everyday multimodal assistant interactions.
agK22lRpG8.method: The authors propose the LIP-Rec paradigm and construct PersonaRec, comprising 200 personas, over 30K human-refined items across Fashion, Food, and Movies (21 sub-domains), and 83.5K-length multimodal daily interaction histories per persona with explicit, implicit, and evolving cues. They evaluate frontier MLLMs and train a reasoning-based baseline (Yo'Rec) using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
agK22lRpG8.key_idea: Embed sparse explicit, implicit, and evolving multimodal item-preference cues across 83.5K-length daily assistant histories linked to traceable sessions and a 30K-item catalog.
agK22lRpG8.evidence: Benchmarked frontier MLLMs and SFT/RL-trained Yo'Rec variants on PersonaRec across 200 personas, over 30K candidate items, and held-out evaluation domains.
agK22lRpG8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that personalized recommendation from long-term incidental MLLM assistant conversations is practical and that PersonaRec offers systematic, traceable multi-domain coverage.
agK22lRpG8.main_concern: Reviewers criticize relying on LLM-synthesized role-play histories that threaten ecological validity, omitting closely related benchmarks such as VisualLens and LoCoMo, and entangling SFT with reasoning/formatting ablations.

wpub2lcZS1.one_liner: Combines frozen source-graph spectral subspaces with target-graph residual variation to align node-feature interfaces for graph foundation models.
wpub2lcZS1.problem: Graph foundation models that preprocess node attributes via independent per-graph spectral projections discard recurring source feature directions when they are not locally dominant.
wpub2lcZS1.method: Under a positional feature convention, SoLIFT combines frozen source subspace statistics with target-graph variation through two preprocessing interfaces: SoLIFT-Split reserves shared source capacity and fills remaining width via residual PCA, while SoLIFT-Fusion jointly selects directions and orients coordinates toward a fixed source reference while preserving within-graph geometry.
wpub2lcZS1.key_idea: Combine frozen source-graph subspace statistics with target-graph residual PCA or basis orientation under positional feature alignment before feeding node attributes into graph foundation models.
wpub2lcZS1.evidence: Supported by theoretical spectral and within-graph geometry analysis and transfer evaluations across seven GFM pipelines onto five unseen target graphs.
wpub2lcZS1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate focusing on a backbone-agnostic feature preprocessing interface with geometry-preserving guarantees and evaluating across seven GFM pipelines.
wpub2lcZS1.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the unrealistic assumption that node-feature columns align semantically by position across heterogeneous graphs, alongside mixed transfer gains over only five target graphs.

Hj1E83Gszd.one_liner: Models post-minus-prior node memory residuals via Chebyshev Laplacian spectral projection and conditional diffusion for dynamic graph anomaly detection.
Hj1E83Gszd.problem: Continuous-time dynamic graph anomaly detectors trained with contrastive or reconstruction objectives overfit source domains and immediate temporal contexts, degrading across domains and irregular time gaps.
Hj1E83Gszd.method: TopoDiff computes memory residuals as the difference between posterior and prior node memory representations after an interaction and projects them via a positive-definite Chebyshev polynomial spectral operator over the normalized graph Laplacian. A conditional diffusion model learns the generative distribution of normal topology-projected residuals for zero-shot anomaly scoring.
Hj1E83Gszd.key_idea: Project interaction-induced node memory residuals through a Chebyshev graph-Laplacian spectral operator and model normal residual distributions with a conditional diffusion network.
Hj1E83Gszd.evidence: Evaluated on continuous-time dynamic graph benchmarks under zero-shot cross-domain transfer (including MOOC, Bitcoin, and Amazon) with component ablations.
Hj1E83Gszd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find modeling interaction-driven memory residuals with topology-conditioned diffusion reasonable and note strong zero-shot cross-domain anomaly detection performance.
Hj1E83Gszd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether memory subtraction and diffusion drive the gains, noting ablations where removing diffusion yields minimal AUROC change within variance and unverified cross-domain residual consistency.

WbLevlVyhb.one_liner: Sparse-autoencoder concept contrasts turn outcome rewards into token-level advantages for reasoning policy optimization.
WbLevlVyhb.problem: Outcome-verified reinforcement learning provides sequence-level correctness without identifying which intermediate reasoning tokens deserve credit.
WbLevlVyhb.method: SAEPO builds token-level semantic representations with a pretrained sparse autoencoder and scores tokens using concepts learned without supervision. The plug-in advantage-shaping module instantiates with GRPO and GSPO.
WbLevlVyhb.key_idea: Contrast correct and incorrect rollouts in sparse concept space to shape token-level advantages from sequence-level outcomes.
WbLevlVyhb.evidence: Evaluation instantiates SAEPO with GRPO and GSPO across three LLM backbones, six math benchmarks, and two code benchmarks.
WbLevlVyhb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value question-local credit assignment without process labels or added inference-time SAE computation across two policy-gradient objectives.
WbLevlVyhb.main_concern: Similarity to SAE representations of correct and incorrect rollouts does not establish token correctness or true local credit.

OZ9nYgmWwn.one_liner: Parallel causal-attention branches add long-range event retrieval to selected layers of pretrained Mamba.
OZ9nYgmWwn.problem: Fixed-size Mamba states can lose distant event information, but standard event-stream benchmarks may not reveal when attention retrieval helps.
OZ9nYgmWwn.method: Moreva shares event-history modeling between a pretrained Mamba backbone and parallel causal-attention branches at selected layers. Synthetic processes vary known dependency length, while EasyTPP tests practical event forecasting.
OZ9nYgmWwn.key_idea: Augment recurrent event summaries with direct attention retrieval of distant events inside selected Mamba layers.
OZ9nYgmWwn.evidence: Synthetic experiments test dependencies hundreds to thousands of events back, and EasyTPP comparisons cover time-point-process, time-series, and language-model baselines.
OZ9nYgmWwn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled lagged-dependency synthetic design and matched Mamba-only and Transformer-only ablations.
OZ9nYgmWwn.main_concern: Attention provides little improvement over the ablations on EasyTPP, and comparisons with the closest hybrid event models are missing.

4xA32aA5kj.one_liner: Composing data, function, and weight anchors with merged LoRA improves hundred-task continual memorization.
4xA32aA5kj.problem: Sequential supervised updates cause catastrophic forgetting during long-horizon memorization without replaying earlier examples or supplying task identifiers.
4xA32aA5kj.method: The study combines three anchor types that specify preserved information with low-rank allocation rules that specify update locations. Task-level successive halving searches compositions, and a factorial experiment measures individual and interaction effects across three 100-task datasets.
4xA32aA5kj.key_idea: Compose complementary preservation anchors with merged low-rank updates to address different forgetting sources across long task sequences.
4xA32aA5kj.evidence: Three constructed 100-task datasets support staged search over 90 configurations and a full factorial analysis of mechanism interactions.
4xA32aA5kj.claimed_gains: The best method ranks among the top 3 on all three datasets and achieves 34.9% average final retention, compared with 8.1% for generative replay.
4xA32aA5kj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the 100-task protocol and systematic comparison of mechanism combinations across datasets and factorial controls.
4xA32aA5kj.main_concern: The work combines existing techniques on an artificial same-question memorization setup without explaining why the best composition works.

fYjpvbs2cX.one_liner: Group-relative policy gradients steer frozen diffusion samplers using demonstration-verified action-space scores.
fYjpvbs2cX.problem: Noise-space diffusion steering must adapt using signals verifiable only in action space, forcing trade-offs between environment RL and inversion.
fYjpvbs2cX.method: DS-GRPO samples noise groups from a steering policy, decodes them through a frozen sampler, and scores actions against demonstrations. These action-space scores drive group-relative steering-policy updates without changing base-policy weights.
fYjpvbs2cX.key_idea: Use demonstration agreement on decoded action groups as the reward for group-relative updates in noise space.
fYjpvbs2cX.evidence: Simulation and real-world experiments cover offline behavior cloning, goal-conditioned behavior cloning, and online DAgger across multiple base policies.
fYjpvbs2cX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the direct decoded-action supervision, forward-only access to frozen samplers, and evaluation across several adaptation settings.
fYjpvbs2cX.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate GRPO from simpler action-space updates or fully account for the cost of decoding multiple candidates.

1fiFCSxDlx.one_liner: CARAT measures prompt-optimization suitability through cross-sample preference stability and shared-prompt success compatibility.
1fiFCSxDlx.problem: Reflective prompt optimization varies across random seeds, leaving run-level accuracy unable to characterize whether a task suits prompt optimization.
1fiFCSxDlx.method: CARAT-A measures whether prompt preferences persist across disjoint case samples, while CARAT-C tests whether observed successes fit a shared prompt. MRFS samples from independent roots under a fixed proposal budget and retains every valid proposal.
1fiFCSxDlx.key_idea: Estimate task-level prompt accessibility and coherence from complete multi-root proposal collections rather than one optimizer's selected prompt.
1fiFCSxDlx.evidence: Ten tasks with Qwen3-8B as answerer and reflector are evaluated using collections from five prompt optimizers over multiple seeds.
1fiFCSxDlx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating preference stability from shared-prompt compatibility reveals task properties hidden by average accuracy.
1fiFCSxDlx.main_concern: The experiments validate repeatable readings but not better prompt-selection decisions or transfer beyond the single Qwen3-8B configuration.

xouua0CCuV.one_liner: Lighting-probe-guided camera selection improves surface coverage for HDR Gaussian reconstruction of game worlds.
xouua0CCuV.problem: Prescribed street trajectories waste limited capture budgets and provide insufficient directional surface observations for free-view game-world reconstruction.
xouua0CCuV.method: Game2GS selects complementary camera poses from baked lighting probes using known source geometry, then reconstructs HDR Gaussians from scene-linear captures. Evaluation includes independently sampled free-6DoF views beyond capture trajectories.
xouua0CCuV.key_idea: Optimize camera acquisition for resolved, directionally diverse surface coverage before HDR Gaussian reconstruction.
xouua0CCuV.evidence: Experiments compare acquisition and radiometric reconstruction under limited image budgets using trajectory-near and free-6DoF evaluation protocols.
xouua0CCuV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value budgeted acquisition from source geometry and the free-6DoF evaluation that exposes failures hidden near capture trajectories.
xouua0CCuV.main_concern: Headline comparisons change both camera acquisition and HDR reconstruction, while matched random, uniform, and prior selection controls are absent.

lgAbT33ZED.one_liner: Stabilizes forward-only node perturbation in continual learning by periodically rescaling neuron incoming and outgoing weight norms.
lgAbT33ZED.problem: Node perturbation injects independent layer noise that causes parameter drift along loss-invariant rescaling symmetries, hurting long-stream adaptation.
lgAbT33ZED.method: Using a frozen-state analysis, the authors show non-gradient perturbation noise induces a random walk along rescaling symmetries. They propose gauge-damped node perturbation (GD-NP), which periodically applies local reciprocal rescaling to each hidden neuron's incoming and outgoing weights.
lgAbT33ZED.key_idea: Periodically applies function-preserving reciprocal rescaling to each hidden neuron's incoming and outgoing weights to damp symmetry drift.
lgAbT33ZED.evidence: Supported by frozen-state theoretical analysis for positively homogeneous activations and small-scale continual-learning experiments.
lgAbT33ZED.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical identification of symmetry drift under node perturbation and the local GD-NP correction are mathematically clean.
lgAbT33ZED.main_concern: Reviewers find limited empirical accuracy gains and insufficient evidence that symmetry drift actually drives plasticity loss, alongside unclear terminology.

DGfz2qVM7P.one_liner: Restores aged color film negatives by detecting blue-channel corruption via cross-channel 3D geometric feature discrepancies.
DGfz2qVM7P.problem: Aged color film negatives suffer severe blue-channel degradation that holistic RGB restoration methods fail to localize and exploit.
DGfz2qVM7P.method: The method treats RGB channels as separate inputs to a pretrained 3D foundation model (DA3) and uses cross-channel geometric feature discrepancies to localize corrupted B-channel regions for selective restoration from R and G. The same geometric features also guide region-aware color mapping from a reference print.
DGfz2qVM7P.key_idea: Uses cross-channel discrepancies in pretrained 3D geometric features to localize degraded blue-channel regions and guide selective restoration and color mapping.
DGfz2qVM7P.evidence: Evaluated on the BlueNeg dataset with degraded-negative/pseudo-ground-truth pairs and synthetic B-channel fading, plus ablations.
DGfz2qVM7P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting cross-channel geometric feature consistency for channel-heterogeneous negative restoration is well-motivated and intuitive.
DGfz2qVM7P.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns over reliance on single-run results with narrow margins on BlueNeg pseudo-ground truth and failure modes of per-image min-max normalization.

yOzVa8Dzn4.one_liner: Distills a centralized cooperation-aware humanoid transport teacher into decentralized base-plus-residual policies from multi-view human demonstrations.
yOzVa8Dzn4.problem: Physical coupling through a shared object makes whole-body control for unconstrained cooperative humanoid transport harder than single-robot control.
yOzVa8Dzn4.method: CoWBC reconstructs human collaboration demonstrations from multi-view videos, trains a centralized teacher with cooperation-aware rewards, and distills it into local student policies with a shared base, role-specific residuals, and learner-state refinement.
yOzVa8Dzn4.key_idea: Combines a shared base policy with role-specific residuals distilled from a centralized teacher and refined on closed-loop student states.
yOzVa8Dzn4.evidence: Ablation studies on learner-state refinement, role residuals, and staged training, plus real-world G1 humanoid-human demonstrations.
yOzVa8Dzn4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cooperative humanoid transport problem and multi-view demonstration/ablation pipeline are interesting and carefully constructed.
yOzVa8Dzn4.main_concern: The paper lacks a zero-shot single-robot transport baseline to prove explicit cooperation is needed, and real-world videos leave unclear whether the humanoid bears load.

YvOMCpTeCx.one_liner: Conditions neural operators explicitly on PDE physical parameters and boundary conditions via a parameter-gated mixture of kernels.
YvOMCpTeCx.problem: Purely data-driven neural operators infer PDE parameters and boundary conditions implicitly from history, causing ill-posedness and poor generalization.
YvOMCpTeCx.method: The Generalized Neural Operator takes physical parameters and boundary conditions as explicit inputs using a parameter-gated mixture of kernels to generalize across PDE instances without retraining.
YvOMCpTeCx.key_idea: Uses explicit physical parameter and boundary-condition conditioning with a parameter-gated mixture of kernels inside a neural operator.
YvOMCpTeCx.evidence: Experiments across multiple PDE families compared against neural operator and numerical baselines, plus an ablation on one PDE setting.
YvOMCpTeCx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important generalization gap in PDE surrogate modeling with clear motivation and empirical baseline improvements.
YvOMCpTeCx.main_concern: Boundary conditions are only soft-conditioned and not strictly satisfied, undermining the well-posedness claim, and mathematical exposition and ablations are incomplete.

TLMgsn20mO.one_liner: Proves a two-layer attention-only Transformer implements finite-temperature in-context Q-learning and analyzes local manifold convergence.
TLMgsn20mO.problem: While Transformers can execute reinforcement learning in context, how off-policy control algorithms like Q-learning emerge from training remains poorly understood.
TLMgsn20mO.method: They construct a two-layer Transformer (softmax attention plus linear attention) implementing finite-temperature Q-learning, train it on random MDPs with output-only supervision, and analyze local convergence to the solution manifold.
TLMgsn20mO.key_idea: Pairs a softmax attention layer with a linear attention layer to implement finite-temperature Q-learning and derives local convergence rates.
TLMgsn20mO.evidence: Theoretical construction and convergence-rate proof, plus training experiments on randomly generated synthetic MDP tasks.
TLMgsn20mO.claimed_gains: Under the random-task model, local worst-case gradient steps to reduce distance to the manifold by factor epsilon scale as Theta(tau^-5 log(1/epsilon)).
TLMgsn20mO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending mechanistic in-context RL theory from policy evaluation to off-policy Q-learning with a clean two-layer construction and training-dynamics analysis.
TLMgsn20mO.main_concern: Experiments are restricted to small random MDPs with a hand-designed architecture, and comparisons with existing off-policy in-context RL methods are incomplete.

0fAlQQVRQW.one_liner: Introduces NEST, a 900+-subject EEG-sMRI-fMRI benchmark via shared film timelines, and NESTOR for native-anatomy fMRI prediction.
0fAlQQVRQW.problem: Existing EEG-to-fMRI benchmarks omit subject-specific anatomy and are limited to cohorts under 40 subjects due to simultaneous recording constraints.
0fAlQQVRQW.method: NEST aligns separately recorded EEG and fMRI along shared film timelines, and NESTOR conditions 4D fMRI prediction on static structural MRI and time-varying EEG.
0fAlQQVRQW.key_idea: Aligns non-simultaneous EEG and fMRI via shared naturalistic film timelines and conditions prediction on native structural MRI.
0fAlQQVRQW.evidence: Evaluated on two film cohorts (904 and 963 subjects) for unseen-subject voxel reconstruction, temporal correlation, functional connectivity, and zero-shot movie transfer.
0fAlQQVRQW.claimed_gains: NEST scales to 904 and 963 subjects across two films, over 40x more subjects than the largest public EEG-fMRI dataset.
0fAlQQVRQW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the large-scale tri-modal benchmark (over 900 subjects per film) and the well-motivated use of subject-specific structural MRI.
0fAlQQVRQW.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are confounded by differing inputs (more EEG channels, longer context, and sMRI), and assuming identical stimulus-driven responses across separate sessions is unverified.

tkxk4VsWta.one_liner: Decomposes LLM-judge variability into prompt, order, interaction, and call noise using two calls per prompt to remove finite-call bias.
tkxk4VsWta.problem: Plug-in prompt-sensitivity scores for LLM judges conflate systematic prompt dependence with stochastic decoding noise across repeated calls.
tkxk4VsWta.method: They cross prompts with candidate orders and use agreement between distinct calls to isolate prompt, position, interaction, and call variance, deriving exact estimator variance and detection bounds.
tkxk4VsWta.key_idea: Uses cross-call agreement under a balanced prompt-by-order design to remove finite-call decoding noise bias from prompt sensitivity.
tkxk4VsWta.evidence: Theoretical variance and detection-bound derivations plus over one million judgments from six judges across three benchmarks and 320 unseen items.
tkxk4VsWta.claimed_gains: Lowering sampling temperature raises Qwen's corrected prompt-sensitivity estimate nearly fivefold (call-level interval 3.3 to 8.5), reversing the Qwen-Gemma-3 sensitivity ranking.
tkxk4VsWta.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separating prompt sensitivity from repeated-call randomness using a balanced second-order decomposition with exact variance and detection bounds.
tkxk4VsWta.main_concern: The estimator equals classical trace-mean-square correction, relevant LLM-judge reliability baselines are missing, and call-level intervals for some cooling claims include zero.

bYlE7gC5qw.one_liner: Formalizes auditable regret for online routing with endogenous feasible sets across observation levels L0-L2 and repayment window W.
bYlE7gC5qw.problem: Online routing consumes resources that alter future feasibility, making offline counterfactual trajectory comparisons unverifiable from deployment logs alone.
bYlE7gC5qw.method: They define an auditable regret frontier (L0/L1/L2 feedback and repayment window W), prove minimax cost bounds for exact L1 oracles, specialize CVQ-Routing, and build a surrogate controller with pathwise certificates.
bYlE7gC5qw.key_idea: Characterizes online routing regret against same-state L1 log-auditable comparators parameterized by a constraint repayment window W.
bYlE7gC5qw.evidence: Minimax lower/upper bounds and controlled synthetic and public-data replays comparing L1 evaluation against L2 own-trajectory replay.
bYlE7gC5qw.claimed_gains: In the normalized exact decision-time L1 oracle game with strict fallback, minimax weighted cost is 0 at W = 1 and Theta(sqrt(WT)) for 2 <= W <= T.
bYlE7gC5qw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the endogenous-feasibility routing problem well-motivated and appreciate the theoretical depth of the auditable regret framework.
bYlE7gC5qw.main_concern: The paper is difficult to follow without a simple example, lacks external constrained-online-learning baselines, and the same-state L1 benchmark may fail to penalize poor trajectory decisions.

hoDYNMy9Ud.one_liner: Introduces RATO, characterizing when causal correction should trade first-order orthogonality for lower local target risk across many treatments.
hoDYNMy9Ud.problem: With many treatments and scarce randomized data, full orthogonal causal correction (A = I) can introduce high variance relative to a preliminary predictor.
hoDYNMy9Ud.method: RATO parameterizes causal correction as an operator A on the (K - 1) treatment-contrast quotient, deriving the local-risk-optimal oracle A* = B(B + S)^-1 and validating a scalar family on deployment data.
hoDYNMy9Ud.key_idea: Trades exact first-order orthogonality for lower local target risk via a shrinkage operator on the treatment-contrast quotient.
hoDYNMy9Ud.evidence: Theoretical risk identities, controlled synthetic experiments, and a retrospective participant-randomized study with 72 actions per context.
hoDYNMy9Ud.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear mathematical characterization of why exact orthogonality (A = I) is generally not finite-sample risk-optimal under many treatments.
hoDYNMy9Ud.main_concern: The optimal operator A* depends on unidentifiable error moments, forcing a 1-D grid-search fallback that lacks theoretical guarantees and shows no consistent real-data gains.

jEhhebXEEl.one_liner: Proposes TopoFT, post-training TRELLIS.2 Stage-2 shape generation with token-wise advantage attribution and anchored dual-branch flow.
jEhhebXEEl.problem: Latent 3D mesh generators like TRELLIS.2 support arbitrary topology but frequently produce non-manifold edges, non-manifold vertices, and boundary holes.
jEhhebXEEl.method: TopoFT decomposes mesh-level group-relative advantages into additive token-wise attributions and optimizes Stage-2 shape-SLat generation with an anchored dual-branch flow objective.
jEhhebXEEl.key_idea: Attributes global mesh topology advantages additively to local tokens and trains Stage-2 with an anchored dual-branch flow objective.
jEhhebXEEl.evidence: Evaluated across four unseen benchmarks, three seeds, mesh simplification (QEM), and slicing tests.
jEhhebXEEl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Stage-2 diagnosis and token-level advantage attribution are well-motivated and consistently improve mesh topology metrics across four benchmarks.
jEhhebXEEl.main_concern: The anchored negative branch is not independently ablated, training time and candidate variance are unreported, and visual evaluation covers only simple low-token shapes.

c95wSsHrBM.one_liner: Combines exact feature-moment sums with weighted class centroids and KL second-order corrections for continual cross-entropy classification.
c95wSsHrBM.problem: Analytic continual learning recovers exact least squares from running feature sums but cannot compute nonlinear cross-entropy gradients over past examples.
c95wSsHrBM.method: QUILT stores exact feature-product and feature-label sums alongside a fixed budget of weighted class centroids to evaluate cross-entropy, using the sums to bound curvature for monotone descent and optionally compute a second-order KL correction.
c95wSsHrBM.key_idea: Pairs exact second-order feature moments with weighted class centroids so cross-entropy updates reuse one matrix factorization with curvature-bounded descent.
c95wSsHrBM.evidence: Evaluated on 14 continual-learning settings across seven datasets and four frozen encoders under equal-byte memory budgets.
c95wSsHrBM.claimed_gains: At the smaller memory budget, QUILT averages 86.12% accuracy versus 85.25% for K-priors and 84.58% for the best analytic method, while matching AIR at the larger budget with lower NLL.
c95wSsHrBM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the theoretical KL decomposition and careful byte-matched experimental comparisons.
c95wSsHrBM.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains over AIR vanish at larger budgets, covariance corrections yield small effects, and ablations do not test reallocating Gram-matrix bytes to extra centroids.

SZuMPlFulF.one_liner: Resolves multi-agent LLM coordination without communication via role-gated and task-coupled scene reading rather than recursive opponent prediction.
SZuMPlFulF.problem: Homogeneous LLM agents acting concurrently without communication suffer a symmetry trap, colliding on exclusive targets and diverging on joint ones.
SZuMPlFulF.method: Theory of Scene (ToS) is a training-free prompting schema where each agent combines its public role (role gating) with shared context (task coupling) to derive a deterministic division of labor or convergence.
SZuMPlFulF.key_idea: Replaces recursive Theory-of-Mind prediction with public role gating and task-coupling rules so homogeneous agents deterministically break symmetry.
SZuMPlFulF.evidence: Evaluated on a new controlled benchmark (DivvyBench) and modified GovSim and Overcooked environments.
SZuMPlFulF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the symmetry-trap framing clear and note strong empirical gains on DivvyBench and GovSim without training or communication.
SZuMPlFulF.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the ToS prompt hardcodes explicit coordination conventions (limiting novelty), lacks frontier closed-model evaluation, and modifies GovSim/Overcooked protocols.

fRznEPwE2E.one_liner: Diagnoses query-independent label collapse in diffusion LLM in-context learning via single-pass log-odds separation and midpoint calibration.
fRznEPwE2E.problem: In-context learning can collapse to query-independent label outputs even under balanced demonstrations while still showing near-chance accuracy.
fRznEPwE2E.method: The authors characterize label collapse across autoregressive and discrete diffusion LLMs, propose single-pass log-odds separation to detect collapse without iterative decoding, and introduce demonstration-anchored calibration (DAC) using midpoint log-odds.
fRznEPwE2E.key_idea: Uses single-pass log-odds separation between candidate labels to expose hidden query-independent collapse and subtracts demonstration-midpoint bias.
fRznEPwE2E.evidence: Evaluated across six diffusion language models, two autoregressive models, 20 label-word pairs, and binary classification tasks.
fRznEPwE2E.claimed_gains: The single-pass diagnostic predicts generation collapse with 93.7% precision (reported in review).
fRznEPwE2E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the systematic characterization of label collapse across diffusion LMs and the simplicity of the single-pass diagnostic.
fRznEPwE2E.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty over existing log-odds calibration, narrow evaluation (two binary tasks, one language), and some inconsistent accuracy numbers.

i2QTmRZ0sh.one_liner: Transports native-resolution radar echoes along K 3D paths and linearly combines path factors for probabilistic nowcasting.
i2QTmRZ0sh.problem: Compressed latent or 3D Gaussian representations degrade high-intensity radar echoes, and iterative diffusion or flow-matching ensembles are too slow for time-critical nowcasting.
i2QTmRZ0sh.method: Probabilistic Sparse Volumetric Transport (PSVT) moves observed native-resolution reflectivity along K 3D transport paths while estimating bounded growth and decay. It models voxelwise Gaussian uncertainty and generates ensemble members as linear combinations of the K shared path-deviation factors without repeated network evaluations.
i2QTmRZ0sh.key_idea: Transports observed native-resolution reflectivity along K shared 3D paths and forms ensemble members via linear combinations of path-deviation factors.
i2QTmRZ0sh.evidence: Experiments on NEXRAD-3Y, TRRD, and SEVIR compare PSVT against deterministic and probabilistic baselines including FlowCast and CasCast, alongside component and dependence ablations.
i2QTmRZ0sh.claimed_gains: On NEXRAD-3Y, PSVT improves single-forecast CSI at 40 dBZ by 114.0% over FlowCast.
i2QTmRZ0sh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transporting native-resolution observations and reusing shared factors yields strong efficiency and high-intensity CSI trade-offs.
i2QTmRZ0sh.main_concern: Reviewers note incomplete probabilistic validation, missing classical optical-flow or pySTEPS baselines, and ambiguity in how paths are defined across leads.

nDmrZCYWto.one_liner: Trains standard byte Transformers with token-superposition and hash embeddings, revealing emergent local abstractions useful for speculative decoding.
nDmrZCYWto.problem: Byte-level language models remove tokenizer biases but suffer from much longer sequences and lack explicit text abstractions.
nDmrZCYWto.method: The authors train flat byte Transformers using token-superposition training (TST) and n-gram hash embeddings without specialized architectures. They probe emergent segmentation-like local abstractions via layer-freezing interventions and exploit boundary-concentrated uncertainty for speculative decoding.
nDmrZCYWto.key_idea: Applies token-superposition training and hash embeddings to flat byte Transformers, inducing emergent local boundary representations that enable speculative decoding.
nDmrZCYWto.evidence: Scaling experiments comparing byte and subword Transformers, intermediate-layer restriction ablations, and speculative decoding evaluations.
nDmrZCYWto.claimed_gains: Exploiting learned local structures for speculative decoding yields 3.4x more accepted tokens than in subword Transformers.
nDmrZCYWto.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the byte-versus-subword scaling results and emergent local abstraction analyses interesting.
nDmrZCYWto.main_concern: Reviewers note that comparisons between BYTE (TST + hash embeddings) and raw SUBWORD are not recipe-matched, leaving it unclear whether gains stem from bytes or training recipe.

q7gKctvQzh.one_liner: Uses a specialized small MLLM to distill query-relevant personalized context from raw history for a frozen large MLLM.
q7gKctvQzh.problem: Pre-compressing user interaction histories into static memories before queries arrive risks losing personalized multimodal evidence needed later.
q7gKctvQzh.method: SMILE pairs a fine-tuned Small MLLM (S-MLLM) that browses the full raw interaction history just-in-time for each query to distill compact relevant evidence with a frozen Large MLLM (L-MLLM) that reasons over the distilled context to generate responses.
q7gKctvQzh.key_idea: Specializes a small MLLM via SFT and RL to extract query-conditioned personalized evidence from raw history for a frozen large MLLM reader.
q7gKctvQzh.evidence: Experiments across four benchmarks (including Persona-MME and LongPersona-MME) comparing against full-history, RAG, and memory baselines, plus FLOPs and RL ablations.
q7gKctvQzh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the small-large division of labor is practical, well-presented, and improves accuracy-FLOPs trade-offs over baselines.
q7gKctvQzh.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing comparisons with learned context-compression baselines, unmeasured scalability/latency when the small model reads growing raw histories, and unclear cross-user generalization.

MUMu0kbJhd.one_liner: Evaluates selective conversational history use across 7,000 paired multimodal visual and audio tasks.
MUMu0kbJhd.problem: Multi-turn multimodal evaluations rarely separate selective history-use demands—reusing old questions or retrieving old evidence—from underlying question difficulty.
MUMu0kbJhd.method: ReTurn constructs 7,000 base tasks across four conditions (Reconfirm, Reground, Retrieve, Rebind) pairing multi-turn conversations with matched single-turn references that preserve target question, media, and answer.
MUMu0kbJhd.key_idea: Isolates task-carrying versus evidence-carrying history dependencies using target-preserving single-turn and multi-turn paired tasks.
MUMu0kbJhd.evidence: Evaluations of 13 omni-modal, vision-language, and audio-language models on open-ended and multiple-choice formats plus behavioral probes.
MUMu0kbJhd.claimed_gains: Across 13 models, median model-level open-ended accuracy drops from 93.7% with direct input to 72.3% in conversation.
MUMu0kbJhd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean decomposition into task-carrying and evidence-carrying history with target-preserving paired tasks.
MUMu0kbJhd.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the lack of human validation/inter-annotator agreement for automated scoring and large discrepancies between rule-based and LLM-reviewed scores, plus parent-video overlap between train/dev and test splits.

UAup7EhBdx.one_liner: Extracts early-layer branch utilities via output-head projection and applies minimal norm-preserving residual edits verified by a forward pass.
UAup7EhBdx.problem: Inference-time activation steering typically targets middle or late layers empirically, missing higher answer coverage in early layers that are obscured by irrelevant signals.
UAup7EhBdx.method: BRIDGE's Early Branch Identification projects early hidden states through the output head to score short natural branches by answer coverage, then Dynamics-aware Geometric Editing computes the smallest norm-preserving residual edit for a target utility gain and keeps it if forward-verified.
UAup7EhBdx.key_idea: Scores early-layer first-token branches via output-head projection and applies forward-verified, minimal norm-preserving residual edits.
UAup7EhBdx.evidence: Evaluated across five Llama and Qwen models (3B to 32B) on truthfulness, fairness, safety alignment, general capabilities, and latency.
UAup7EhBdx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well-motivated and achieves consistent alignment improvements across Llama and Qwen models up to 32B while preserving general capabilities.
UAup7EhBdx.main_concern: Reviewers point out that Figure 2 compares EBI-processed early layers against raw middle/late layers without applying the same branch-scoring pipeline to later layers, leaving early-layer superiority unisolated.

wpp6QPc1ln.one_liner: Trains multimodal LLMs via GRPO to invoke thinking as a virtual tool using global mode balancing and counterfactual sample rewards.
wpp6QPc1ln.problem: Fixed Think-then-Answer MLLMs waste compute on simple inputs, while learning when to think via RL collapses toward always-thinking or always-direct modes.
wpp6QPc1ln.method: Switch-Reasoner frames explicit reasoning as a virtual tool call in GRPO, stabilized by dual-level regulation that balances global Thinking/Direct mode usage and provides sample-level supervision from counterfactual mode comparisons.
wpp6QPc1ln.key_idea: Models explicit reasoning as a virtual tool action in GRPO, regulated by global mode-ratio balancing and counterfactual sample-level rewards.
wpp6QPc1ln.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-VL-4B and 8B across 11 multimodal tasks against GRPO-Thinking and GRPO-Direct.
wpp6QPc1ln.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the adaptive reasoning formulation is practical, well-motivated, and reduces thinking frequency on Qwen3-VL-4B/8B while maintaining aggregate accuracy.
wpp6QPc1ln.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons with prior adaptive-reasoning baselines, lack of output-length/actual compute metrics, and an inconsistent Eq. (11) rule when both modes succeed.

htPloxEtAk.one_liner: Evaluates LLM agents over a simulated 365-day multi-store e-commerce operation with deterministic demand and supplier negotiation kernels.
htPloxEtAk.problem: Short-horizon agent benchmarks do not capture long-range dependencies, liquidity constraints, and multi-round negotiation across evolving business environments.
htPloxEtAk.method: E-Commerce Bench simulates a year-long operation with 6,886 products and 576 suppliers derived from real platform data, pairing deterministic demand and negotiation kernels (verbalized by an LLM) with a calendar of promotions, disasters, and shocks.
htPloxEtAk.key_idea: Decouples deterministic demand and supplier-negotiation kernels from LLM verbalization to benchmark 365-day multi-store autonomous business operation.
htPloxEtAk.evidence: Evaluated 18 frontier models across seven dimensions over 5 episodes each on a fixed 365-day world seed.
htPloxEtAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the rich, consequential 365-day environment and the clean separation between deterministic economic kernels and LLM language generation.
htPloxEtAk.main_concern: Reviewers highlight label leakage where supplier email identifiers reveal fraud status, alongside single-seed evaluation (n=5 episodes) with high variance and no significance tests.

CujR1jaoeS.one_liner: Models each federated client as a semiparametric mixture of latent components with empirical-likelihood density ratios for query routing.
CujR1jaoeS.problem: Routing-prediction federated learning ignores intra-client subpopulations (dual heterogeneity), degrading both server-side query routing and local prediction.
CujR1jaoeS.method: FedSPM represents each client with latent components pairing a classifier and a feature density modeled via density ratios against a shared nonparametric empirical-likelihood baseline, trained via federated EM with a tractable surrogate.
CujR1jaoeS.key_idea: Models client subpopulations as density-ratio mixtures anchored to a shared empirical-likelihood baseline, enabling well-defined cross-client query routing.
CujR1jaoeS.evidence: Proved O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence of the profiled objective and evaluated on controlled benchmarks and the Fed-ISIC2019 medical dataset.
CujR1jaoeS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the semiparametric DRM-EL formulation that puts client feature distributions in a common coordinate system and the tractable closed-form M-step surrogate.
CujR1jaoeS.main_concern: Reviewers note that routing by input density does not guarantee selecting the most accurate client predictor, and key baselines (multi-client averaging, matched per-client GMM) and ablations are missing.

ze600GlifV.one_liner: Resolves intra-sample atom-correspondence ambiguity in crystal flow matching using local periodic optimal coupling.
ze600GlifV.problem: Diffusion and flow-matching crystal generators require many sampling steps and generalize poorly to crystal cells larger than those seen in training.
ze600GlifV.method: OCFlow introduces per-structure local optimal coupling (periodic Hungarian matching and translation correction) into flow matching to shorten and straighten coordinate transport paths for de novo crystal generation.
ze600GlifV.key_idea: Applies intra-sample periodic optimal coupling between prior and target atoms to straighten crystal flow-matching coordinate paths.
ze600GlifV.evidence: Experiments on MP-20 and MPTS-52 benchmarks, including few-step (10 NFEs) sampling and out-of-distribution larger crystal systems.
ze600GlifV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the strong empirical performance on size-transferable out-of-distribution crystal generation and few-step (10 NFEs) sampling.
ze600GlifV.main_concern: Reviewers note overlapping novelty with prior torus-aware optimal coupling methods (such as OMatG and Equivariant Flow Matching) and limited DFT or strict S.U.N. validation.

cTHo9guGdv.one_liner: Adapts a mixture of format-aligned visual connector experts per token using self-critical RL for multimodal table reasoning.
cTHo9guGdv.problem: Multimodal table-image reasoning requires recovering layout, headers, and cell contents without structured table inputs.
cTHo9guGdv.method: TableMoE pairs a General visual connector with experts aligned to HTML, JSON, and table-redrawing code, fusing two experts per visual token. Answer-level RL (Multi-GRPO and deployment-relative SC-RPO) jointly adapts the router, experts, and LoRA modules.
cTHo9guGdv.key_idea: Routes each visual token to two format-aligned connector experts (General, HTML, JSON, redrawing code) adapted jointly via answer-level self-critical RL.
cTHo9guGdv.evidence: Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B across six table benchmarks, TableVQA-Bench, 1,800 held-out questions, and fixed-pair interventions.
cTHo9guGdv.claimed_gains: Multi-GRPO and SC-RPO improve six-task mean accuracy over dense softmax SFT by 4.07 and 6.46 percentage points, reaching 75.79% on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 81.41% on Qwen3-VL-8B.
cTHo9guGdv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reward-based adaptation improves over matched SFT baselines across six benchmarks and that the analysis and ablations are extensive.
cTHo9guGdv.main_concern: Reviewers point out that a fixed expert pair nearly matches learned token-level routing and joint updates confound whether gains come from routing or LoRA/expert tuning.

UTyo1bQB2D.one_liner: Separates worker-agnostic multi-agent task decomposition and collaboration planning from online bandit-based worker selection.
UTyo1bQB2D.problem: Learned multi-agent orchestrators couple planning to fixed worker pools and train decomposition and collaboration from a single terminal outcome, hindering transfer and credit assignment.
UTyo1bQB2D.method: DeOrch uses a two-stage planner that first decomposes tasks without worker identities and then selects collaboration operations using compact matchability feedback, enabling conditional credit assignment. A lightweight probe-based matcher estimates worker suitability and adapts online via a contextual bandit to support new workers without retraining.
UTyo1bQB2D.key_idea: Decouples worker-agnostic decomposition and collaboration planning with nested conditional credit assignment from probe-and-bandit online worker matching.
UTyo1bQB2D.evidence: Experiments on in-distribution, out-of-distribution, and unseen-worker-pool tasks with rollout-budget and training ablations.
UTyo1bQB2D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the separation of planning from worker identities, the conditional credit-assignment mechanism, and the unseen-pool transfer results.
UTyo1bQB2D.main_concern: Reviewers question the necessity of learned collaboration when single-worker decomposition nearly matches full performance, note same-family overlap in the unseen pool, and cite dense notation.

SfzHeH3XnN.one_liner: Encodes sensor images into compact latents and transcodes them once into task-compatible standard JPEG files via learnable transforms.
SfzHeH3XnN.problem: Low-power sensors cannot run heavy encoders like AVIF, while neural codecs impose high consumer decoding costs and break compatibility with standard JPEG infrastructure.
SfzHeH3XnN.method: SEAOTTER pairs a Sensor Embedded Autoencoder with a one-time cloud transcode into standard JPEG using learnable JPEG color and quantization transforms. Both general-purpose and task-aware transcoding pipelines are trained for a frozen encoder to support global, dense, and vision-language perception.
SfzHeH3XnN.key_idea: Transcodes lightweight sensor-side neural latents once in the cloud into standard JPEG using learnable color and quantization transforms.
SfzHeH3XnN.evidence: Evaluations on global, dense, and vision-language perception tasks plus CPU consumer decoding measurements.
SfzHeH3XnN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the sensor-cloud-consumer split-computing framing practical and acknowledge the concrete consumer-side CPU decoding savings.
SfzHeH3XnN.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over prior differentiable/sandwiched JPEG compression works, missing hardware edge-device benchmarks, and insufficient isolation of the learned JPEG components.

6JpwS2ZxsS.one_liner: Decouples structure and semantics in text-attributed graphs using routed hyperbolic/spherical manifold experts and tangent-space text alignment.
6JpwS2ZxsS.problem: Text-attributed graph representation learning suffers from structural-semantic modality mismatch and heterogeneous local topologies that a single geometric space cannot capture.
6JpwS2ZxsS.method: R-MESD initializes structural positions from Laplacian spectra and routes nodes to Hyperbolic and Spherical experts fused in a shared latent space with cross-geometry attention. Node text semantics are represented as tangent vectors anchored at those structural positions and refined via cross-geometry alignment and local tangent-space attention.
6JpwS2ZxsS.key_idea: Routes nodes across Hyperbolic and Spherical manifold experts while anchoring text semantics as tangent vectors aligned via cross-geometry and tangent-space attention.
6JpwS2ZxsS.evidence: Experiments and ablation studies across five public text-attributed graph benchmarks.
6JpwS2ZxsS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that R-MESD achieves strong, consistent accuracy across five benchmarks and that its ablations support combining hyperbolic and spherical experts.
6JpwS2ZxsS.main_concern: Reviewers raise limited novelty over prior mixed-curvature geometric MoE works like CRGFM and RiemannGFM, which are not directly evaluated, alongside reliance on citation networks.

973snYjj21.one_liner: Stabilizes aerial scene coordinate regression under altitude and heading shifts via expanded scale training, yaw canonicalization, and GeoCells.
973snYjj21.problem: Scene coordinate regression degrades under large altitude-induced scale changes and heading rotations in near-nadir aerial relocalization.
973snYjj21.method: AeroSCR expands decoder scale-training coverage, canonicalizes large heading changes in descriptor space, and trains tolerance to residual yaw errors. It adds direct metric supervision and retrieval-gated GeoCells to handle weak aerial geometry and large maps.
973snYjj21.key_idea: Combines scale-coverage training, descriptor-space yaw canonicalization, residual yaw tolerance, and retrieval-gated GeoCells to stabilize aerial coordinate decoding.
973snYjj21.evidence: Controlled descriptor-vs-decoding experiments and localization benchmarks on six AnyVisLoc scenes and the 10 km^2 Oslo-Large scene against HLoc and R-SCoRe.
973snYjj21.claimed_gains: Reaches 90.8% success at 5 m/5 deg on AnyVisLoc (matching HLoc's 90.2%) with 4.0x less storage and 8.2x lower latency, and 86.2% on Oslo-Large with 6.0x less storage and 3.1x lower latency.
973snYjj21.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled insight distinguishing descriptor correspondence from coordinate decodability and the HLoc-comparable accuracy with substantially lower storage and latency.
973snYjj21.main_concern: Reviewers find the methodological combination of scale augmentation, yaw canonicalization, and metric supervision incremental and note reliance on orientation priors and missing qualitative visualizations.

rs10O2r4z9.one_liner: Benchmarks 17 vision-language models on 34,754 questions from real-robot and human demonstrations across recognition, alignment, and temporal grounding.
rs10O2r4z9.problem: Existing video benchmarks rely on human-centric or passive footage and lack direct evaluation of temporal and cross-view understanding in robot task execution.
rs10O2r4z9.method: RoboChrono provides 39 scenarios and 34,754 questions from GIMME_ARM and Marvin Pro robot executions plus human recordings across synchronized views, scoring seven capabilities in recognition, alignment, and temporal grounding.
rs10O2r4z9.key_idea: Evaluates vision-language models on real-robot manipulation videos across seven decomposed capabilities spanning recognition, cross-view/temporal alignment, and temporal grounding.
rs10O2r4z9.evidence: Evaluation of 17 vision-language models across 34,754 questions and input-modality ablations.
rs10O2r4z9.claimed_gains: Doubao-Seed-2.0-Lite reaches 71.7% recognition accuracy and 0.576 tIoU@0.5, while median frame-ordering accuracy across models is 28.9% near the 25% chance baseline.
rs10O2r4z9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the physically grounded multi-view real-robot dataset and the broad evaluation of 17 VLMs across decomposed temporal capabilities.
rs10O2r4z9.main_concern: Reviewers point out that blind text-only inputs nearly match full video on action anticipation and frame shuffling improves matching, undermining task validity.

WYEHwUb0LD.one_liner: Introduces SinusTriplet-95 and refines rare surgical triplet predictions using structural relations, a tail memory bank, and prototype queries.
WYEHwUb0LD.problem: Long-tailed class distributions and narrow, occluded views cause severe visual ambiguity when recognizing instrument-verb-target triplets in sinus endoscopy.
WYEHwUb0LD.method: The authors curate SinusTriplet-95 (324 videos, 95 triplets from 15 patients) and propose RIVET, which combines bidirectional component-triplet calibration, a Tail-Class Memory Bank storing rare-triplet history, and a Tail-Class Prototype Query searching current frames via frame-adaptive gating.
WYEHwUb0LD.key_idea: Fuses component-triplet structural calibration, a rare-triplet memory bank, and frame-level prototype queries via adaptive gating at inference.
WYEHwUb0LD.evidence: Experiments and module ablations on the dual-center SinusTriplet-95 dataset.
WYEHwUb0LD.claimed_gains: RIVET ensemble achieves 50.80% AP_IVT on SinusTriplet-95, surpassing the strongest ensemble baseline by 5.71 percentage points.
WYEHwUb0LD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the importance of extending surgical triplet recognition to sinus endoscopy and the reasonable multi-evidence design.
WYEHwUb0LD.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about the small 15-patient cohort without variance across splits, unclear tail-split definitions, limited module novelty, and unconfirmed public dataset release.

RDDgS1gnpm.one_liner: Controlled study isolating how upstream LLM agent messages override correct downstream answers via fixed-evidence message interventions.
RDDgS1gnpm.problem: Prior multi-agent LLM studies do not separate the accuracy benefits of upstream communication from the harm caused when incorrect upstream messages override a downstream agent's correct evidence-backed answer.
RDDgS1gnpm.method: The authors run paired item-level experiments holding downstream tasks and evidence fixed across three conditions—no message, original upstream message, and opposite-conclusion message—along with controls for source labels, review calls, and minimal edits, and test selective message filtering.
RDDgS1gnpm.key_idea: Holds downstream evidence fixed while intervening on upstream messages (none, original, or reversed) to isolate harmful correct-to-incorrect overrides and answer substitution.
RDDgS1gnpm.evidence: Controlled experiments across five benchmarks and five receiver LLMs with matched controls and audits of harmful transitions.
RDDgS1gnpm.claimed_gains: Incorrect upstream messages override correct downstream answers in up to 32% of cases, and in 94% of audited harmful cases the downstream agent copies the upstream's specific wrong answer.
RDDgS1gnpm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the paired item-level experimental design, thorough controls for alternative explanations, and cross-model replication across five benchmarks.
RDDgS1gnpm.main_concern: Reviewers worry that draft-revision prompts confound free disposal, that the two-node oracle-evidence setup may not generalize to realistic multi-agent workflows, and that novelty over prior LLM conformity studies is limited.

CbCah9CKMR.one_liner: Interventional analysis separating expert utilization from token-expert assignment in genomic mixture-of-experts models via per-layer balancing and router permutations.
CbCah9CKMR.problem: It is unclear whether standard load-balancing objectives inherited from language modeling actually regulate performance-critical behavior in genomic mixture-of-experts models.
CbCah9CKMR.method: The authors compare cross-layer pooled versus per-layer and genome-composition-targeted load-balancing objectives during fine-tuning against inference-time router expert permutations, pair swaps, gate recomputations, and single-expert ablations that alter token-expert assignment while preserving utilization histograms.
CbCah9CKMR.key_idea: Contrasts training-time utilization shifts against utilization-preserving inference-time router permutations to show genomic MoE loss depends on token-expert assignment rather than utilization balance.
CbCah9CKMR.evidence: Fine-tuning and interventional experiments on a JanusDNA checkpoint (14 non-divergent checkpoints, 128 evaluation windows, generation coverage, and three linear probes) plus permutation tests on two additional genomic MoEs spanning a 34× scale range.
CbCah9CKMR.claimed_gains: Retargeting load balancing shifts within-layer max/min utilization up to 5.06–5.98× while validation loss spans only 0.06%, whereas permuting expert identity raises validation loss by 7.48% (gate recomputation retains 89% of that cost) and prior-targeted per-layer arms reduce layer-7 permutation sensitivity by about 39%.
CbCah9CKMR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the conceptual separation between expert utilization and token-expert assignment clear and the decomposition of permutation interventions well targeted.
CbCah9CKMR.main_concern: Reviewers note that breaking learned router-expert alignment via permutation is expected, that training-arm comparisons lack uniform-target controls and multi-seed replication, and that practical downstream value is not established.

nwLmSrhvkP.one_liner: Estimates counterfactual response surfaces for algorithmic pricing agents using matched intervention and control rollouts under common shocks.
nwLmSrhvkP.problem: Observed market price trajectories cannot distinguish independent pricing sellers from sellers that strategically react to a rival's price changes.
nwLmSrhvkP.method: For each unilateral rival-action intervention across a finite grid of sizes and horizons, the method compares an intervention rollout with a matched control rollout sharing the same initial market and learner states and future shocks, forming a counterfactual response surface for policy identification, extrapolation, and remedy targeting.
nwLmSrhvkP.key_idea: Replays matched intervention and control rollouts from identical market and learner states under common future shocks to construct a counterfactual response surface across intervention settings.
nwLmSrhvkP.evidence: Identifiability analysis plus experiments with scripted and learned pricing policies evaluating policy identification, held-out response prediction, and targeted remedy welfare.
nwLmSrhvkP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that extending common random numbers to matched learner-state rollouts provides a clean causal contrast.
nwLmSrhvkP.main_concern: Reviewers criticize underspecified experimental components (classifiers, prediction models, and scripted rules), elementary theory, and restrictive simulator-snapshotting assumptions that limit real-world applicability.

3F3ZddGRJK.one_liner: Decouples slow asynchronous latent lookahead imagination from fast control-rate action decoding on a shared video DiT world-action model.
3F3ZddGRJK.problem: World-action models face a speed-success trade-off where synchronous video generation is too slow for real-time control while removing test-time visual imagination lowers task success.
3F3ZddGRJK.method: GlanceWAM runs an asynchronous proposer on a slow clock to imagine a single future lookahead frame in latent space while an action head on the same video DiT backbone decodes action chunks at control rate using a non-interfering attention mask and staleness-robust horizon training.
3F3ZddGRJK.key_idea: Runs slow asynchronous latent lookahead imagination off the critical path on a shared video DiT with an isolation attention mask and staleness-robust offset conditioning.
3F3ZddGRJK.evidence: Evaluated on the 24-task RoboCasa kitchen benchmark, LIBERO, and single-arm and bimanual real-robot manipulation tasks.
3F3ZddGRJK.claimed_gains: Attains 71.6% on RoboCasa (vs. 67.1% for synchronous Cosmos Policy) and 98.7% on LIBERO while cutting per-chunk control latency 24× relative to synchronous WAMs to 48 ms on one A100.
3F3ZddGRJK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and appreciate the clean architectural decoupling of asynchronous latent lookahead generation from control-rate action decoding.
3F3ZddGRJK.main_concern: Reviewers point out that main simulation benchmarks pause the simulator during lookahead generation rather than evaluating success and latency jointly under the sparse asynchronous schedule, and note limited novelty of individual components.

nbOr6CmP5L.one_liner: Demonstrates theoretically and empirically that per-element CRPS and QICE miss temporal dependence in generative time-series forecasters.
nbOr6CmP5L.problem: Standard multivariate time-series forecasting metrics (CRPS and QICE) are computed independently per time step and channel, making them blind to temporal dependence across the forecast horizon.
nbOr6CmP5L.method: The authors prove that per-element marginal metrics and point-wise likelihoods cannot identify or train temporal dependence, benchmark a diagonal Gaussian floor lacking temporal dependence against generative forecasters, and run a structure-by-objective study comparing point-wise likelihood with joint proper scoring rules (energy and variogram scores).
nbOr6CmP5L.key_idea: Replaces a generative forecaster's sampler with a zero-dependence diagonal Gaussian head and proves point-wise likelihoods preserve initial dependence unless trained with joint proper scoring rules.
nbOr6CmP5L.evidence: Theoretical proofs plus empirical comparisons across 14 dataset-horizon cells (20 cells for residual autocorrelation) on diffusion-lineage forecasters and a structure-by-objective study on three datasets.
nbOr6CmP5L.claimed_gains: The diagonal Gaussian floor wins CRPS in 10 of 14 dataset-horizon cells, reverses ordering in all 20 cells under residual autocorrelation, and outside the two highest-dimensional benchmarks the generative model recovers only 10–29% of temporal dependence in its forecast errors.
nbOr6CmP5L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper exposes a real blind spot in standard marginal forecasting metrics (CRPS and QICE) with clear theoretical and empirical support.
nbOr6CmP5L.main_concern: Reviewers note the empirical scope is narrow (centered mostly on one model lineage) and that lag-1 autocorrelation and variogram score provide an incomplete evaluation of joint predictive distributions.

UIZ1d4gzGC.one_liner: Detects jailbreaks and scales conditional refusal steering using signed attention-routing deviations at assistant-header tokens.
UIZ1d4gzGC.problem: Conditional activation-steering gates that read residual-stream projections can be bypassed when jailbreak rewrites shift projections toward the benign regime.
UIZ1d4gzGC.method: RISA aggregates signed attention-routing deviations of selected heads at the assistant-header tokens into a Routing Deviation Index (RDI), using a benign-calibrated threshold for detection (RISA-D) and scaling a bounded refusal update in a second prefill pass when triggered (RISA-S).
UIZ1d4gzGC.key_idea: Aggregating signed attention-routing deviations across a small set of heads at assistant-header tokens decouples jailbreak detection gating from refusal steering direction.
UIZ1d4gzGC.evidence: Evaluated across three open-weight aligned chat models (including Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3.1) against diverse jailbreak families with leave-one-attack-out calibration and runtime overhead tests.
UIZ1d4gzGC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling detection gating from steering via assistant-header attention routing is a clean, low-overhead inference-time safety design.
UIZ1d4gzGC.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization and evaluation hygiene, noting calibration on the same attack families tested in main tables, potential sensitivity to ordinary prompt-structure changes or unseen distributions, older models, and a missing comparison to assistant-header baseline ADA.

ehy5wJlLJZ.one_liner: Normalizes short-horizon trajectories to domain characteristic scales in a domain-agnostic backbone for zero-shot cross-mobility forecasting.
ehy5wJlLJZ.problem: Trajectory predictors overfit to single-domain scales and contexts, failing to beat constant-velocity extrapolation when transferred zero-shot to unseen mobility domains.
ehy5wJlLJZ.method: Exploiting a shared scale-normalized short-horizon kinematic distribution across pedestrians, vehicles, vessels, and aircraft, KineTraj pairs a scale-invariant kinematic encoder with a domain-agnostic backbone (no domain labels or absolute scales) and a KineMix decoder.
ehy5wJlLJZ.key_idea: Expressing short-horizon motion windows at each domain's characteristic scale lets a domain-agnostic encoder-backbone-KineMix architecture transfer zero-shot across distinct mobility domains.
ehy5wJlLJZ.evidence: Evaluated zero-shot across six mobility datasets spanning pedestrians, vehicles, ships, and aircraft using a 0.59M-parameter model.
ehy5wJlLJZ.claimed_gains: KineTraj uses 0.59M parameters (and reviewers note lowest best-of-20 ADE on 5 of 6 datasets, with a 26% improvement over EqMotion on aircraft; exact numeric gains not stated in abstract).
ehy5wJlLJZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find zero-shot trajectory transfer across distinct mobility domains a meaningful problem and commend the lightweight 0.59M-parameter model's empirical results.
ehy5wJlLJZ.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the theoretical bound covers only conditional means rather than multimodal distributions, ablations do not isolate scale normalization from KineMix, and baselines may not receive matching scale normalization.

gDTqivjGnm.one_liner: Uses influence-function control variates from partially observed sites with permutation screening to reduce Shapley attribution variance.
gDTqivjGnm.problem: Multi-source datasets exhibit blockwise missingness and distribution shift across sites, preventing standard Shapley feature-attribution estimators from using incomplete auxiliary sites without brittle imputation.
gDTqivjGnm.method: DASH derives the influence function of the constrained weighted-least-squares Shapley estimator to form site-specific control variates from partially observed auxiliary sites, screens out misaligned sites via permutation testing, and calibrates site weights adaptively.
gDTqivjGnm.key_idea: Constructing site-specific control variates from the Shapley estimator's influence function fuses partially observed auxiliary sites without feature imputation, guarded by permutation screening.
gDTqivjGnm.evidence: Simulations plus real-world environmental monitoring and multi-center clinical datasets comparing against single-site and imputation baselines.
gDTqivjGnm.claimed_gains: In simulations, DASH achieves 3-8x lower MSE than the single-site estimator and 2-3x lower error than imputation baselines with 82% screening power; on environmental and clinical data, it reduces error by 3-7x over single-site.
gDTqivjGnm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using influence-function control variates to fuse blockwise-missing auxiliary data for Shapley attribution without imputation is practical and well-motivated.
gDTqivjGnm.main_concern: Reviewers identify a theoretical gap under covariate shift, where the implemented calibration uses unweighted covariances rather than density-weighted ones and relies on unjustified fast density-ratio convergence assumptions.

sf5RW1rKeq.one_liner: Separates transformer read depth from KV broadcast depth and proves communication-complexity lower bounds for cross-layer KV sharing.
sf5RW1rKeq.problem: Cross-layer KV cache sharing is widely deployed in LLMs, yet its exact expressivity costs relative to fresh-query depth are poorly characterized.
sf5RW1rKeq.method: The authors define read depth (layers querying context afresh) and broadcast depth (distinct KV generations computed below readers) and prove communication-complexity and pointer-chasing bandwidth separations, producing a depth ledger for architectures like YOCO, YOIO, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
sf5RW1rKeq.key_idea: Separating read depth from broadcast depth via communication-complexity lower bounds shows that KV sharing preserves sequential lookup depth while restricting multi-level aggregation.
sf5RW1rKeq.evidence: Formal communication-complexity proofs, counterexamples, and architectural depth ledgers for YOCO, YOIO, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
sf5RW1rKeq.claimed_gains: Following rho+1 pointers across m-entry tables requires read bandwidth Omega(m) - O(rho log m) at read depth rho versus O(rho log n) at rho+1, and N/2 - log2(1/(2 epsilon)) without sliding windows.
sf5RW1rKeq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the conceptual distinction between read depth and broadcast depth and consider the communication-complexity proofs careful and well-structured.
sf5RW1rKeq.main_concern: Reviewers question practical relevance because the bounds rely on idealized exact-accumulation arithmetic and yield unrealistically long hard prompts (e.g., 7M tokens) with no real-hardware evaluation.

wYl8MAFDZM.one_liner: Combines LLM reference prioritization, paired short-horizon rollout verification, valence constraints, and multi-objective selection for drug design.
wYl8MAFDZM.problem: Retrieval-augmented molecular generation relies on reference similarity that does not ensure chemically valid growth, desirable properties, or diverse candidates under fixed budgets.
wYl8MAFDZM.method: ForesightMol uses an LLM scientific agent to prioritize retrieved references and guide local molecular growth, validates alternative references with paired short-horizon rollouts under shared valence/connectivity constraints, and applies multi-objective set selection balancing quality, binding, and diversity.
wYl8MAFDZM.key_idea: Pairing LLM-proposed molecular reference guidance with short-horizon rollout verification, hard valence filtering, and multi-objective set selection aligns retrieval-augmented growth with downstream outcomes.
wYl8MAFDZM.evidence: Evaluated on 100 CrossDocked2020 protein pockets with controlled analyses separating generation and selection contributions.
wYl8MAFDZM.claimed_gains: On 100 CrossDocked2020 pockets, ForesightMol improves mean QED by 29.4% and scaffold diversity by 14.8% over the best baseline.
wYl8MAFDZM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that outcome-oriented reference validation via short-horizon rollouts paired with budget-aware multi-objective selection addresses a real limitation of retrieval-augmented drug design.
wYl8MAFDZM.main_concern: Reviewers question the fairness and isolated value of the LLM agent, noting extra inference-time rollout search and potential metric alignment/leakage when prompting for drug-likeness without non-LLM rollout controls.

CQhfkgeoPM.one_liner: Trains a lightweight PPO tool-selection policy over structured schema-and-execution task states while a frozen LLM generates arguments.
CQhfkgeoPM.problem: Long-horizon tool-using database agents struggle to organize incomplete schema details, execution traces, and errors over many interaction steps.
CQhfkgeoPM.method: TSADB encodes schema topology, query intent, execution traces, and error semantics into a structured task-state abstraction that drives a lightweight PPO tool-selection policy, delegating tool argument generation to a frozen language model.
CQhfkgeoPM.key_idea: Compressing schema topology, intent, execution traces, and error semantics into a structured state lets a lightweight PPO policy select tools while a frozen LLM fills arguments.
CQhfkgeoPM.evidence: Evaluated with frozen GPT-5 on BIRD-SQL, Spider 2.0-Lite (including schema perturbations), and DS-Bench, plus flat-encoder, RL-ReAct, and reward ablations and conversational/SPARQL transfer studies.
CQhfkgeoPM.claimed_gains: TSADB reaches 82.0% EX on BIRD-SQL, 44.6% EX on Spider 2.0-Lite, and 55.1% TSR on DS-Bench (8.8, 9.3, and 9.0 points above training-free baselines), beats a flat encoder by 7.2 points overall and 14.4 points on 16+-call BIRD tasks, and beats RL-ReAct by 6.6 points on BIRD.
CQhfkgeoPM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the controlled ablations that separate state representation, reward, and policy effects on long-horizon database tasks.
CQhfkgeoPM.main_concern: Reviewers note that headline comparisons pit PPO-trained TSADB against untrained baselines, it is unclear what PPO optimizes in frozen-GPT-5 RL controls versus end-to-end LLM post-training, and warmup/recovery/mask details are underspecified.

MoWArBc1XI.one_liner: Calibrates neural tone-mapper pre-activations across exposures using exposure-conditioned residual offsets in dynamic HDR Gaussian Splatting.
MoWArBc1XI.problem: Varying exposures in dynamic HDR Gaussian Splatting shift neural tone-mapper pre-activations, pushing neurons into inactive or single-linear regimes and degrading reconstruction.
MoWArBc1XI.method: Adaptive Multi-Exposure Regularization (AME-REG) adds exposure-conditioned residual offsets and a quantile-based regularization objective to calibrate the tone mapper's pre-activation distribution across exposure conditions.
MoWArBc1XI.key_idea: Exposure-conditioned residual offsets and quantile regularization center neural tone-mapper pre-activations across exposure levels so nonlinear units remain active during dynamic HDR optimization.
MoWArBc1XI.evidence: Evaluated across multiple dynamic HDR Gaussian Splatting pipelines on both real-world and synthetic dynamic HDR datasets.
MoWArBc1XI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis of exposure-driven pre-activation shifts in HDR tone mappers clear and well-presented, with experiments spanning real and synthetic datasets.
MoWArBc1XI.main_concern: Reviewers view the regularization as incremental and ReLU-specific (treating zero as the sole nonlinearity transition), with limited analysis of generalization to other tone mappers and activation functions like GELU or SiLU.

R8vnFuDNce.one_liner: Accelerates LLM agent serving via multi-step draft tool speculation, prefill-based target verification with KV reuse, and slack-aware shared-GPU scheduling.
R8vnFuDNce.problem: Interleaved LLM reasoning and sequential tool execution keep multi-turn agent chains on the critical path, which single-call optimizations and single-step action speculation do not resolve.
R8vnFuDNce.method: SpecRoute runs a lightweight draft agent to speculate multiple future tool calls while the target model processes its current context. At target tool-call boundaries, the target performs incremental prefill-based verification with KV reuse, coordinated by a slack-aware scheduler managing target-draft switching on a shared GPU.
R8vnFuDNce.key_idea: Interleave multi-step draft tool speculation with target inference, verify speculative observations via incremental prefill with KV reuse, and schedule both engines with slack awareness.
R8vnFuDNce.evidence: Evaluated across seven agent benchmarks in single-request and online-serving settings against vLLM, Continuum, and SpecActions.
R8vnFuDNce.claimed_gains: Achieves 1.28–1.56x single-request speedups over vLLM with comparable task performance, and cuts online mean completion time by 28–36% at low load and 9–20% at the highest tested loads.
R8vnFuDNce.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the latency problem is practical, the paper is clearly written, and end-to-end speedups over vLLM are solid.
R8vnFuDNce.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited novelty and missing comparisons against recent speculative-agent systems (SPAgent, DualSpec, SpecHop, DSP), missing multi-step depth ablations, and unaddressed state-mutating tool calls.

dAKZobvGWw.one_liner: Learns rank-controlled bilinear edge weights over multimodal subgraphs and aligns text and vision at node, subgraph, and batch levels.
dAKZobvGWw.problem: In multimodal graphs, neighbor utility depends on the target node's content and modality, causing static graph aggregation to ingest irrelevant or noisy context.
dAKZobvGWw.method: DMGraph scores induced multimodal subgraph edges with content-conditioned, rank-controlled bilinear relevance functions to achieve learned sparsity. It jointly aligns textual and visual features at node, subgraph, and batch-context levels using hardness-aware contrastive learning.
dAKZobvGWw.key_idea: Combine content-conditioned rank-controlled bilinear edge reweighting with three-level hardness-aware cross-modal contrastive alignment on induced subgraphs.
dAKZobvGWw.evidence: Evaluated on WikiWeb2M, FB15K237, Ele-Fashion, and Goodreads-LP using OPT-125M and LLaMA-1B backbones, plus expanded-neighborhood, 50% edge-corruption, and ablation studies.
dAKZobvGWw.claimed_gains: Under 50% edge corruption, limits relative performance degradation to about 15% on both evaluated datasets while outperforming graph-multimodal baselines.
dAKZobvGWw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find content-conditioned neighbor weighting and multi-level alignment well motivated and appreciate the expanded-neighborhood and edge-corruption analyses.
dAKZobvGWw.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over existing attention-based graph methods, note that default 11-node subgraphs with K_s=15 perform no actual pruning, and criticize reliance on outdated OPT-125M and LLaMA-1B backbones without controlled strong VLM baselines.

k7PszMmZBA.one_liner: Benchmarks career-stage capability calibration in role-playing LLMs and enforces persona boundaries via a training-free metacognitive auditing agent.
k7PszMmZBA.problem: Role-playing LLMs leak expert knowledge beyond a persona's career history, causing junior or unrelated personas to respond like senior experts.
k7PszMmZBA.method: The authors introduce CapRoleBench, holding 355 workplace tasks fixed across Senior, Mid, Junior, and Unrelated career profiles. They also propose CapRoleAgent (CRA), a training-free metacognitive framework that matches career-supported capabilities to task demands, enforces behavioral contracts, and audits overreach and omission.
k7PszMmZBA.key_idea: Enforce persona-specific behavioral contracts and metacognitive overreach/omission audits to align LLM responses with the capability level justified by a career profile.
k7PszMmZBA.evidence: Evaluated across 14 open and proprietary LLMs on CapRoleBench and a matched 100-task diagnostic subset, using multiple LLM judges, human evaluation, and ablations.
k7PszMmZBA.claimed_gains: On a matched 100-task subset, CRA raises macro-average Ordering Consistency from 66.0% to 81.6% and lowers macro-average Overreach Rate from 33.2% to 10.9%, improving both across all 14 models.
k7PszMmZBA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled benchmark framing that varies career evidence over fixed tasks and the consistent metric improvements across 14 models.
k7PszMmZBA.main_concern: Reviewers criticize evaluating CRA only on a difficulty-selected 100-task subset with potential selection bias, question whether relative ranking metrics truly measure boundary adherence, and note 7x token cost without simpler prompting baselines.

gocqaRjDgq.one_liner: Audits spatial histology representation benchmarks with matched controls separating baseline effects, target smoothing, and visible tissue leakage.
gocqaRjDgq.problem: High spatial prediction scores in computational pathology can reflect smoothed targets, encoder-favoring targets, or visible target tissue rather than true prediction beyond the local crop.
