gocqaRjDgq.method: The authors design a matched diagnostic protocol comparing raw versus smoothed expression targets, training-mean baselines, shared measured targets, flexible versus linear readouts, and withheld target-region controls across pathology and vision encoders.
gocqaRjDgq.key_idea: Isolate baseline hiding, target smoothing, and direct tissue-access leakage in histology spatial prediction via matched counterfactual evaluation controls.
gocqaRjDgq.evidence: Evaluated across 13 TCGA cancer cohorts, colorectal (Xenium) and renal (Visium) spatial-omics datasets, retrained TRIPLEX/MERGE models, six frozen encoders, and two slide encoders.
gocqaRjDgq.claimed_gains: Retrained TRIPLEX and MERGE show 74–92% smaller context gains on raw expression than on smoothed neighboring targets, and the UNI2-H versus ResNet50 gap shrinks by 77–78% on shared measured targets.
gocqaRjDgq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation problem is well motivated and that showing 74–92% of apparent context gains stem from target smoothing and visible tissue access is a strong empirical finding.
gocqaRjDgq.main_concern: Reviewers flag sensitivity of tissue-access conclusions to readout choice (MLP vs. ridge), unclear organization of dense experimental setups, and questionable alignment between unseen-tissue prediction and prior methods' goals.

J3ZwoknQjw.one_liner: Generalizes random data splitting to related samples using approximate proximity graphs, community detection, and production-aligned resolution selection.
J3ZwoknQjw.problem: Random train-test splits leak dependent samples in biochemical datasets, while existing relation-aware splitting methods scale poorly to large datasets.
J3ZwoknQjw.method: ReLaG models sample relatedness via a hierarchical latent-variable process, builds an HNSW approximate proximity graph, and runs community detection to partition datasets at the atomic group level. It also selects splitting resolution using unlabeled production data to align evaluation with deployment.
J3ZwoknQjw.key_idea: Partition datasets by detecting communities on an HNSW approximate proximity graph and calibrating split resolution against unlabeled production data.
J3ZwoknQjw.evidence: Evaluated on molecular and protein datasets plus synthetic group-recovery experiments against relation-aware splitting methods.
J3ZwoknQjw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree preventing cross-split leakage at scale is important and that ReLaG substantially improves computational scalability over pairwise relation-aware splitters.
J3ZwoknQjw.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty in combining HNSW with community detection, unvalidated approximation-induced leakage versus exact graphs, and strong reliance on good embeddings and unavailable production data for threshold selection.

6G4PNsgJ3H.one_liner: Threads a nonlinear token-wise recurrence inside an append-only KV cache with chunk-sweep semi-parallel training to extend serial reasoning depth.
6G4PNsgJ3H.problem: Looped transformers saturate in depth and fail to length-generalize, while fixed-state linear RNNs cannot track many registers or perform NC^1-complete state tracking.
6G4PNsgJ3H.method: Dual-Mod Attention (DM) is a superset of self-attention that conditions each token's append-only KV write on the preceding attention read, creating a nonlinear recurrence across the sequence. Training is semi-parallelized using chunk sweeps that converge to the exact sequential recurrence with one extra write per decoded token.
6G4PNsgJ3H.key_idea: Condition each append-only KV-cache write on the current attention read and train via converging chunk sweeps to gain unbounded serial depth with growing memory.
6G4PNsgJ3H.evidence: Evaluated on the P-complete circuit value problem, NC^1-complete A_5 word problem, and K interleaved A_5 register tracking, plus standard benchmarks.
6G4PNsgJ3H.claimed_gains: A single DM layer solves the circuit value problem to depth 1024 and tracks 1024 interleaved A_5 registers at full depth, where single-pass attention stops by 32 and fixed states by 128.
6G4PNsgJ3H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the compact KV-write recurrence formulation, the chunk-parallel training scheme, and the single-layer state-tracking results on CVP and keyed A_5.
6G4PNsgJ3H.main_concern: Reviewers flag limited gains on general tasks, insufficient differentiation from prior recurrent-memory and non-associative scan architectures, and manuscript inconsistencies in reported seeds and figures.

eTSri5pJ2X.one_liner: Integrates parameter-wise contributions along personality merging paths to prune counteracting updates and build sparse personality vectors.
eTSri5pJ2X.problem: Personality vector merging adds entire fine-tuning parameter displacements, including counteracting updates that weaken target traits and degrade general capabilities.
eTSri5pJ2X.method: Functional Path Attribution (FPA) computes path-integrated parameter attributions along personality-merging trajectories under a contrastive personality objective. It selectively retains only the most functionally constructive coordinates to form sparse personality vectors for training-free merging.
eTSri5pJ2X.key_idea: Use path-integrated gradients along personality merging trajectories to identify and prune counteracting parameter updates before sparse vector merging.
eTSri5pJ2X.evidence: Evaluated on Big Five personality control (TRAIT) and general reasoning benchmarks (GPQA, AIME25, MATH-500) against Full SFT, prompting, random (DARE), and magnitude-based baselines.
eTSri5pJ2X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the empirical finding of functional cancellation in personality vectors and the strong trade-off between trait control and general capability retention.
eTSri5pJ2X.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over existing parameter-space integrated gradients, focus of ablations on Extraversion, and potentially unmatched effective update scaling (20x rescaled baselines vs. unscaled FPA).

xUJFgBzOOu.one_liner: Diagnoses visual ignorance in VLMs using per-layer probes, counterfactual residual interchange, and progressive Gaussian blur sensitivity tests.
xUJFgBzOOu.problem: High VLM accuracy on VQA benchmarks can mask cases where models encode task-relevant visual details internally without using them to determine the output.
xUJFgBzOOu.method: The authors combine linear per-layer probing on matched counterfactual image pairs, causal residual interchange across layers, and progressive Gaussian blur degradation to separate visual information availability from causal output influence.
xUJFgBzOOu.key_idea: Pair intermediate-layer probing and causal residual interchange with progressive Gaussian blur tests to separate encoded visual availability from output-level visual usage.
xUJFgBzOOu.evidence: Evaluated five VLMs across twelve benchmarks under progressive blur, with causal residual-interchange and attention localization experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B.
xUJFgBzOOu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important VLM evaluation gap by clearly distinguishing visual information encoding from its causal use in answering.
xUJFgBzOOu.main_concern: Reviewers point out that causal interventions are run only on Qwen2.5-VL-3B, probing decodability is already known, and unchanged predictions under heavy Gaussian blur do not cleanly prove visual ignorance without text-only controls.

5m2Av0sJSN.one_liner: Constructs diagnostic and large-scale AI-generated document image benchmarks revealing spatial artifact inconsistency and text-density-dependent separability.
5m2Av0sJSN.problem: AI-generated image detection focuses on natural images, leaving security-critical AI-generated and edited document images underexplored.
5m2Av0sJSN.method: The authors build AIGDoc-Pilot, a controlled diagnostic benchmark, to analyze detector drops and uncover spatial artifact inconsistency and higher separability in text-dense regions. They then construct AIGDoc, a larger dataset of real and multi-model AI-generated/edited documents, and evaluate document-based training and text-density-guided region selection.
5m2Av0sJSN.key_idea: Diagnose natural-to-document detector failure via controlled benchmarks and exploit stronger synthetic-artifact separability in text-dense document regions.
5m2Av0sJSN.evidence: Evaluated existing AI-generated image detectors on AIGDoc-Pilot and AIGDoc across multiple generation and editing models.
5m2Av0sJSN.claimed_gains: Existing detectors suffer a mean AUC drop of more than 7% on AI-generated document images in AIGDoc-Pilot.
5m2Av0sJSN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree AI-generated document detection is a timely, practically important security problem and find the benchmark and empirical gap valuable.
5m2Av0sJSN.main_concern: Reviewers note that the text-density proxy may confound text with general high-frequency edges, that key detector families (CLIP-based and frequency-domain methods like FreqNet/SPAI) are missing, and that generalization beyond documents is untested.

qCDgzAUjrR.one_liner: Preserves coarse-feature spatial phase via Haar decomposition with SO(3) rotations and refines SimCC pose logits through entropy-guided recurrent spectral correction.
qCDgzAUjrR.problem: Upsampling-free coordinate classification for human pose estimation loses directional detail during downsampling and produces ambiguous distributions under occlusion or low resolution.
qCDgzAUjrR.method: PhasePose applies critically sampled Haar analysis to stride-16 features, adapting three directional detail bands via grouped SO(3) rotations into a read-only correction memory. A weight-shared corrector summarizes SimCC logits with a DCT-anchored spectrum, expectation, and entropy, then runs three gated recurrent refinement steps with entropy-conditioned band routing and anatomical message passing.
qCDgzAUjrR.key_idea: Cache Haar-decomposed directional detail bands on a coarse lattice and query them via entropy-routed recurrent spectral refinement of SimCC coordinate distributions.
qCDgzAUjrR.evidence: Evaluated on COCO val2017 and low-resolution settings across ResNet-50 and ViT-S backbones, with phase/Haar component ablations.
qCDgzAUjrR.claimed_gains: On COCO val2017, PhasePose achieves 73.8 AP with ResNet-50 and 75.1 AP with ViT-S (+1.2 AP over ViTPose-S).
qCDgzAUjrR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find caching coarse phase details for upsampling-free recurrent coordinate refinement a coherent, efficiency-minded architectural idea with strong reported numbers.
qCDgzAUjrR.main_concern: Reviewers flag potential evaluation-protocol mismatches in baseline tables (detected vs. ground-truth boxes for CIGPose and mismatched low-resolution input sizes for SimCC/SAR) and weak justification for the many frequency-domain components.

sE3pWZVGy3.one_liner: Optimizes downstream decisions against adversarial conditional generators constrained to a frozen nominal generator solely via sample-based Sinkhorn divergence.
sE3pWZVGy3.problem: Transport-based DRO ignores generative model structure while existing generative ambiguity-set methods require likelihoods, gradients, or training-data certificates from the nominal model.
sE3pWZVGy3.method: Generative Distributionally Robust Optimization (GDRO) treats any pretrained conditional generator as a black-box nominal sampler and constrains an adversarial conditional generator using sample-based Sinkhorn divergence. The authors solve an expected mini-batch formulation via a stochastic primal-dual algorithm and derive loss-sensitivity and Lagrangian-gap bounds.
sE3pWZVGy3.key_idea: Constrain a learned adversarial conditional generator to a frozen nominal generator using sample-only Sinkhorn divergence within a stochastic primal-dual DRO loop.
sE3pWZVGy3.evidence: Backed by Sinkhorn-proximity and relaxation-gap bounds and experiments on contextual newsvendor inventory management and robot navigation.
sE3pWZVGy3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the flexible black-box formulation that needs only samples from the nominal generator while keeping adversarial shifts inside a structured generator family.
sE3pWZVGy3.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty beyond combining Sinkhorn constraints with adversarial generators, missing ablations isolating generator constraints from divergence choices, unmatched optimization budgets, and a gap between exact inner-maximization theory and finite gradient steps.

BGKc7sHJvD.one_liner: Benchmarks sequence-based epitope reasoning in LLMs across five antibody-discovery tasks built from structural contacts, B-cell assays, and escape data.
BGKc7sHJvD.problem: It is unclear whether general-purpose LLMs can infer epitope properties directly from raw antigen and antibody sequences across the antibody drug discovery workflow.
BGKc7sHJvD.method: EpiBench provides 1,609 closed-book, automatically scorable sequence-based samples grounded in antibody-antigen structures, functional B-cell assays, and deep mutational scanning escape data. It spans five connected tasks—region discovery, antibody-conditioned identification, binning, functional assessment, and escape assessment—with shortcut controls.
BGKc7sHJvD.key_idea: Evaluate sequence-only LLM epitope reasoning across five unified, shortcut-controlled antibody-discovery tasks grounded in structural and experimental assay data.
BGKc7sHJvD.evidence: Evaluated nine general-purpose LLMs alongside specialized baselines (such as BepiPred-3.0 and EpiPred-derived methods) with length-stratification and reasoning analyses.
BGKc7sHJvD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree EpiBench unifies relevant antibody-discovery tasks into a clean, automatically scorable framework with thoughtful shortcut controls.
BGKc7sHJvD.main_concern: Reviewers question the validity of functional-assessment distractors (binding-only or untested synthetic peptides are not proven functionally negative) and note that near-random sequence-only LLM performance confirms an expected prior.

cruu1zw7bn.one_liner: Closes the loop between code-as-policy agents and a dual-stream latent world model via rendered geometric programs and decoded part-state updates.
cruu1zw7bn.problem: Code-as-policy agents cannot verify whether proposed programs cause desired physical changes, while latent world models do not express predictions in program-readable terms.
cruu1zw7bn.method: CTRL-Z introduces Structured Object Programs (SOPs) encoding object geometry and physical parameters, which render into geometric views. A dual-stream world model ingests RGB images and rendered geometric views to predict future latents, from which dynamic object parameters are decoded back into the SOP so the code agent can revise actions before execution.
cruu1zw7bn.key_idea: Bridge code agents and a dual-stream RGB-plus-geometry latent world model by decoding predicted latents into updated Structured Object Program physical parameters.
cruu1zw7bn.evidence: Evaluated on rigid-body and articulated manipulation tasks, object generalization settings, and real-robot block stacking and drawer opening.
cruu1zw7bn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view the bidirectional program-world-model interface as a clean solution for making latent predictions readable and revisable by code agents.
cruu1zw7bn.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing decisive baselines (direct future part-state prediction and a practical physics simulator initialized from the same SOP), unclear novelty beyond integrating existing modules, and fragile LLM-backbone dependence.

wX92FoQOrp.one_liner: Benchmarks execution-cost differences across functionally viable agent skills and selects lower-cost skills via a multi-stage cost-aware reference retriever.
wX92FoQOrp.problem: Relevance-based skill retrieval ignores that functionally viable skills for the same task can induce drastically different downstream agent execution times and token costs.
wX92FoQOrp.method: The authors formalize Cost-Aware Skill Retrieval, build a benchmark measuring actual agent execution costs across candidate skills, and propose a lightweight multi-stage Cost-Aware Reference Method that incorporates task reasoning and cost-aware route selection.
wX92FoQOrp.key_idea: Augment functional skill retrieval with multi-stage cost-aware route selection to favor skills that minimize downstream agent execution time and token usage.
wX92FoQOrp.evidence: Evaluated with actual downstream agent execution across two models and three retrievers (BM25, Qwen, SkillRouter) on a 35-task benchmark, reporting end-to-end overhead.
wX92FoQOrp.claimed_gains: Reduces agent execution time by 36.93% and full token consumption by 54.39% on average versus Top-10 retrieval, with an average Pass Rate drop of 3.17 percentage points.
wX92FoQOrp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate studying execution cost beyond functional relevance and validating cost savings via actual end-to-end agent execution with selection overhead accounted for.
wX92FoQOrp.main_concern: Reviewers flag the small 35-task benchmark scale, noticeable task-accuracy drops (e.g., 3.17 pp average), and lack of ablations isolating cost awareness from general route planning.

z2UNucJ1Vt.one_liner: Trains a lightweight history-gated visual-token retention policy via reinforcement learning with video-caption feedback for streaming video MLLMs.
z2UNucJ1Vt.problem: Streaming video understanding needs bounded visual memory, but training-free compression relies on heuristics and KV-cache pruning does not readily apply to hybrid linear-attention backbones.
z2UNucJ1Vt.method: Memory Update Reinforcement Learning (MURL) freezes the MLLM backbone and trains a lightweight token selector via RL to perform recursive visual-memory updates. A history gate fuses current contextual token scores with stored importance estimates, supervised by video-level caption feedback from a frozen backbone.
z2UNucJ1Vt.key_idea: Train a history-gated visual-token retention selector via RL over recursive compression steps using video-level caption rewards from a frozen backbone.
z2UNucJ1Vt.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B on StreamingBench, OVO-Bench, and Video-MME under a streaming protocol.
z2UNucJ1Vt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the practical recursive streaming formulation, clear presentation, and lightweight history-gated selector design.
z2UNucJ1Vt.main_concern: Reviewers cite marginal gains over adapted baselines (under 0.8 points on Qwen3.5-9B), missing or modified competing baselines (SCORE, SimpleStream, StreamForest), incomplete efficiency metrics, and limitations of single-caption rewards.

1XJs03cwyl.one_liner: Jointly trains JEPA with short/long-term forward rollouts and endpoint-conditioned inverse action decoders for fast test-time replanning.
1XJs03cwyl.problem: One-step JEPA latent world models struggle to capture long-term dynamics for action recovery and require expensive search during planning.
1XJs03cwyl.method: LS-JEPA jointly optimizes one-step forward prediction, fixed-horizon autoregressive rollout, and an endpoint-conditioned inverse action decoder reconstructing single-step and multi-step action sequences from latent displacements. At inference, Test-Time Replanning (TTR) decodes a goal-directed action sequence and applies a one-step correction from fresh observations.
1XJs03cwyl.key_idea: Combine multi-step forward latent rollouts with endpoint-conditioned multi-step inverse action decoding to replace heavy action search with direct test-time replanning.
1XJs03cwyl.evidence: Evaluated on four LeWorldModel simulation tasks (Push-T, OGBench-Cube, Reacher, Two-Room) with ablations on forward and inverse supervision.
1XJs03cwyl.claimed_gains: Achieves 96.00%, 100.00%, 99.67%, and 100.00% success rates on Push-T, OGBench-Cube, Reacher, and Two-Room, respectively.
1XJs03cwyl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly training forward and inverse dynamics across temporal scales yields fast execution and strong performance on the tested tasks.
1XJs03cwyl.main_concern: Reviewers view the method as incremental over prior goal-conditioned inverse-dynamics planners and note the evaluation is confined to four simple LeWorldModel simulation tasks with limited long-horizon testing.

hLuDjOxoA8.one_liner: Empirically estimates each LLM's effective context threshold and routes queries across threshold-bounded hierarchical document indices.
hLuDjOxoA8.problem: LLMs' reliable usable context often falls well short of nominal window limits, and existing evaluations do not translate degradation into an operational inference budget.
hLuDjOxoA8.method: CALIBER measures answer correctness, faithfulness, and consistency risk across context lengths to estimate a model-specific effective threshold (tau_eff). It then hierarchically indexes documents into tau_eff-bounded subcontexts, routes queries to relevant indices, processes them in parallel, and aggregates partial responses.
hLuDjOxoA8.key_idea: Calibrates a model-specific effective context threshold from quality and consistency degradation, then executes parallel query routing and aggregation over threshold-bounded hierarchical subcontexts.
hLuDjOxoA8.evidence: Evaluated across 14 proprietary and open-weight LLMs for boundary calibration and on three frontier models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.5) for inference quality.
hLuDjOxoA8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that translating effective context limits into actionable inference budgets is practically relevant and appreciate the broad 14-model calibration study.
hLuDjOxoA8.main_concern: Reviewers note that the boundary estimator is not decisively tested against simpler fixed-budget or validation-accuracy rules, introduces multi-stage compute/hyperparameter overhead, and depends heavily on calibration tasks.

OsC2nzBprP.one_liner: Accelerates Speculative Jacobi Decoding in autoregressive image generation by upweighting draft tokens with rising Jacobi probabilities.
OsC2nzBprP.problem: Speculative Jacobi Decoding for autoregressive image generation suffers from low token acceptance rates due to token selection ambiguity.
OsC2nzBprP.method: SJD-VP tracks token probability changes across Jacobi iterations and biases the drafting distribution toward tokens exhibiting an increasing probability trend, acting as a training-free plug-and-play module for existing SJD variants.
OsC2nzBprP.key_idea: Tracks per-token probability trajectories across Jacobi iterations and upweights tokens with consecutive probability growth during speculative drafting.
OsC2nzBprP.evidence: Evaluated training-free across multiple autoregressive image backbones (including Lumina-mGPT and LlamaGen) and SJD variants using NFE, latency, FID, and CLIP scores.
OsC2nzBprP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, training-free observation on Jacobi probability dynamics and the consistent NFE and decoding speedups across backbones.
OsC2nzBprP.main_concern: Reviewers flag unmeasured memory/compute overhead from storing full-vocabulary probability histories, lossy sampling evaluated only with FID/CLIP rather than distributional or compositional metrics, and modest conceptual novelty.
